Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

In the early hours of the seventh of September 1838, a young woman looked out of a lighthouse window on the Farne Islands, off the coast of Northumberland, and saw something that would change her life. Her name was Grace Darling, she was twenty-two years old, and she had spent almost her whole life on the islands, where her father, William, was the lighthouse keeper.

That night a terrible storm was blowing. A steamship called the Forfarshire, carrying around sixty passengers and crew from Hull to Dundee, had problems with its engines and was driven onto a group of rocks called Big Harcar. The ship broke in two, and the back half sank almost immediately. Grace spotted the wreck at about a quarter to five in the morning, and through a telescope she could make out a few people clinging to the rocks.

The sea was far too rough for the lifeboat from the mainland to set out, so Grace and her father decided to row out themselves in a small fishing boat. They took the longer, more sheltered route, almost a mile, to reach the rocks. William jumped onto the rocks to help the survivors, while Grace kept the boat steady in the waves. They rescued nine people in two trips: the first time they took five, including an injured man, back to the lighthouse, and two of the rescued crew then helped William row back for the rest.

When the story appeared in the newspapers, Grace became a celebrity almost overnight. Artists travelled to the islands to paint her portrait, people wrote poems and songs about her, and she received hundreds of letters, some of them asking for a lock of her hair. Even Queen Victoria sent her fifty pounds. Grace found the attention exhausting; she was a shy person and did not understand why so much fuss was made, since her father had done just as much.

Sadly, she did not enjoy her fame for long. In 1842, just four years after the rescue, she died of tuberculosis at the age of twenty-six. Today there is a museum dedicated to her in the village of Bamburgh, and her name is still used for lifeboats around the British coast.

Grace Darling

As you listen to the recording, complete the sentences. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words.

  1. 0.Grace Darling lived on the ___, off the coast of Northumberland.
    Farne Islands
  2. 1.Grace Darling's father worked as a ___ on the Farne Islands.
  3. 2.The Forfarshire was sailing from Hull to ___.
  4. 3.The ship broke in two after it was driven onto rocks because of problems with its ___.
  5. 4.Grace first saw the wreck at about ___ in the morning.
  6. 5.Grace and her father rowed out in a small ___.
  7. 6.While her father helped the survivors, Grace's job was to ___.
  8. 7.Altogether, Grace and William saved ___.
  9. 8.Among the many letters she received, some people asked for ___.
  10. 9.Grace died in 1842 of ___.

1. lighthouse keeper
2. Dundee
3. engines
4. a quarter to five / 4.45
5. fishing boat
6. keep the boat steady
7. nine people
8. a lock of her hair

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami.
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem predvidi, kaj manjka (število, kraj, samostalnik). Med poslušanjem zapiši ključno besedo, pri drugem poslušanju preveri.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del posnetka. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. lighthouse keeper
»her father, William, was the lighthouse keeper«. »worked as a« + poklic: lighthouse keeper.
2. Dundee
»from Hull to Dundee«. »from Hull to« + kraj: Dundee.
3. engines
»had problems with its engines«. »problems with its« + samostalnik: engines.
4. a quarter to five / 4.45
»at about a quarter to five in the morning«. »at about« + čas: a quarter to five.
5. fishing boat
»in a small fishing boat«. »a small« + samostalnik: fishing boat.
6. keep the boat steady
»Grace kept the boat steady in the waves«. »job was to« + nedoločnik: keep the boat steady.
7. nine people
»They rescued nine people in two trips«. »saved« + število oseb: nine people.
8. a lock of her hair
»asking for a lock of her hair«. »asked for« + samostalnik: a lock of her hair (koder las).
9. tuberculosis
»she died of tuberculosis«. »died of« + bolezen: tuberculosis.

naloge.besedilo:
You will hear an interview with Dr Leila Hassan, an emergency doctor who advises colleagues in remote areas. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Hassan, you work in a London hospital, but you also help patients thousands of kilometres away. How does that work?

Dr Hassan: Through a very simple system. Doctors in remote clinics – in mountain villages, on small islands, sometimes in places affected by war – send me photographs, X-rays and short videos on their mobile phones. I look at them and we discuss the case over a video call. It's not science fiction; most of it works on an ordinary smartphone with a decent internet connection.

Interviewer: How did it all begin?

Dr Hassan: When I was a medical student, I spent a summer volunteering at a clinic in the mountains of Nepal. There was one doctor for about twenty thousand people. I remember a young boy with a broken leg who had to be carried for two days to reach us. I promised myself then that I would find a way to help places like that, even if I couldn't be there in person.

Interviewer: What kind of cases do you deal with?

Dr Hassan: Mostly emergencies – injuries, burns, difficult births. Often the local doctor knows exactly what to do but needs a second opinion before taking a big decision, like whether to send a patient on a long journey to a hospital. Sometimes I simply confirm what they already think. That confidence can save a life.

Interviewer: Are there limits to what you can do?

Dr Hassan: Of course. I can't touch the patient, and a photograph doesn't show everything. The biggest problem, though, is electricity. In many clinics, the power goes off for hours every day, so we've started giving them solar chargers. A phone with an empty battery is no use to anyone.

Interviewer: You also train volunteers.

Dr Hassan: Yes, we now have about four hundred doctors in twenty countries who give their time for free. Before they start, they do an online course about working with different cultures – how to explain things politely, how to ask questions without making a colleague feel stupid. That part is just as important as the medicine.

Interviewer: What's your next goal?

Dr Hassan: We want to translate our training materials into more languages. At the moment they exist only in English and French, which excludes many of the people who need them most.

A doctor who works from a distance

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where does Dr Hassan work?
    In a London hospital.
  2. 1.What do doctors in remote clinics send Dr Hassan?
  3. 2.What equipment does most of the system need?
  4. 3.Where did Dr Hassan volunteer as a student?
  5. 4.How long did the boy with the broken leg travel to the clinic?
  6. 5.Why do local doctors often contact her?
  7. 6.What is the biggest practical problem in many clinics?
  8. 7.What have they started giving clinics?
  9. 8.What is the online course for volunteers about?
  10. 9.Why do they want to translate the materials?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Photographs, X-rays and videos.
2. An (ordinary) smartphone (and internet).
3. In (the mountains of) Nepal.
4. Two days.
5. For a second opinion.
6. Electricity. / Power cuts.
7. Solar chargers.
8. Working with different cultures.
9. They exist only in English and French. / To reach more people.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Photographs, X-rays and videos.
»send me photographs, X-rays and short videos«. Zdravniki pošiljajo tri vrste gradiv; ker vprašanje sprašuje »what«, navedeš vse tri.
2. An (ordinary) smartphone (and internet).
»works on an ordinary smartphone with a decent internet connection«. »Equipment« = oprema; dovolj je navaden pametni telefon (z internetom).
3. In (the mountains of) Nepal.
»a clinic in the mountains of Nepal«. »Where« = kraj; klinika v gorah Nepala.
4. Two days.
»had to be carried for two days«. »How long« = koliko časa; dva dneva so ga nosili.
5. For a second opinion.
»needs a second opinion before taking a big decision«. »Why« = razlog; potrebujejo drugo mnenje pred veliko odločitvijo.
6. Electricity. / Power cuts.
»The biggest problem, though, is electricity.« »The biggest problem, though« – »though« opozori na novo, pomembno informacijo: elektrika.
7. Solar chargers.
»we've started giving them solar chargers«. »Started giving« = začeli dajati; solarne polnilnike, ki rešijo težavo z elektriko.
8. Working with different cultures.
»an online course about working with different cultures«. »About« = tema tečaja: delo z različnimi kulturami.
9. They exist only in English and French. / To reach more people.
Gradiva so samo v angleščini in francoščini, zato izključujejo mnoge. »Why … translate« zahteva razlog: zdaj so samo v angleščini in francoščini; dovolj je tudi namen (da dosežejo več ljudi).

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

You are a secondary school student interested in a career in medicine. To gain practical experience, you would like to apply for a two-week volunteer placement at a children's hospital in Edinburgh.

Write an e-mail of application of 150–180 words to the hospital's volunteer coordinator, in which you:

  • explain why you would like to volunteer with children in a hospital,
  • describe your relevant experience and your level of English,
  • explain what you hope to learn from the placement.
TO: volunteers@childrens-hospital.org.uk
SUBJECT: Volunteer placement
Dear Sir or Madam,
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-sporočilo (prošnja) z vsemi tremi iztočnicami, konkretnimi dokazi o izkušnjah in znanju jezika ter formalnim zaključkom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (150–180 words), formal style
  2. explain why you would like to volunteer with children in a hospital
  3. describe your relevant experience and your level of English
  4. explain what you hope to learn from the placement
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba prošnje
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor; konec Yours faithfully.
I am writing to apply for a volunteer placement at your hospital, which I learned about from my school's career adviser.
Namen v prvem stavku.
Having spent two summers helping at a children's holiday camp, I have discovered that I am patient and good at calming children down.
Participni stavek (Having spent …) – zgradba, primerna za višjo raven.
I hold a Cambridge C1 certificate and use English daily in my school's bilingual programme.
Konkreten dokaz jezikovnega znanja.
I hope to gain an insight into the work of paediatric nurses, which would help me decide on my future studies.
Tretja iztočnica: kaj želiš pridobiti.
I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss my application. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Vljuden zaključek.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the two-week volunteer placement at your children's hospital, which I found on your website.

I am a seventeen-year-old student from Slovenia, and I hope to study medicine after my final exams. I would particularly like to volunteer with children, as a hospital stay is especially frightening for them, and small things such as reading a story can help.

I have some relevant experience. For the past two years I have volunteered at a day centre for children with disabilities, where I help with activities and homework. I have also completed a first aid course with the Red Cross. As for my English, I passed the Cambridge C1 Advanced exam last year, so I can communicate confidently with both children and staff.

From the placement, I hope to learn how a hospital team works together and how doctors and nurses talk to young patients and their parents. This would help me choose my future specialisation.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Eva Zajc

Število besed: 175 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss the theme of loneliness in Nick Hornby's About a Boy.

Nick Hornby: About a Boy

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo o osamljenosti, ki jo dokaže na obeh glavnih osebah (Willova izbrana osamljenost, Marcusova vsiljena) in pokaže razvoj do »mreže« ljudi ob koncu; 250–300 besed, brez obnove.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the theme of loneliness in Nick Hornby's About a Boy.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – both Will and Marcus are lonely, but in different ways, and the novel shows that loneliness ends only when people allow themselves to depend on others.
Teza že v uvodu; ne pišeš o avtorju na splošno.
Jedro 1 – Will: chosen loneliness; he fills his days with 'units of time' and believes that 'all men are islands'.
Navedi prizor in kratek citat, nato razloži njegov pomen.
Jedro 2 – Marcus: forced loneliness; he is bullied at school and has to look after his depressed mother, Fiona.
Primerjaj vzroke: Will se osamljenosti izbere, Marcus jo trpi.
Jedro 3 – resolution: the 'island' metaphor changes; both build a wider network (Ellie, Rachel, Fiona) rather than a traditional family.
Pokaži razvoj osebe: od začetka do konca romana.
Sklep: loneliness is overcome through responsibility for others.
Zaokroži z vrnitvijo k tezi.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Loneliness in About a Boy

Nick Hornby's About a Boy is a funny novel, but at its centre lies a serious theme: loneliness. Both main characters, Will Freeman and twelve-year-old Marcus, are lonely, though in very different ways, and the novel shows that they can only escape loneliness by letting other people into their lives.

Will's loneliness is chosen. He lives comfortably on the royalties from his father's Christmas song, has no job and avoids any real commitment. He even sees himself as an island, proud that he needs nobody. Yet his empty days, filled with television, shopping and haircuts, show that this freedom is also a kind of emptiness. When he invents a son to meet single mothers, it is clear that he wants company without responsibility.

Marcus, by contrast, is lonely against his will. At his new school in London, he is bullied because of his clothes and his habit of singing aloud. At home, he cannot talk openly with his mother, Fiona, whose depression leads to a suicide attempt. Marcus feels responsible for her and has no one to share this burden with.

The turning point comes when Marcus starts visiting Will's flat after school. Their unlikely friendship slowly changes both of them. Marcus learns from Will how to look and behave more like other teenagers, while Will discovers that caring about someone gives his life meaning. Through Marcus, he also meets Rachel and falls in love.

By the end, neither character is alone. Instead of one perfect family, they have a wider network of friends and relatives. Hornby thus suggests that the cure for loneliness is not independence but connection.

Število besed: 274 (zahtevanih 250–300). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

Old films, new audiences: what to watch with your children

When my children were small, film nights in our house began with an argument. Everybody wanted something different, nobody wanted anything old, and by the time we had chosen, the youngest had fallen asleep on the sofa. Then, one rainy weekend, our internet stopped working and we were left with a box of DVDs that had belonged to my parents. That was how my children discovered the classics – and how I discovered that "old" is not the same as "boring".

The first film we tried was a black-and-white comedy from the 1950s. My son, then eight, complained for the first ten minutes that "the colours were broken". By the end he was laughing so hard that he slid off his chair. What won him over was not the story but the physical comedy: people falling into rivers, getting stuck in doors, being chased by geese. It works, I realised, because it doesn't depend on language or on knowing who the actors are.

Older films also move at a different speed. There are fewer cuts and longer scenes, which at first my daughter found frustrating. Then something interesting happened: she started noticing details – a clock on the wall, a character's expression – and asking questions. Slow films, I have come to believe, train children to pay attention.

Of course, not every classic has aged well. Some contain attitudes towards women or other cultures that are uncomfortable today. We decided not to avoid these films completely, but to pause and talk about what we were seeing. My children now have a habit of shouting "Pause!" whenever something seems unfair, which I count as one of the most useful lessons I have ever taught them.

Our film nights still involve a certain amount of arguing. But we have a new rule: every second week, the film must be at least thirty years older than the youngest person watching. My daughter keeps a list in a notebook and gives each film a mark out of ten. So far, her highest score has gone to a silent film made a hundred years ago, in which a man climbs the outside of a skyscraper and hangs from the hands of a clock.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.What did film nights in the family use to begin with?
    An argument.
  2. 1.What often happened to the youngest child before a film was chosen?
  3. 2.Why did the family start watching their grandparents' films?
  4. 3.What did the son complain about at the beginning of the first film?
  5. 4.What kind of comedy made the son laugh?
  6. 5.Why does this type of comedy work for children?
  7. 6.What did the daughter dislike about older films at first?
  8. 7.According to the author, what do slow films teach children?
  9. 8.How does the family deal with unfair attitudes in old films?
  10. 9.What must the film be like every second week?
  11. 10.What does the daughter record in her notebook?
naloge.rezultat:
1. He/She fell asleep.
2. The internet stopped working.
3. The colours were broken. / It was black and white.
4. Physical comedy.
5. It doesn't depend on language.
6. The slow speed. / Longer scenes and fewer cuts.
7. To pay attention.
8. They pause and talk (about them).
9. Thirty years older than the youngest viewer.
10. A list of films with marks. / Marks out of ten.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. He/She fell asleep.
»the youngest had fallen asleep on the sofa«. »What often happened« = kaj se je pogosto zgodilo; past perfect »had fallen asleep« pove, da je najmlajši zaspal, preden so izbrali.
2. The internet stopped working.
»our internet stopped working and we were left with a box of DVDs«. »Why … start« zahteva vzrok: internet ni deloval, ostala jim je škatla DVD-jev.
3. The colours were broken. / It was black and white.
Sin je črno-beli film opisal kot »broken colours«. Sin je pritožbo izrazil otroško (»broken colours«); pomen je, da je film črno-bel.
4. Physical comedy.
»What won him over was … the physical comedy«. »What kind of comedy« zahteva vrsto: fizična komedija (slapstick).
5. It doesn't depend on language.
»because it doesn't depend on language or on knowing who the actors are«. »Why … work« zahteva razlog: ni odvisna od jezika.
6. The slow speed. / Longer scenes and fewer cuts.
»fewer cuts and longer scenes, which at first my daughter found frustrating«. Hči je bila sprva nestrpna zaradi počasnosti (daljši prizori, manj rezov); dovolj je ena parafraza.
7. To pay attention.
»Slow films … train children to pay attention«. »Train children to pay attention« → odgovor z nedoločnikom: to pay attention.
8. They pause and talk (about them).
»to pause and talk about what we were seeing«. »How … deal with« = kako ravnajo; ustavijo film in se pogovorijo.
9. Thirty years older than the youngest viewer.
Novo pravilo: »at least thirty years older than the youngest person watching«. Pravilo za vsak drugi teden: film mora biti vsaj trideset let starejši od najmlajšega gledalca.
10. A list of films with marks. / Marks out of ten.
»keeps a list in a notebook and gives each film a mark out of ten«. V zvezek zapisuje seznam filmov z ocenami od 1 do 10.

Winter in Tallinn: a fairy tale with a frozen sea

On the edge of the Baltic, where the sea freezes in a hard winter, Tallinn's old town looks like the illustration of a children's book, [0].

I arrived in late January, when the temperature had fallen to minus fifteen and the cobbled streets were covered in a thin layer of ice [1]. Within an hour I had given up trying to look elegant and was walking like a penguin, as the locals sensibly do.

The medieval walls, with their red-roofed towers, are among the best preserved in Europe. In summer the old town is crowded with tourists from cruise ships, [2]. In winter, however, you can wander for an hour and meet only a few cats and a man selling roasted almonds.

The cold explains much about Estonian life. Houses have thick walls and small windows, and almost everyone owns a sauna, [3]. My guide, Kristi, told me that a traditional sauna is not only about heat but about silence: "It is the one place where nobody checks a phone."

To see how people enjoy winter, I joined a group [4]. We drove an hour east to the coast, where the sea had frozen solid for several hundred metres. Children were skating, a man was fishing through a hole, and a family had set up a table [5].

Back in town, I warmed up in a café that has served hot chocolate since 1864. Its walls are decorated with marzipan figures, [6]. According to local legend, marzipan was invented here as a medicine, [7].

In the evening, the old town square filled with people for a winter music festival. Musicians played on a stage built of ice blocks, [8]. It was so cold that the violinist wore gloves with the fingertips cut off.

Leaving Tallinn, I realised that I had spent four days being cold, [9]. Winter here is not something to escape from but something to be lived – slowly, warmly and, preferably, in a sauna [10].

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. Awhich can be used even when the snow is too deep to go outside
  2. Bwhich a local chocolate maker has been producing by hand for over a century
  3. Cand lit by candles that flickered in the frozen air
  4. Dalthough I had been warned to bring proper boots
  5. Ethat organises trips to the frozen sea
  6. Fyet I could not remember a holiday I had enjoyed more
  7. Gespecially when the snow lies thick on its towers
  8. Hwhich makes it difficult to see anything of the town
  9. Iprescribed to a sick city councillor in the fifteenth century
  10. Jwith a flask of tea and sandwiches on the ice
  11. Kwhere children learn to swim before they can walk
  12. Lwho often stay for only a few hours
  13. Mfollowed by a quick roll in the snow

1. D
2. L
3. A
4. E
5. J
6. B
7. I
8. C
9. F
10. M
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. D
Poledenele ulice – kljub opozorilu glede škornjev (although) hodi kot pingvin. although = čeprav; kljub opozorilu ni imela primernih škornjev, zato je hodila kot pingvin.
2. L
who se nanaša na turiste s križark, ki ostanejo le nekaj ur. who se nanaša na tourists (osebe); kratek obisk razloži, zakaj ne spoznajo mesta.
3. A
which se nanaša na savno, ki jo lahko uporabljajo tudi ob globokem snegu. which se nanaša na savno (stvar); uporabna je tudi, ko je zunaj preveč snega.
4. E
a group that organises trips – oziralni stavek; naslednji stavek opiše izlet na morje. Za »a group« sledi oziralni stavek s that; naslednja poved opiše izlet na zamrznjeno morje.
5. J
A family had set up a table with a flask of tea – opis piknika na ledu. »with« doda opis: družina je imela na ledu čaj in sendviče – piknik.
6. B
Marcipanove figure, ki jih izdeluje lokalni čokoladnik. which se nanaša na marcipanove figure; present perfect continuous (has been producing) pove trajanje do zdaj.
7. I
Legenda: marcipan kot zdravilo, predpisano mestnemu svetniku. Deležnik prescribed (predpisan) opiše marcipan kot zdravilo iz legende.
8. C
Oder iz ledenih blokov, osvetljen s svečami. »and lit by« nadaljuje opis odra: osvetljen s svečami.
9. F
yet – nasprotje: štiri dni mraza, a najlepše počitnice. yet = pa vendar; nasprotje med mrazom in užitkom.
10. M
Savni sledi valjanje v snegu – estonska zimska navada. »followed by« = čemur sledi; po savni se povaljajo v snegu.

1. which
2. when / if / whenever
3. but / although / though
4. in

6. more

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. which
Nedoločni oziralni stavek po vejici: which lies. Za vejico in stvar (island) samo which.
2. when / if / whenever
Časovni ali pogojni odvisnik: when the weather is good enough. Časovni/pogojni veznik: ko/če je vreme dovolj lepo.
3. but / although / though
Nasprotje: but it often cannot sail. Nasprotje: ladja obstaja, a pogosto ne more pluti.
4. in
in an emergency – stalna zveza. Stalna zveza in an emergency = v nujnem primeru.
5. for
be famous for. be famous for = slaven po.
6. more
more than three years. more than + število = več kot.
7. that
fear that + stavek. fear that + stavek.
8. to
offer something to somebody. offer something to somebody.
9. why
explain why – vzrok. explain why = pojasniti, zakaj.
10. over
from all over the world. from all over the world = z vsega sveta.
11. that
forget that + stavek. forget that + stavek.
12. who / that
Oziralni zaimek za osebe: the families who were chosen. Oziralni zaimek za osebe brez vejice: who/that.
13. who
Nedoločni oziralni stavek za birdwatchers (osebe). Za vejico in osebe samo who.
14. each
each other – vzajemni zaimek. each other = drug drugega (vzajemno).
15. could / can
than you could ever imagine. Modalni glagol v primerjavi: than you could ever imagine.

The surprising benefits of personality tests at work

Which colour are you? No, I am not talking about a silly online quiz. I am talking about the (0) (OFFICE) test my colleagues and I took last month, which divided us into four colours according to our working style.

I approached the test with a great deal of (1) (SCEPTICAL). Personality tests have a reputation for being (2) (SCIENCE) at best and a waste of time at worst. Psychologists point out that people's behaviour changes depending on the situation, which makes it (3) (POSSIBLE) to put anyone into a single box.

And yet, to my surprise, the results were (4) (USE). I was labelled "green", meaning I prefer harmony and avoid conflict. My manager turned out to be "red": direct, quick and (5) (DECIDE). Suddenly, years of small misunderstandings made sense. When she sent me a two-word e-mail, it was not (6) (RUDENESS), just her natural style.

The real value of the test, I realised, was not its (7) (ACCURATE) but the conversation it started. For the first time, our team talked openly about how we like to work, how we deal with (8) (CRITICISE), and what makes us feel stressed. People who had seemed (9) (FRIEND) turned out to be shy.

Some companies use personality tests in (10) (EMPLOY) decisions, which experts consider (11) (RESPONSIBLE) because there is little evidence that the tests predict how well someone will do a job. There is also a danger that people use their colour as an excuse: "Sorry I was late, I'm blue – I'm not a natural (12) (ORGANISE)."

My advice? Take the test with a smile and a pinch of salt. Treat the result as a starting point for discussion, not as a (13) (SCIENCE) fact. And remember that people are far more (14) (COMPLICATE) than four colours. After all, my colleague who is supposed to be the calmest person in the office still loses his temper (15) (REGULAR) when the printer jams.

4. useful

6. rude

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. scepticism
a great deal of + samostalnik: sceptical → scepticism. »a great deal of« + nešteven samostalnik: scepticism (dvom).
2. unscientific
Negativna ocena (at best … at worst): un- + scientific. Negativna ocena: nikalna predpona un- pred scientific.
3. impossible
Smisel: nemogoče je vsakogar dati v en okvir. Smisel je nemogočnost: im- (pred p) + possible.
4. useful
were + pridevnik: use → useful. were + pridevnik: useful (koristen).
5. decisive
Pridevnik ob direct, quick: decide → decisive. Vrsta pridevnikov (direct, quick, …): decisive (odločen).
6. rude
was not + pridevnik: rudeness → rude. Za was not pridevnik: rude (nevljuden).
7. accuracy
its + samostalnik: accurate → accuracy. Za its samostalnik: accuracy (natančnost).
8. criticism
deal with + samostalnik: criticise → criticism. deal with + samostalnik: criticism (kritika).
9. unfriendly
Nasprotje: zdeli so se neprijazni, a so le sramežljivi. Nasprotje »a so le sramežljivi« zahteva negativni pridevnik: unfriendly.
10. employment
Samostalnik pred decisions: employ → employment. Samostalnik kot prilastek pred decisions: employment (zaposlovanje).
11. irresponsible
Strokovnjaki to štejejo za neodgovorno: ir- + responsible. Strokovnjaki obsojajo – ir- (pred r) + responsible.
12. organiser
a natural + oseba: organise → organiser. »a natural« + oseba: organiser.
13. scientific
Pridevnik pred fact: science → scientific. Pridevnik pred samostalnikom fact: scientific.
14. complicated
far more + pridevnik: complicate → complicated. far more + pridevnik: complicated (zapleten).
15. regularly
Prislov ob glagolu loses: regular → regularly. Ob glagolu loses prislov: regularly.

You are going to listen to an interview with Anna Berg, a Norwegian free diver who swims under frozen lakes. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Anna, you hold a world record for swimming under ice without breathing equipment. How far did you swim?

Anna: Ninety-five metres, in a lake in northern Norway, on a single breath. The water was about two degrees, and the ice above me was half a metre thick. I wore only a swimsuit, goggles and a hat.

Interviewer: Why no wetsuit?

Anna: For this record the rules don't allow one. Many people think that's crazy, but the body is surprisingly well designed for cold. In the first seconds your heart rate drops and the blood moves away from your arms and legs towards the organs that matter most. It's called the diving reflex, and every human has it, even babies.

Interviewer: How did you get into this sport?

Anna: I grew up on a farm next to a lake, and my grandmother swam in it every morning, all year round. When I was twelve she took me with her in January. I screamed, but I was hooked. I didn't start free diving seriously until I was thirty, after a difficult divorce. I needed something that made my mind completely quiet.

Interviewer: Is it dangerous?

Anna: Very, if you're careless. Under ice you can't simply come up for air – you have to find the hole you went in through. So we drill a second hole every twenty-five metres in case something goes wrong, and I'm connected to a safety line. I have a team of six divers and a doctor with me. The cold isn't the biggest risk. Panic is.

Interviewer: How do you train?

Anna: Mostly in a normal swimming pool, and on land. I do yoga and breathing exercises, and I spend a lot of time in cold showers. Mental training is half the work. Before a dive I imagine every metre, every stroke, until it feels like something I've already done.

Interviewer: What's next?

Anna: I want to use the attention to talk about climate change. The lakes where I train used to freeze in November. Now we sometimes wait until January. In twenty years, there may not be enough ice for this sport at all.

Swimming under the ice

  1. 0.Anna Berg holds a world record. (T)

  3. 2.The water temperature was below zero. T / F
  4. 3.Anna was allowed to wear a wetsuit for the record. T / F
  5. 4.During a dive in cold water, blood moves towards the body's most important organs. T / F
  6. 5.Anna first swam in the cold lake with her grandmother. T / F
  7. 6.Anna has been free diving seriously since she was a teenager. T / F
  8. 7.Holes are drilled in the ice at regular distances for safety. T / F
  9. 8.According to Anna, cold is the greatest danger under the ice. T / F
  10. 9.Anna does most of her training in lakes. T / F
  11. 10.The lakes where Anna trains now freeze later than they used to. T / F

1. T
2. F
3. F
4. T
5. T

10. T
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
»Ninety-five metres … on a single breath«. T: razdalja 95 m na en vdih je točno tista iz posnetka.
2. F
Voda je imela približno dve stopinji. F: voda je imela okoli dve stopinji, torej nad ničlo (led je zgoraj, voda pod njim ni pod 0 °C).
3. F
»the rules don't allow one«. F: pravila neoprena ne dovolijo.
4. T
»the blood moves away from your arms and legs towards the organs that matter most«. T: kri se umakne iz rok in nog k najpomembnejšim organom.
5. T
»When I was twelve she took me with her in January«. T: babica jo je pri dvanajstih prvič vzela s seboj januarja.
6. F
Resno se je začela potapljati šele pri tridesetih. F: resno potapljanje je začela šele pri tridesetih, ne kot najstnica.
7. T
»we drill a second hole every twenty-five metres«. T: vsakih 25 m izvrtajo drugo luknjo – v rednih razmikih.
8. F
»The cold isn't the biggest risk. Panic is.« F: največja nevarnost je panika, ne mraz.
9. F
Večinoma trenira v bazenu in na kopnem. F: večinoma trenira v bazenu in na kopnem.
10. T
Včasih so zamrznila novembra, zdaj šele januarja. T: jezera zdaj zamrznejo januarja namesto novembra – pozneje.

naloge.besedilo:
You are going to listen to an interview with Dr Mia Torres about communication among wild chimpanzees. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Torres, you've spent fifteen years watching chimpanzees in Uganda. What were you looking for?

Dr Torres: Gestures. Chimpanzees use their voices, of course, but they also use their hands, faces and bodies to send very specific messages. We've now recorded more than seventy different gestures, and we're still finding new ones.

Interviewer: How do you study animals that live high in the trees?

Dr Torres: With enormous patience. The first rule is to behave as boringly as possible. If you're quiet and predictable, after a few months the chimps stop paying attention to you, and that's when they show you their real lives. I spend most days sitting on the ground with a video camera and a notebook, often for ten hours at a time.

Interviewer: Can you give an example of a gesture?

Dr Torres: One of my favourites is a gentle touch on the back of another chimp's hand. It means 'let's go' – a mother uses it with her baby when she wants to move on. Another is a loud slap on the ground, which is a way of saying 'stop that' or 'go away'. What's fascinating is that the meanings seem to be the same in different groups that have never met.

Interviewer: Does that tell us something about human language?

Dr Torres: We think it might. Babies point and wave long before they can speak, and many of their gestures look very similar to those of young chimps. One study even found that adults could guess the meaning of chimpanzee gestures from videos more often than chance would predict. That suggests that our ancestors may have communicated with their hands before they used words.

Interviewer: What are the biggest threats to the chimps you study?

Dr Torres: Loss of forest, mainly to farming, and diseases that humans pass on to them – a simple cold can kill a chimpanzee. That's why researchers in our project wear masks and keep a distance of at least seven metres.

How chimpanzees talk to each other

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where does Dr Torres study chimpanzees?
    In Uganda.
  2. 1.How many different chimpanzee gestures have been recorded?
  3. 2.What is the first rule when studying chimpanzees?
  4. 3.What equipment does Dr Torres use in the forest?
  5. 4.What does a gentle touch on the back of the hand mean?
  6. 5.What does a loud slap on the ground mean?
  7. 6.What is surprising about the meanings of the gestures?
  8. 7.What do babies do before they can speak?
  9. 8.Why do researchers wear masks?
naloge.rezultat:
1. More than seventy.
2. To behave as boringly as possible. / To be quiet and predictable.
3. A video camera and a notebook.
4. Let's go.
5. Stop that. / Go away.
6. They are the same in different groups.
7. Point and wave.
8. To protect chimps from human diseases.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. More than seventy.
»more than seventy different gestures«. »How many« = število; »more than« je del podatka.
2. To behave as boringly as possible. / To be quiet and predictable.
»behave as boringly as possible«. »The first rule« v vprašanju ustreza pravilu, ki ga dr. Torres navede prvo; »boringly« pomeni, da šimpanzov ne vznemirjaš.
3. A video camera and a notebook.
»with a video camera and a notebook«. »Equipment« = oprema; navedeš oba predmeta (kamera in zvezek).
4. Let's go.
»It means 'let's go'«. Pomen geste pove s premim govorom: 'let's go' (gremo).
5. Stop that. / Go away.
Dovolj je ena od obeh razlag. Govorec navede dve razlagi udarca po tleh; zadošča ena.
6. They are the same in different groups.
»the meanings seem to be the same in different groups that have never met«. »Surprising« = presenetljivo; pomeni so enaki v skupinah, ki se nikoli niso srečale.
7. Point and wave.
»Babies point and wave long before they can speak«. »Before they can speak« = preden znajo govoriti; dojenčki kažejo in mahajo, kar je podobno gestam šimpanzov.
8. To protect chimps from human diseases.
Človeške bolezni so za šimpanze smrtno nevarne; zato maske in razdalja. »Why« zahteva namen: zaščititi šimpanze pred človeškimi boleznimi (ne obratno).

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

You have just finished your matura exams and you are looking for a part-time summer job. You have seen this advertisement online:

CITY BIKE TOURS – GUIDES WANTED
We are looking for friendly students to lead bike tours for foreign visitors in Ljubljana. Flexible hours, good pay, free bike.
We are looking for: a good knowledge of the city • communication skills • reliability

Write an e-mail of application of 120–150 words to City Bike Tours, in which you:

  • give two reasons why you are a good candidate for the job and explain each of them,
  • ask about the length of the tours and the payment.
TO: jobs@citybiketours.si
SUBJECT: Application
Dear Sir or Madam,
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-sporočilo (prošnja), ki navede in razloži dva razloga (povezana z zahtevami iz oglasa) ter vpraša o dolžini ogledov in plačilu; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. give two reasons why you are a good candidate for the job and explain each of them
  3. ask about the length of the tours and the payment
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba prošnje
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor.
I am writing to apply for the position of bike tour guide advertised on your website.
Namen in vir oglasa.
Firstly, I have lived in Ljubljana all my life and know many interesting stories about its history and architecture.
1. razlog + razlaga – oglas zahteva poznavanje mesta.
Secondly, I have good communication skills: I have worked as a volunteer at the city library, helping foreign students.
2. razlog + razlaga (dokaz). Povezovalca Firstly, Secondly.
I would also like to ask how long the tours usually last and whether the payment is per tour or per hour.
Obe vprašanji iz iztočnice; posredno vprašanje (how long the tours last).
I look forward to hearing from you. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Formalni zaključek.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of bike tour guide which I saw advertised on your website.

I believe I would be a good candidate for two reasons. Firstly, I have lived in Ljubljana all my life and know many interesting stories about its history and architecture, from the Roman walls to Plečnik's bridges. Secondly, I have good communication skills. Last year I volunteered as a guide during our school's open day, and I also speak fluent English and some German, so I can easily talk to foreign visitors.

I would also like to ask a few questions. How long do the tours usually last, and how many tours would I lead per day? Could you also tell me whether guides are paid per hour or per tour?

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Ana Horvat

Število besed: 146 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. People show their true character in a crisis.
  2. Buying local food is worth the higher price.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt
Uvod: stališče (I mostly agree that difficult situations reveal what people are really like).
Jasna teza.
Argument 1: in a crisis people have no time to pretend; e.g. the 2023 floods in Slovenia, when neighbours helped each other.
Primer iz Slovenije je konkreten in prepričljiv.
Argument 2: some people surprise us – quiet people become leaders.
Povezovalci: Moreover, Similarly.
Protiargument: stress can make good people behave badly, so a single moment is not the whole truth.
Delno se strinjaš – zato »mostly agree«.
Sklep: a crisis shows an important part of character, but not all of it.
Sklep odgovori na »How far do you agree?«.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: fresher food, support for farmers, fewer transport emissions. Against: not everyone can afford it; some 'local' labels are misleading.
Izberi en naslov.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
People show their true character in a crisis.

When everything goes well, it is easy to be kind, patient and generous. Many people therefore believe that we only see someone's true character in a crisis. I largely agree with this statement, although I think that a crisis can also change people.

Firstly, a crisis removes the time to pretend. During the floods in Slovenia in 2023, there was no time to think about how to look good. Some people immediately drove to the flooded villages with shovels and food, while others used the situation to raise prices. Both reactions showed what these people valued most.

Secondly, a crisis reveals qualities that stay hidden in everyday life. My grandmother, who seems quiet and shy, organised the whole street when our neighbour's house caught fire. Nobody would have expected such calm leadership from her, not even our family, and she herself was surprised by her courage.

On the other hand, critics argue that people under extreme stress do not act normally, so we should not judge them by a single moment. This is partly true, as fear can make even good people selfish. However, how someone behaves after the first shock still tells us a great deal about them.

All things considered, I believe that a crisis is the best test of character, even if it is not the only one.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and choose the correct answer (A, B, C or D). There is an example at the beginning (0).

The Collector

Mr Ferris collected things that other people threw away. Not rubbish, exactly – he was very particular about that – but objects that had lost their purpose: keys without locks, single gloves, maps of towns that had since changed their names. He kept them in labelled boxes in the attic of the narrow house on Pell Street, where he had lived alone since his sister's death.

I was eleven when I began to visit him, officially to deliver the newspaper, unofficially because he paid me in stories. Each week he would choose an object from a box and tell me where it had come from. A brass key had belonged to a lighthouse in Cornwall. A child's shoe had been found in the ruins of a bombed theatre. A ticket for a train that no longer ran had been bought, he said, by a woman who never used it, because the man she was meant to meet had changed his mind.

I believed every word. It was only years later, sorting through the boxes after his funeral, that I found the notebooks. In them, in his small, careful handwriting, were the stories – each one drafted, crossed out and rewritten several times. Some objects had three or four different histories. The brass key had once belonged to a prison, then to a castle, before he finally settled on the lighthouse.

My first reaction was anger, as if I had been cheated of something. My mother, who had never liked my visits to Pell Street, said that she had always known the old man was "a bit of a fantasist". But the anger did not last. Reading the notebooks, I began to understand what he had been doing. He had not been lying to me; he had been practising. Every week he had tested a story on his only audience, watched my face, and gone back to his desk to improve it.

He never published anything. As far as I know, he never showed the notebooks to anyone. Perhaps he did not think they were good enough. Perhaps he was simply happy to have one listener who wanted to hear the next chapter.

I kept the brass key. It sits on my desk now, beside the laptop on which I write my own stories. When I get stuck, I pick it up and ask it where it has been. It always has an answer, though rarely the same one twice.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.Where did Mr Ferris keep his collection?
    A In the cellar.B In the attic.C In his sister's house.D In a shop.
    Answer: B
  2. 1.What kind of objects did Mr Ferris collect?
    A Valuable antiques.B Things that were no longer useful.C Rubbish from the streets.D Souvenirs from his travels.
  3. 2.Why did the narrator really visit Mr Ferris?
    A To earn money.B To deliver the newspaper.C To hear his stories.D Because her mother asked her to.
  4. 3.According to Mr Ferris, why was the train ticket never used?
    A The train was cancelled.B The woman lost it.C A man did not come to meet her.D The woman changed her mind.
  5. 4.What did the narrator discover after Mr Ferris died?
    A That the objects were worthless.B That he had invented the stories carefully.C That he had been a famous writer.D That his sister had written the stories.
  6. 5.What does the history of the brass key show?
    A Mr Ferris tried several versions before choosing one.B The key really belonged to a lighthouse.C Mr Ferris had worked in a prison.D The key was the oldest object in the collection.
  7. 6.How did the narrator's mother feel about Mr Ferris?
    A She admired his imagination.B She had never trusted him completely.C She was grateful for his kindness.D She did not know about the visits.
  8. 7.Why did the narrator's anger disappear?
    A She realised he had been practising his writing.B Her mother apologised.C She found money in the boxes.D She forgot about the notebooks.
  9. 8.What role did the narrator play for Mr Ferris?
    A A critic.B A co-author.C An audience.D A publisher.
  10. 9.What does the narrator suggest about why Mr Ferris never published?
    A He was afraid of critics.B He had no money.C He may have been content with one listener.D He died before he could finish.
  11. 10.What does the narrator do with the key when she cannot continue writing?
    A She locks her desk.B She uses it to imagine a story.C She reads the notebooks again.D She thinks of selling it.
naloge.rezultat:
1. B
2. C
3. C
4. B
5. A
6. B
7. A
8. C
9. C
10. B
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: izbrati eno od štirih možnosti (A–D).
  • Postopek: najprej preberi vprašanje brez možnosti in v besedilu poišči odgovor; šele nato preberi možnosti in izberi tisto, ki pove isto z drugimi besedami (parafraza).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilna možnost se ujema s pomenom besedila; napačne možnosti pogosto uporabijo iste besede kot besedilo, a povedo nekaj drugega, preveč posplošijo (always, never) ali so resnične, a ne odgovarjajo na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. B
»objects that had lost their purpose« – ne smeti (»Not rubbish, exactly«). »objects that had lost their purpose« pomeni stvari, ki niso več uporabne (B). C odpade, ker besedilo izrecno reče »Not rubbish«.
2. C
Uradno časopis, neuradno »because he paid me in stories«. Uradni razlog (časopis) ni pravi; »paid me in stories« pomeni, da je hodila zaradi zgodb (C).
3. C
»the man she was meant to meet had changed his mind«. Po Ferrisovi zgodbi si je moški, s katerim naj bi se ženska srečala, premislil – torej ni prišel (C). D pripiše spremembo napačni osebi.
4. B
Zvezki z večkrat prepisanimi zgodbami. Zvezki s prepisanimi različicami kažejo, da je zgodbe skrbno izmišljal (B).
5. A
Ključ je bil najprej iz zapora, nato iz gradu in na koncu iz svetilnika. Ključ je imel v zvezkih več različnih zgodovin, preden je izbral eno (A); ostale možnosti so le ena od različic.
6. B
Obiskov ni marala, imela ga je za »fantasist«. Mati ga je imela za »fantasist« (sanjača, izmišljevalca) in obiskov ni marala – ni mu povsem zaupala (B).
7. A
»He had not been lying to me; he had been practising.« Spoznala je, da ni lagal, ampak vadil pisanje (A).
8. C
»tested a story on his only audience«. »his only audience« = njegovo edino občinstvo (C).
9. C
»Perhaps he was simply happy to have one listener«. »Perhaps« pokaže domnevo: morda mu je zadoščal en poslušalec (C).
10. B
Vpraša ključ, kje je bil – sproži domišljijo. Ključ ji pomaga, da si izmisli zgodbo (B) – nadaljuje Ferrisov način.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and match the statements with the paragraphs. More than one statement may refer to the same paragraph. There is an example at the beginning: Example 0.

Five board games worth clearing the table for

Board games are enjoying a golden age. Here are five very different games for very different players.

A Moonfall

Moonfall is a co-operative game in which all players work together to save a space station from a falling moon. There is no single winner: either everybody survives or nobody does. The tension comes from a deck of event cards that makes things worse every turn. It is an excellent choice for families with competitive children, because nobody can gloat.

B Inkwell

In Inkwell, players are rival writers in nineteenth-century London, competing to publish novels before their opponents. The rules take about an hour to learn, and the first game can feel slow, but experienced players love the way every decision affects later ones. The illustrations, by a former newspaper cartoonist, are worth the price on their own.

C Snap Decision

This is the opposite of Inkwell: a party game that you can explain in thirty seconds. One player reads a question, everybody writes an answer, and points go to the players who agree with the majority. It works best with at least six people and gets louder as the evening goes on. Older relatives who claim to hate board games tend to enjoy it most.

D Harvest

Harvest is a calm farming game in which players plant crops, build fences and feed their families through the seasons. There is very little direct conflict, which makes it a good introduction for people who dislike games where you attack each other. A solo mode means you can also play it alone, and many players say they find it relaxing after work.

E Shadow Court

Shadow Court is a game of lies. Each player secretly belongs to one of two groups at a royal court, and the aim is to discover who your allies are while hiding your own identity. It can damage friendships if taken too seriously, and it does not work with fewer than five players. But when it goes well, it produces stories that players will be retelling for years.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Which game prevents players from boasting about winning? (A)
  2. 1.Which game can be played by one person?
  3. 2.Which game needs a large group to work well?
  4. 3.Which game has artwork that is especially recommended?
  5. 4.Which game makes all players win or lose together?
  6. 5.Which game may cause tension between friends?
  7. 6.Which game rewards players who think like everybody else?
  8. 7.Which game becomes more rewarding with experience?
  9. 8.Which game is suitable for players who dislike conflict?
  10. 9.Which game is popular with people who say they do not like games?
  11. 10.Which game creates memorable experiences?
naloge.rezultat:
1. D
2. C
3. B
4. A
5. E
6. C
7. B
8. D
9. C
10. E
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. D
»A solo mode means you can also play it alone«. »alone« = sam; samo igra D ima način za enega igralca.
2. C
»works best with at least six people«; E zahteva vsaj pet. »at least six« za C; E zahteva pet, a besedilo pri C poudari, da deluje najbolje v veliki skupini.
3. B
Ilustracije nekdanjega karikaturista. Ilustracije nekdanjega karikaturista so posebej pohvaljene pri B.
4. A
»either everybody survives or nobody does«. »everybody survives or nobody does« = vsi zmagajo ali vsi izgubijo (sodelovalna igra).
5. E
»It can damage friendships if taken too seriously«. »damage friendships« = napetosti med prijatelji.
6. C
»points go to the players who agree with the majority«. »agree with the majority« = misliti kot vsi drugi.
7. B
»experienced players love the way every decision affects later ones«. »experienced players« in odločitve z daljšimi posledicami = igra je z izkušnjami boljša.
8. D
»very little direct conflict«. »very little direct conflict« ustreza igralcem, ki ne marajo spopadov.
9. C
»Older relatives who claim to hate board games tend to enjoy it most«. »claim to hate board games« = pravijo, da ne marajo iger.
10. E
»stories that players will be retelling for years«. »retelling for years« = nepozabna doživetja.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The library that floats

In a country (0) many villages can only be reached by river, books are not easy to find. That is why, ten years ago, a retired teacher in Bangladesh decided (1) turn an old wooden boat into a floating library.

Every morning the boat sets off from the town of Sirajganj and travels (2) village to village along the river. When it arrives, children run to the bank, climb on board and spend an hour reading, (3) the boat's solar-powered computers are used for lessons in English and maths.

The project began with just one boat and a few hundred books, most of (4) had been donated by friends. Today, there are more than twenty boats, and they serve around 90,000 people. Some of the boats also work as schools for children (5) families cannot afford to send them to the town.

The idea was born (6) necessity. In the rainy season, large parts of the region are flooded for months, and roads disappear (7) water. "If the children can't go to school, the school must go to the children," says the founder, (8) himself grew up in a village on the river.

The boats have also changed the lives of adults. In the evenings, they are used for courses on farming, health and (9) to deal with floods. Women in particular have benefited, because many of (10) were not able to leave their villages to study.

Climate change has made the project more important than ever. Floods are becoming (11) frequent and more severe, and every year thousands of families lose their homes. "We (12) always tried to teach people to live with the water, not against it," the founder explains.

The idea has spread far beyond Bangladesh. Floating libraries and schools now operate in Nigeria, Cambodia and the Philippines. For the founder, this is the greatest reward. "When I started, people laughed at (13). They said a boat full of books was a crazy dream. Now they come to ask how they can build one (14)." He smiles. "Sometimes the best ideas are the ones (15) seem impossible."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. where
naloge.rezultat:
1. to
2. from
3. while / and / or
4. which
5. whose
6. of
7. under
8. who
9. how
10. them
11. more
12. have
13. me
14. themselves / too
15. that / which
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. to
decide to + nedoločnik. decide + to + nedoločnik.
2. from
from village to village. from … to … = od vasi do vasi.
3. while / and / or
Sočasna dejanja: while the computers are used. Dve sočasni dejanji: while (medtem ko).
4. which
most of which – oziralni zaimek za stvari po predlogu. Za predlogom (most of) za stvari which.
5. whose
children whose families – svojilni oziralni zaimek. whose = katerih (svojilni oziralni zaimek): otroci, katerih družine …
6. of
be born of necessity = nastati iz nuje. be born of necessity = nastati iz nuje.
7. under
disappear under water. disappear under water = izginiti pod vodo.
8. who
Nedoločni oziralni stavek za osebo: who himself grew up. Za vejico in osebo who.
9. how
how to deal with floods. how to + nedoločnik = kako.
10. them
many of them – osebni zaimek za ženske. Osebni zaimek v predmetni obliki po of: many of them.
11. more
more frequent and more severe – vzporedni primernik. Vzporedna primernika: more frequent and more severe.
12. have
Present perfect: We have always tried. Present perfect z always (od nekdaj do zdaj): have always tried.
13. me
laughed at me. laugh at + zaimek v predmetni obliki: me.
14. themselves / too
build one themselves – povratni zaimek za poudarek. Povratni zaimek za poudarek (sami): themselves.
15. that / which
the ones that seem impossible. Oziralni zaimek za ones (stvari): that/which.
