naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt
Uvod: stališče (I partly agree that the books and news we read shape who we are).
Teza.
Argument 1: reading builds empathy – we experience other lives; primer knjige.
Primer.
Argument 2: what we read online shapes our opinions (algorithms, echo chambers).
Povezovalci.
Protiargument: experiences, family and friends matter more than books.
Delno strinjanje.
Sklep.
Odgovor na vprašanje »How far …«.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: students copy answers, stop thinking. Against: AI can be a tutor if used wisely; the problem is how we use it.
Izberi en naslov.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
We are what we read.

The books, articles and posts we read every day fill our minds with ideas, images and opinions. It is therefore often said that we are what we read. I agree with this statement to a large extent, although reading is only one of many influences on our personality.

Firstly, what we read shapes our opinions. A person who reads only one newspaper or follows only one type of account on social media will probably see the world in a very narrow way. On the other hand, someone who reads widely is more likely to understand different points of view and to question what they are told.

Secondly, books can influence our values and even our decisions. When I was fourteen, I read a novel about a girl who volunteered in a refugee camp. It made me think about people whose lives are very different from mine, and the following summer I joined a local volunteer group.

However, critics argue that our families, friends and experiences shape us far more than reading. This is certainly true, as a book cannot replace real relationships. Still, reading often helps us understand those experiences and gives us words to describe them.

All things considered, I believe that our reading does not decide who we are, but it plays an important part in who we become.

Število besed: 226 (zahtevanih 220–250). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Visitor

The woman who came to the door that Thursday was wearing a red coat that was far too warm for September. She asked for my grandmother by her first name, Nell, which nobody had used for years, and when I said that Nell had died in the spring, she sat down on the doorstep as if her legs had been taken away.

I did not know what to do, so I made tea. That was what my grandmother would have done. The woman – she said her name was Irene – drank it slowly, holding the cup with both hands, and told me that she and Nell had been at school together in Glasgow during the war. They had been evacuated to the same farm in the Highlands, aged eight, with labels tied to their coats and a gas mask each in a cardboard box.

"We promised to write," Irene said. "And we did, for a while. Then her family moved to England and mine went to Canada, and the letters stopped. I always thought I'd find her one day."

She had flown from Toronto, at eighty-four, with an address that was thirty years out of date. It had taken her two days and the help of a very patient postman to find our house.

I showed her the photographs I had found while clearing out my grandmother's bedroom. Most of them meant nothing to me: unsmiling children in front of a stone farmhouse, a dog, a man with a horse. Irene knew every face. She named the farmer and his wife, the dog – Bess – and a boy called Archie who had fallen through the ice on the pond and been pulled out by my grandmother. I had never heard that story. My grandmother, who could talk for an hour about the price of butter, had never mentioned it.

When Irene left, I gave her one of the photographs: two girls on a gate, squinting into the sun. She put it inside her coat, against her chest, and did not say anything.

A week later a parcel arrived from Canada. Inside was a bundle of letters tied with ribbon, all written in my grandmother's round, careful hand, and all signed "your sister, Nell". There was a note from Irene, too. "These belong in your family now," it said. "She was braver than she ever let you know."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.When did the narrator's grandmother die?
    In the spring.
  2. 1.What was unusual about the visitor's clothing?
  3. 2.How did the visitor react to the news of Nell's death?
  4. 3.Why did the narrator make tea?
  5. 4.Where were the two girls sent during the war?
  6. 5.Why did the girls stop writing to each other?
  7. 6.Who helped Irene to find the house?
  8. 7.What did Nell do for Archie?
  9. 8.What surprised the narrator about the story of Archie?
  10. 9.What did the narrator give Irene?
  11. 10.How did Nell sign her letters?

1. Her coat was too warm (for September).
2. She sat down on the doorstep.
3. Grandmother would have done it.
4. To a farm in the Highlands.
5. Their families moved (to England and Canada).
6. A (very patient) postman.
7. She pulled him out of the (icy) pond.
8. Grandmother had never mentioned it.
9. A photograph (of two girls on a gate).
10. Your sister, Nell.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Her coat was too warm (for September).
»a red coat that was far too warm for September«. Nenavadno: rdeč plašč, pretopel za september.
2. She sat down on the doorstep.
»she sat down on the doorstep as if her legs had been taken away«. Odziv: sedla je na prag, kot da bi ji odpovedale noge.
3. Grandmother would have done it.
»That was what my grandmother would have done.« »Why« = razlog; tako bi storila babica.
4. To a farm in the Highlands.
»evacuated to the same farm in the Highlands«. »Where« = kraj evakuacije; kmetija v Škotskem višavju.
5. Their families moved (to England and Canada).
Družini sta se preselili, pisma so prenehala. Družini sta se preselili (Anglija, Kanada), zato so pisma prenehala.
6. A (very patient) postman.
»the help of a very patient postman«. »Who« = oseba; zelo potrpežljiv poštar.
7. She pulled him out of the (icy) pond.
Archie je padel skozi led, Nell ga je potegnila ven. Nell je Archieja potegnila iz zaledenelega ribnika.
8. Grandmother had never mentioned it.
Babica, ki je govorila o ceni masla, te zgodbe ni nikoli omenila. Presenečenje: babica, ki je govorila o vsakdanjih stvareh, zgodbe ni nikoli omenila.
9. A photograph (of two girls on a gate).
»I gave her one of the photographs«. Podarila ji je fotografijo dveh deklic na ograji.
10. Your sister, Nell.
»all signed 'your sister, Nell'«. Podpis »your sister« pokaže, kako blizu sta si bili.

Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (C).

Our online selves are not as private as we think

However hard we try to keep "real life" separate from social media, the two are becoming impossible to separate. [0] What we post – and what others post about us – increasingly shapes how we are seen at school, at work and even in court.

Employers are a good example. Surveys suggest that around seven in ten companies look at candidates' social media profiles before offering them a job. [1] A photograph from a party five years ago or an angry comment in an online argument can be enough to tip the balance.

Young people are often more aware of this than adults assume. [2] Many keep two accounts: a public one, carefully designed to impress, and a private one for close friends, where they can be more honest.

Yet even careful users cannot control everything. [3] A friend might share a photograph, a classmate might take a screenshot, and once something has been copied, it can never be fully deleted.

The consequences can be serious. [4] Psychologists say that teenagers who are bullied online often feel there is no escape, because the bullying follows them home on their phones.

Some countries have introduced a "right to be forgotten", which allows people to ask search engines to remove certain information about them. [5] Critics say it is too easy to abuse, while supporters argue that people should not be judged forever by a single mistake.

Schools are beginning to respond as well. [6] Lessons on digital citizenship teach students how to protect their privacy, think before posting and support friends who are targeted.

Experts agree, however, that rules and lessons are not enough. [7] We need to accept that people change, and that the person someone was at fifteen is not necessarily the person they are at twenty-five.

Perhaps the healthiest approach is to remember that an online profile is never the whole story. [8] Behind every post is a real person – complicated, imperfect and still growing. [9]

So the next time you are about to post something in anger, wait a moment. [10]

  5. EOther people's posts can reveal what we have chosen to hide.
  6. FWhat we really need is a change in attitude.
  7. GMost students say they have never used social media.
  8. HCyberbullying, for example, has been linked to anxiety and depression.
  9. IThat is something worth remembering every time we scroll.
  10. JSeveral have added online safety to the timetable.
  11. KIt is like a shop window: it shows only what we want people to see.
  12. LMany adults spend more time online than their children.
  13. MTomorrow, you may be glad you did.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. B
Nadaljuje misel o delodajalcih in pripravi primer s fotografijo z zabave. »Some even admit« stopnjuje misel o delodajalcih; sledi primer fotografije z zabave.
2. D
Mladi vedo, da lahko objave vidi bodoči delodajalec – zato dva računa. »They« = mladi; zato imajo dva računa.
3. E
Tudi previdni ne nadzorujejo vsega: objave drugih razkrijejo skrito. Tudi previdni ne nadzorujejo vsega: objave drugih razkrijejo skrito.
4. H
Resne posledice – primer spletnega nadlegovanja. »for example« uvede primer resnih posledic (spletno nadlegovanje).
5. A
Pravica do pozabe – v EU del zakonodaje. »this right« = pravica do pozabe; v EU od leta 2018.
6. J
Šole se odzivajo: varnost na spletu na urniku, sledi opis pouka. »Several« = šole; sledi opis pouka o varnosti.
7. F
Pravila niso dovolj – potrebujemo spremembo odnosa; sledi »We need to accept …«. »What we really need« – nasprotje pravilom; sledi »We need to accept …«.
8. K
Profil kot izložba: kaže le, kar želimo pokazati. Primera z izložbo pojasni, da profil kaže le izbrano.
9. I
Zaključna misel: zapomniti si ob vsakem drsenju po zaslonu. »That« se nanaša na prejšnjo misel; zaključni nauk.

Nasvet »počakaj« – jutri boš morda vesel, da si. »you did« se navezuje na nasvet, da počakaš.

He taught himself the necessary maths and physics (2) watching university lectures on the internet. "I failed many times," he admits. "The first engine I built exploded (3) it even left the ground."

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. of
attract the attention of. attract the attention of = pritegniti pozornost.
2. by
by + -ing = s tem, da … by + -ing = s tem, da.
3. before
before it even left the ground. before it even left the ground = preden je sploh vzletela.
4. that
insist that + stavek (s konjunktivom: take, wear). insist that + stavek.
5. all
at all times. at all times = vedno.
6. whether / if
find out whether they were (possible) or not. find out whether/if = ugotoviti, ali.
7. who
Nedoločni oziralni stavek za osebo. Za vejico in osebo who.
8. within / in
within seconds. within seconds = v nekaj sekundah.
9. more
more than two million times. more than + število.
10. who
Nedoločni oziralni stavek za osebo (founder). Za vejico in osebo who.
11. who / that
anyone who understood. anyone who/that = vsak, ki.
12. else
someone else. someone else = nekdo drug.
13. of
be afraid of + -ing. be afraid of + -ing.
14. make
make sure. make sure = poskrbeti.
15. about / that
found out about it the hard way – pri tej vrzeli je smiselna tudi beseda that. find out about = izvedeti za; the hard way = na težji način.

Why some cities are switching off at night

Night-time darkness used to be taken for granted. Today, more than eighty per cent of the world's population lives under skies affected by artificial light, and in Europe and North America the figure is close to (0) (HUNDRED) per cent. Scientists warn that this "light pollution" has serious (1) (CONSEQUENT) for both people and wildlife.

For animals, the effects can be (2) (DESTROY). Birds that migrate at night use the stars to navigate, and bright city lights can draw them off course, causing millions of (3) (COLLIDE) with buildings every year. Newly hatched sea turtles head towards the brightest horizon, which should be the sea but is often a road. Insects, which play an (4) (ESSENCE) role in pollinating plants, are attracted to street lamps in such numbers that local populations can (5) (APPEAR) altogether.

Humans are affected too. Our bodies produce a hormone called melatonin in the dark, which helps us sleep. Exposure to light at night reduces its (6) (PRODUCE) and has been linked to sleep disorders, (7) (OBESE) and even some forms of cancer.

Some towns have decided to act. In parts of France, shops must now switch off their window lights after 1 a.m., and several towns have reduced street (8) (LIGHT) in quiet areas. The results have been (9) (ENCOURAGE): energy bills have fallen, and residents report that they can see the stars again.

Critics worry that darker streets will make people feel less safe. However, research from several countries suggests that crime does not (10) (NECESSARY) increase when lights are dimmed. What matters, experts say, is not the amount of light but its (11) (DIRECT): lamps that shine downwards light the pavement without lighting up the sky.

In 2001, the town of Flagstaff in Arizona became the world's first "International Dark Sky Community". Since then, dozens of places have followed, attracting tourists who are (12) (WILL) to travel long distances to see the Milky Way. For many visitors, it is an (13) (FORGET) experience.

Perhaps the most (14) (REMARK) thing about light pollution is how easily it could be solved. Unlike most environmental problems, it disappears almost (15) (INSTANT) when we switch off the lights.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.

You will hear a recording in which Liam Doyle, the lead singer of an Irish rock band, talks about his life. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

I got my nickname, 'Sparrow', at school in Dublin, because I was the smallest boy in the class and I never stopped singing. I hated it at first. Now it's on the cover of every album, so I suppose I've made my peace with it.

We started the band forty years ago in my parents' garage. There were four of us, all fifteen, and only one of us could actually play an instrument. Our first concert was at a school disco, and we were so nervous that we played the same song three times because we'd forgotten the others. Somehow, people danced anyway.

It's strange, but the four of us are still together. People often ask how we've managed it, and the honest answer is that we never let money divide us. From the very first day, everything has been split equally – four ways – no matter who wrote the song. That has saved us from a lot of arguments.

My mother died when I was fourteen, and I think that's really why I started writing songs. I didn't know how to talk about what I felt, so I wrote it down instead. Many of our most famous songs are, if you listen carefully, about loss.

Over the years I've used our success to support causes I care about, especially the fight against poverty in Africa. I've met presidents and prime ministers, and I'm sometimes criticised for that. People say a rock star should stick to music. But if a politician will listen to me for ten minutes because I'm famous, I think I'd be foolish not to use those ten minutes.

These days I still write every morning, usually before anyone else in the house is awake. I'm not as fast as I used to be. But I've learned that the best songs often come when you stop trying so hard.

A singer looks back

You will hear a recording about a new book on Harold Gillies, a pioneer of plastic surgery. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Today I'm talking to the historian Dr Laura Finch, whose new book tells the story of Harold Gillies, the man often called the father of modern plastic surgery. Laura, why did you want to write about him?

Dr Finch: Simply because it's a wonderful story. Gillies was a New Zealander who came to England to study medicine and ended up working as an ear, nose and throat surgeon. When the First World War began, he volunteered for the Red Cross and was sent to France.

Presenter: And that changed his career?

Dr Finch: Completely. The war produced injuries that doctors had never seen before. New weapons, especially shells and machine guns, caused terrible damage to soldiers' faces. In the trenches, a man's head was often the only part of his body above ground, so facial wounds were extremely common.

Presenter: What did Gillies do differently?

Dr Finch: Before him, surgeons simply closed the wound as quickly as possible, which often left men unable to eat or speak properly. Gillies insisted on rebuilding the face step by step, using skin and bone from other parts of the patient's own body. He also made detailed drawings before each operation, with the help of an artist, so that he could plan the result.

Presenter: Where did this work take place?

Dr Finch: At a special hospital in Sidcup, near London, which opened in 1917. More than five thousand men were treated there. Gillies developed a technique called the 'tubed pedicle', a tube of skin that stayed attached to the body and kept its blood supply while it was moved to the face.

Presenter: What happened to the patients after the war?

Dr Finch: Many of them found it very hard to return to normal life. In some towns, benches were painted blue as a signal to the public that men sitting on them might have injured faces. That detail affected me more than anything else I discovered while researching the book.

The surgeon who rebuilt faces

  6. 5.Who helped Gillies to plan operations?
  7. 6.When did the hospital in Sidcup open?
  8. 7.How many men were treated at Sidcup?
  9. 8.What did blue benches signal to the public?

Report

You have just returned from a four-week Erasmus+ exchange in Ireland, where you lived with a host family and attended a secondary school. You have been asked to write a report for the programme coordinators.

Write a report of 150–180 words in which you:

  • describe your experience with the host family,
  • describe the most rewarding course or activity at the school,
  • give an account of a cultural event you took part in.
To: Erasmus+ Coordinators
From: Dominik(a) Novak
Subject: Exchange in Ireland
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, namenom, tremi odstavki s podnaslovi (gostiteljska družina, najkoristnejši predmet, kulturni dogodek) in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (150–180 words), formal style
  2. describe your experience with the host family
  3. describe the most rewarding course or activity at the school
  4. give an account of a cultural event you took part in
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Erasmus+ Coordinators / From: Dominik(a) Novak / Subject: Exchange in Galway
Glava in naslov.
Introduction: The purpose of this report is to describe my four-week exchange in Galway.
Namen.
Host family
I stayed with a welcoming family of five who involved me in daily life, including weekend trips to Connemara.
Konkretni podatki in vtis.
School
The most rewarding course was Irish history, as the teacher used local sources and museum visits.
Kaj in zakaj.
Cultural event
I took part in a traditional céilí, an evening of Irish dancing, where I learned two dances and met many local students.
Opis dogodka.
Conclusion: I would strongly recommend the programme to other students.
Sklep s priporočilom.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Erasmus+ Programme Coordinators
From: Klara Novak
Subject: Exchange in Galway, Ireland

Introduction

The purpose of this report is to describe my four-week Erasmus+ exchange in Galway, Ireland, where I lived with a host family and attended a local secondary school.

Host family

I stayed with the O'Briens, a friendly family with two teenage daughters. They made me feel welcome and included me in their weekend trips. The only drawback was the long bus journey to school, which took almost an hour.

The most rewarding course

The most rewarding activity was the creative writing course. Classes were small, and by the end our group had published a short collection of stories. As a result, I feel much more confident writing in English.

A cultural event

In my third week, I took part in a traditional céilí, an evening of Irish music and dancing at the school. The dancing was easy to learn and everybody joined in.

Conclusion

Overall, the exchange was an extremely valuable experience, and I would recommend it to other students.

Nick Hornby: About a Boy

Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba

  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).

  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).

  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …

Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – Will changes from a man who avoids all responsibility into someone who accepts that he needs other people.
Teza.
Jedro 1 – Will at the beginning: lives on royalties from his father's Christmas song, invents a son to meet single mothers (SPAT).
Konkreten prizor: izmišljeni sin Ned.
Jedro 2 – the turning point: Marcus forces his way into Will's life; Will buys him trainers and starts to care.
Pokaži, kako odnos z Marcusom sproži spremembo.
Jedro 3 – the ending: Will falls in love with Rachel, is honest about himself, and stands by Marcus when he and Ellie get into trouble in Cambridge.
Razvoj: od laži do iskrenosti.
Sklep: the boy in the title is as much Will as Marcus.
Pomen naslova kot sklepna misel.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
How Will Freeman changes in About a Boy

At the beginning of Nick Hornby's About a Boy, Will Freeman is a thirty-six-year-old man who has never grown up. By the end of the novel, he has learned to care about other people and to accept responsibility. This change is caused mainly by his unlikely friendship with twelve-year-old Marcus.

At first, Will lives an empty but comfortable life. He does not need to work, because he earns money from his father's Christmas song, and he fills his days with television, shopping and music. He even invents a two-year-old son, Ned, so that he can join a single parents' group and meet attractive women. This lie shows how selfish and dishonest he is at the start.

Everything begins to change when Marcus discovers the truth and starts visiting Will's flat after school. At first Will only tolerates him, but gradually he begins to help him. He buys Marcus fashionable trainers and teaches him about music, so that he will be bullied less at school. For the first time, Will is thinking about somebody else's problems.

The final stage of his development comes through Rachel. When he falls in love with her, he realises that he cannot continue lying, and he becomes honest about himself. He also stands by Marcus when he and Ellie get into trouble in Cambridge, which shows that he is now willing to take responsibility.

By the end of the novel, Will is no longer an "island". He has become part of a wider network of friends, and he has discovered that relationships, though complicated, give life meaning. Hornby thus presents growing up as something that can happen at any age.

All aboard: the comeback of the European night train

Twenty years ago, the night train seemed to be dying. Budget airlines had made it cheaper to fly from Paris to Rome than to sleep on a train, and one by one, the old sleeper services disappeared from European timetables. Today, the night train is back – and in some places, tickets sell out months in advance.

The revival began in 2016, when Austrian Railways took over several routes that German Railways had decided to close. Many experts thought the decision was a mistake. Instead, passenger numbers grew so quickly that the company ordered a new generation of trains, with private cabins that include their own shower and toilet.

The main reason for the change is climate. A journey by night train produces up to ten times less carbon dioxide than the same journey by plane. For a growing number of travellers, especially young people, this matters. "I used to fly to my grandmother's in Vienna three times a year," says Lena, a 23-year-old student from Brussels. "Now I take the night train. I fall asleep in Belgium and wake up in Austria. It feels like a small adventure every time."

There are practical advantages too. Night trains arrive in the city centre, not at an airport an hour away, and passengers save the cost of a hotel. There is no need to arrive two hours early for security checks, and you can bring as much luggage as you can carry.

The night train still has its problems, however. Tickets are often more expensive than flights, partly because airlines pay no tax on fuel. Delays are common, as trains must pass through several countries with different rail systems. And not everyone can sleep on a moving train.

Still, governments are beginning to listen. France has banned short domestic flights where a train journey of less than two and a half hours exists, and several countries have promised money for new sleeper routes. For travellers like Lena, the message is simple: "The journey is part of the holiday."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.When did night trains seem to be dying?
    Twenty years ago.
  2. 1.What made flying cheaper than night trains twenty years ago?
  3. 2.Which company started the revival of night trains?
  4. 3.What did experts think of the company's decision?
  5. 4.What do the new private cabins include?
  6. 5.What is the main reason for the return of the night train?
  7. 6.How often did Lena use to fly to Vienna?
  8. 7.Where do night trains arrive?
  9. 8.What do passengers save on besides travel time to the airport?
  10. 9.Why are flights often cheaper than night trains?
  11. 10.What has France banned?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Budget airlines.
2. Austrian Railways.
3. That it was a mistake.
4. A shower and a toilet.
5. Climate (change). / Lower CO₂ emissions.
6. Three times a year.
7. In the city centre.
8. (The cost of) a hotel.
9. Airlines pay no tax on fuel.
10. Short domestic flights (where a train takes under 2.5 hours).
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Budget airlines.
»Budget airlines had made it cheaper to fly …«. »What made flying cheaper« = kaj je poceni letenje omogočilo; nizkocenovni prevozniki.
2. Austrian Railways.
»Austrian Railways took over several routes«. »Which company« = katero podjetje; avstrijske železnice so prevzele proge.
3. That it was a mistake.
»Many experts thought the decision was a mistake«. »What did experts think« = mnenje; mislili so, da je odločitev napaka.
4. A shower and a toilet.
»with private cabins that include their own shower and toilet«. Kabine imajo lastno prho in stranišče; navedeš oboje.
5. Climate (change). / Lower CO₂ emissions.
»The main reason for the change is climate«. »Main reason« = glavni razlog; podnebje (manj izpustov CO₂).
6. Three times a year.
»three times a year«. »How often« = kako pogosto; trikrat na leto. »used to« pove, da tega ne počne več.
7. In the city centre.
»arrive in the city centre, not at an airport«. »Where« = kraj prihoda; v središču mesta, ne na letališču.
8. (The cost of) a hotel.
»passengers save the cost of a hotel«. »Besides« = poleg; prihranijo še stroške hotela.
9. Airlines pay no tax on fuel.
»partly because airlines pay no tax on fuel«. »Why« = razlog; letalske družbe ne plačujejo davka na gorivo.
10. Short domestic flights (where a train takes under 2.5 hours).
Prepoved kratkih notranjih letov, kjer obstaja vlak. »What has France banned« = prepoved kratkih notranjih letov tam, kjer obstaja vlak.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (C).

Why schools should teach students how to fail

Most of us are afraid of failure. At school, a bad mark can feel like a disaster, and many students would rather not try at all than risk getting something wrong. [0] Yet psychologists say that learning to deal with failure may be one of the most important skills a young person can have.

The idea is not new. [1] Thomas Edison is said to have tested thousands of materials before he found one that worked in his light bulb.

Some schools are now trying to put this idea into practice. [2] In one London school, pupils take part in a "failure week", during which teachers talk openly about their own mistakes.

The results have been surprising. [3] Students who had previously avoided difficult questions began to put their hands up more often.

Researchers explain this with the idea of a "growth mindset". [4] People who believe that intelligence is fixed tend to give up quickly, while those who believe it can grow see mistakes as information.

Not everyone is convinced, however. [5] Some critics argue that celebrating failure sends the wrong message and that students still need to know when work is not good enough.

Parents, too, play an important role. [6] Children who are always protected from disappointment may find it harder to cope when things go wrong later in life.

The key, experts say, is how adults react. [7] Praising effort and strategy, rather than talent, teaches children that they can improve.

Of course, failure is never pleasant. [8] But it is often the moment when real learning begins.

As one teacher puts it, "If my students never make mistakes, the work is too easy." [9] Perhaps, then, the most useful lesson a school can teach is how to get up again. [10]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AMany famous inventors failed many times before they succeeded.
  2. BIn the long run, this can be more harmful than helpful.
  3. CThis fear, they say, can stop us from learning.
  4. DThey believe that resilience can be taught like any other subject.
  5. EAccording to this theory, our attitude towards our abilities matters.
  6. FComments such as 'You're so clever' can actually do harm.
  7. GExam results at the school fell sharply.
  8. HTeachers reported that their classes became more willing to take risks.
  9. IThey worry that standards will fall.
  10. JNobody enjoys getting something wrong.
  11. KAnd that is exactly when they stop learning.
  12. LAfter all, life is full of second chances.
  13. MMost students prefer easy tasks.
naloge.rezultat:
1. A
2. D
3. H
4. E
5. I
6. B
7. F
8. J
9. K
10. L
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A
Ideja ni nova – izumitelji; sledi primer Edisona. Poved o izumiteljih pokaže, da ideja ni nova; naslednja poved da primer (Edison).
2. D
Šole poskušajo idejo uresničiti – odpornost (resilience) kot predmet; sledi primer šole. »They« = šole; verjamejo, da se odpornosti lahko učimo kot predmeta.
3. H
Presenetljivi rezultati – razredi bolj pripravljeni tvegati; sledi primer učencev. Rezultati: učitelji poročajo, da so razredi bolj pripravljeni tvegati.
4. E
Teorija »growth mindset«: odnos do lastnih sposobnosti; sledi razlaga. »this theory« se nanaša na prej omenjeno teorijo; naslednja poved jo razloži.
5. I
Ni vsak prepričan – skrb, da bodo standardi padli; sledi mnenje kritikov. »They« = kritiki; skrbi jih, da bodo standardi padli.
6. B
Vloga staršev: pretirana zaščita je dolgoročno škodljiva. »this« = pretirana zaščita staršev; dolgoročno bolj škodi kot koristi.
7. F
Odziv odraslih: pohvala »You're so clever« škodi; sledi: pohvali trud. Primer pohvale, ki škodi; naslednja poved svetuje hvaliti trud.
8. J
Neuspeh ni prijeten – nihče ne uživa v napakah; But … sledi. Kratka splošna resnica (nihče ne mara napak), nato »But« uvede nasprotje.
9. K
»If my students never make mistakes« – takrat se nehajo učiti. »that is exactly when« se navezuje na pogoj »if my students never make mistakes«.
10. L
Življenje je polno drugih priložnosti – sklep o vstajanju po padcu. »After all« uvede sklepno utemeljitev: življenje je polno drugih priložnosti.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Life on the rock: the last lighthouse keepers

For centuries, lighthouse keepers were among the loneliest workers in Britain. Their job was to make sure that the light never went out, (0) the weather was like.

Most lighthouses were staffed by three men, who worked in shifts of a month or more. During that time they could not leave the rock, and they depended (1) supply boats for food, water and news. In winter, storms sometimes made it impossible for the boats to land (2) weeks at a time.

The keepers had to be practical. (3) cleaning the lamp and winding the clockwork that turned it, they repaired engines, cooked, and kept a detailed record of the weather. Many of them also found ways to fight boredom. Some painted, some built model ships, and (4) learnt to play musical instruments.

Life on the rock could be dangerous as (5) as dull. In 1900, three keepers disappeared from a lighthouse on the Flannan Isles, off the west coast of Scotland. When a relief boat arrived, the lighthouse was empty, the clocks (6) stopped, and one of the keepers' coats was still hanging by the door. (7) really happened to the men remains a mystery. The most likely explanation is that they (8) swept into the sea by a huge wave.

The age of the lighthouse keeper came to an end in 1998, (9) the last lighthouse in Britain was automated. Today the lights are controlled by computers, and engineers visit only (10) or twice a year. Many of the keepers' cottages have been turned (11) holiday homes, and visitors often say they understand for the first time (12) the keepers felt, cut off from the rest of the world.

One former keeper, now in his eighties, still misses the life. "People think it was lonely," he says, "but I have never felt as free as I (13) out there. The sea teaches you patience. You can't hurry a storm – you just wait (14) it passes." He keeps his old logbook on the kitchen table, and its pages, (15) are full of notes on wind and waves, still smell of salt.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. whatever
naloge.rezultat:
1. on
2. for
3. Besides / Beyond
4. others
5. well
6. had
7. What
8. were
9. when
10. once
11. into
12. how
13. did
14. until / till
15. which
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. on
depend on. depend on = biti odvisen od.
2. for
for weeks at a time – trajanje. for + časovno obdobje: for weeks at a time.
3. Besides / Beyond
Poleg tega, da so čistili svetilko … (besides + -ing). Besides + -ing = poleg tega, da …
4. others
some …, some … and others. Naštevanje some … some … and others.
5. well
dangerous as well as dull – as well as = in tudi. as well as = in tudi.
6. had
Predpreteklik: ure so se ustavile že prej (had stopped). Ure so se ustavile prej kot drug pretekli dogodek: had stopped.
7. What
What really happened … – samostalniški odvisnik. What uvede samostalniški odvisnik (to, kar se je zgodilo).
8. were
Trpnik v pretekliku: were swept. Trpnik v pretekliku, osebek množina: were swept.
9. when
Časovni oziralni odvisnik za letnico. when za letnico (časovni oziralni odvisnik).
10. once
once or twice a year. once or twice a year = enkrat ali dvakrat na leto.
11. into
turn into – spremeniti v. turn into = spremeniti se v.
12. how
understand how they felt. Odvisno vprašanje: understand how they felt.
13. did
as free as I did (= felt) – pomožni glagol namesto ponovitve. Pomožni glagol did nadomesti felt: as free as I did.
14. until / till
wait until – dokler. wait until = čakati, dokler.
15. which
Nedoločni oziralni stavek med vejicama: its pages, which are … Med vejicama za stvar which.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The wrong suitcase

Last summer my sister and I (0) (FLY) to Lisbon for a week's holiday. When we (1) (ARRIVE) at the airport, we went straight to the baggage hall. Our flight (2) (DELAY) by three hours, so we were tired and hungry, and the hall was almost empty. My sister's suitcase (3) (ALREADY / GO) round the belt twice before she noticed it. She grabbed it and we (4) (TAKE) a taxi to the hotel.

It was only that evening, when she opened it, that she realised it (5) (NOT / BELONG) to her. Instead of her summer dresses, it (6) (CONTAIN) two men's suits, a pair of shoes and a book about birds. "Somebody (7) (MUST / TAKE) mine by mistake," she said. We called the airport, but the lost luggage office (8) (ALREADY / CLOSE) for the night.

The next morning a man rang the hotel. He (9) (LOOK) for his suitcase all night, he said, and he was flying home that afternoon. "If I (10) (NOT / FIND) it soon, I'll have to give my lecture in a T-shirt," he joked.

We met him in the hotel lobby an hour later. While the two of them (11) (EXCHANGE) suitcases, he told us he was an ornithologist. By the end of our conversation, he (12) (INVITE) us to join a birdwatching trip along the coast. My sister, who (13) (NEVER / BE) interested in birds before, said yes immediately.

Since then she (14) (JOIN) a birdwatching club, and next spring she (15) (TRAVEL) to Portugal again – this time with binoculars.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. flew
naloge.rezultat:
1. arrived
2. had been delayed
3. had already gone
4. took
5. didn't belong / did not belong
6. contained
7. must have taken
8. had already closed
9. had been looking
10. don't find / do not find
11. were exchanging
12. had invited
13. had never been
14. has joined
15. is travelling / is going to travel / will travel / will be travelling
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. arrived
Zaporedje dejanj v pripovedi: past simple. Zaporedje dejanj v preteklosti: arrived.
2. had been delayed
Trpnik v predpretekliku: zamuda je bila pred prihodom. Let je bil zamujen pred prihodom (trpnik): had been delayed.
3. had already gone
Predpreteklik z already: preden je opazila. already + past perfect: kovček je že odšel, preden je opazila.
4. took
Past simple v zaporedju dejanj. Naslednje dejanje v vrsti: took.
5. didn't belong / did not belong
belong je glagol stanja – ni -ing oblike. belong je glagol stanja, zato ni -ing; nikalni preteklik did not belong.
6. contained
Glagol stanja v pretekliku. contain je glagol stanja: contained.
7. must have taken
must have + 3. oblika: sklepanje o preteklosti. must have + 3. oblika = moral je vzeti (sklepanje).
8. had already closed
Predpreteklik: zaprli so pred klicem. Zaprli so pred njenim klicem: had already closed.
9. had been looking
Predpreteklik trajni: ves večer je iskal (poročani govor). Trajanje pred drugim preteklim trenutkom: had been looking.
10. don't find / do not find
Prvi pogojnik: if + present simple, … will. Prvi pogojnik: v if-stavku present simple, nikalno don't find.
11. were exchanging
While + past continuous: dejanje v teku. while + past continuous: dejanje v teku (were exchanging).
12. had invited
By the end of … + past perfect. By the end of + preteklost → past perfect: had invited.
13. had never been
Predpreteklik z never … before. never … before glede na pretekli trenutek: had never been.
14. has joined
Since then + present perfect. Since then + present perfect: has joined.
15. is travelling / is going to travel / will travel / will be travelling
Načrt za prihodnost. Načrt za prihodnost: present continuous ali going to / will.

naslov: Angleščina, osnovna raven, jesenski rok 2024, izpitna pola 2: slušno razumevanje (vadbena pola Učilnica.com)
navodilo: do 20 minut. Dva posnetka, vsakega poslušaš dvakrat, 17 točk.
vir: Vadbena pola Učilnica.com. Zgradba, vrsta nalog in točkovanje sledijo uradni poli splošne mature (jesenski rok 2024, osnovna raven, izpitna pola 2), besedila posnetkov, naloge in rešitve pa so naši. Uradne pole izdaja Državni izpitni center (RIC), ki ima nanje vse avtorske pravice. Besedila posnetkov so naša, prebere jih bralnik v brskalniku.

naloge.besedilo:
You are going to listen to an interview with Tom Hughes, a volunteer with a mountain rescue team in the Lake District. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Tom, how long have you been a mountain rescue volunteer?

Tom: Eighteen years now. I joined when I was twenty-four, after I twisted my ankle on a mountain myself and had to be carried down. I was so grateful that I decided I wanted to give something back.

Interviewer: Are all the team members volunteers?

Tom: Every one of them. We have about forty members – teachers, farmers, a dentist, two nurses. Nobody is paid, and we even raise most of the money for our equipment ourselves. A new vehicle costs around sixty thousand pounds, so we spend a lot of weekends shaking collection boxes.

Interviewer: What happens when someone calls for help?

Tom: They ring 999 and ask for the police, who then contact us. Our phones beep, and whoever is free drops what they are doing. I've left a birthday party, a wedding and once even a dentist's chair with my mouth still numb. Usually we're on our way within fifteen minutes.

Interviewer: What kind of people do you rescue?

Tom: All kinds. Many are walkers who are lost or injured, often because they started too late in the day. In summer we see a lot of people in trainers who are not prepared for the weather, which can change very quickly up there. Mobile phones have changed things a lot. People use them to call us, but they also rely on them for maps, and then the battery dies.

Interviewer: What was your most difficult rescue?

Tom: A climber who fell at night in a snowstorm. It took us nine hours to reach him and bring him down. We couldn't use the helicopter because of the wind. He survived, and every Christmas he sends us a card. That makes it all worthwhile.

Interviewer: Any advice for our listeners?

Tom: Tell someone where you're going and when you expect to be back. And carry a paper map. It never runs out of battery.

Mountain rescue volunteer

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Tom has been a volunteer for eighteen years. (T)
  2. 1.Tom joined the team after he had needed rescuing himself. T / F
  3. 2.Some members of the team are paid for their work. T / F
  4. 3.The team pays for most of its equipment through its own fundraising. T / F
  5. 4.People who need help call the rescue team directly. T / F
  6. 5.Tom once left a dentist's appointment to join a rescue. T / F
  7. 6.Many walkers get into trouble because they start their walk too early. T / F
  8. 7.The weather in the mountains can change quickly. T / F
  9. 8.A helicopter was used in Tom's most difficult rescue. T / F
  10. 9.Tom recommends taking a paper map. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. T
2. F
3. T
4. F
5. T
6. F
7. T
8. F
9. T
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
Zvil si je gleženj in so ga morali nesti v dolino. T: najprej so njega rešili (zvit gleženj), nato se je pridružil.
2. F
»Nobody is paid«. F: »Nobody is paid« – nihče ni plačan.
3. T
»we even raise most of the money for our equipment ourselves«. T: večino denarja za opremo zberejo sami.
4. F
Pokličejo 999 in policijo, ta obvesti ekipo. F: ljudje pokličejo 999, policija obvesti ekipo – ne neposredno.
5. T
»once even a dentist's chair«. T: enkrat je odšel celo z zobozdravniškega stola.
6. F
Prepozno: »because they started too late in the day«. F: težave imajo, ker začnejo prepozno, ne prezgodaj.
7. T
»the weather, which can change very quickly up there«. T: vreme se lahko zelo hitro spremeni.
8. F
»We couldn't use the helicopter because of the wind«. F: helikopterja zaradi vetra niso mogli uporabiti.
9. T
»carry a paper map. It never runs out of battery«. T: priporoča papirni zemljevid, ker se mu baterija ne izprazni.

naloge.besedilo:
You are going to listen to an interview with Dr Priya Shah, an ecologist who plants small forests in cities. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Shah, what exactly is a tiny forest?

Dr Shah: It's a very dense forest about the size of a tennis court. The method comes from a Japanese botanist, Akira Miyawaki, who developed it in the 1970s. Instead of planting a few trees far apart, you plant around six hundred young trees very close together – three per square metre.

Interviewer: Why so close?

Dr Shah: Because the trees compete for light, so they grow upwards very fast – about ten times faster than in a normal plantation. After three years the forest needs no more care at all. We also use only native species, at least thirty different ones, so the forest is similar to the one that would have grown there naturally.

Interviewer: What are the benefits in a city?

Dr Shah: Many. A tiny forest can be several degrees cooler than the street next to it on a hot day. It absorbs rainwater, reduces noise and attracts wildlife. In our first forest in Leeds, volunteers counted over five hundred species of insects and animals within two years.

Interviewer: Who does the planting?

Dr Shah: Local people, especially schoolchildren. A planting day usually takes a single morning. We think it's important that people feel the forest belongs to them, so each forest has a group of "tree keepers" from the neighbourhood who collect data and organise events.

Interviewer: Are there any critics?

Dr Shah: Yes. Some foresters say the method is expensive, and that not all the trees will survive in such crowded conditions. That's true – some will die. But that is exactly what happens in a natural forest too.

Tiny forests

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Who developed the method?
    Akira Miyawaki.
  2. 1.How big is a tiny forest?
  3. 2.How many trees are planted per square metre?
  4. 3.How much faster do the trees grow than in a normal plantation?
  5. 4.After how many years does the forest need no more care?
  6. 5.What kind of tree species are used?
  7. 6.How many species were counted in the Leeds forest?
  8. 7.What do the 'tree keepers' do?
  9. 8.What do some foresters criticise about the method?
naloge.rezultat:
1. About the size of a tennis court.
2. Three.
3. About ten times faster.
4. Three (years).
5. Native species (at least thirty).
6. Over five hundred.
7. Collect data and organise events.
8. It is expensive. / Not all trees survive.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. About the size of a tennis court.
»about the size of a tennis court«. »How big« = kako velik; odgovor je primerjava z znano velikostjo (teniško igrišče).
2. Three.
»three per square metre«. »Per square metre« = na kvadratni meter; odgovor je število: tri.
3. About ten times faster.
»about ten times faster«. »How much faster« zahteva primerjavo: približno desetkrat hitreje.
4. Three (years).
»After three years the forest needs no more care«. »After how many years« = po koliko letih; tri leta.
5. Native species (at least thirty).
»we also use only native species«. »What kind of« = katere vrste; samo domače (avtohtone) vrste.
6. Over five hundred.
»over five hundred species … within two years«. »How many species« = število vrst; več kot petsto v dveh letih.
7. Collect data and organise events.
»who collect data and organise events«. »What do … do« zahteva dejavnosti; zbirajo podatke in organizirajo dogodke (obe dejavnosti).
8. It is expensive. / Not all trees survive.
Dovolj je ena od obeh kritik. Gozdarji navedejo dve kritiki; zadošča ena (dražje ali ne preživijo vsa drevesa).

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

Two months ago you joined a fitness club in your town. The advertisement promised modern equipment, small groups and personal advice from a qualified trainer. Unfortunately, you are not satisfied with the club.

Write an e-mail of complaint of 120–150 words to the club's manager, in which you:

  • explain two problems you have had and give an example for each of them,
  • say what you expect the club to do.
TO: manager@fitclub.si
SUBJECT: Complaint
Dear Sir or Madam,
naloge.rezultat: Formalna pritožba z namenom, dvema težavama (vsaka s primerom, primerjava z obljubami oglasa) in jasnim pričakovanjem (popravilo, nadomestilo); 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. explain two problems you have had and give an example for each of them
  3. say what you expect the club to do
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba pritožbe
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor (ime ni znano).
I am writing to complain about the service at your fitness club, which I joined two months ago.
Namen v prvem stavku.
Firstly, although your advertisement promised small groups, there are often more than thirty people in my evening class, so the trainer cannot correct our exercises.
1. težava + primer; primerjava z oglasom.
Secondly, two of the running machines have been out of order for over three weeks, and nobody has repaired them.
2. težava + konkreten primer.
I would therefore expect you to repair the equipment as soon as possible and to offer me a month's free membership as compensation.
Pričakovanje – vljudno, a odločno.
I look forward to your prompt reply. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Formalni zaključek.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the service at your fitness club, which I joined two months ago.

Your advertisement promised modern equipment, but much of it is old or broken. For example, three of the five running machines have been out of order since I joined, so I often have to wait more than twenty minutes to use one.

The second problem is the lack of personal advice. I was promised help from a qualified trainer, yet I have only spoken to a trainer once. When I asked for a training plan, I was told that nobody had time.

I expect you to repair the equipment as soon as possible and to provide the personal advice I am paying for. Otherwise, I would like a refund for the last two months.

I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Jan Kos

Število besed: 146 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Travelling teaches us more than school does.
  2. Social media is changing friendship for the worse.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt
Uvod: stališče (I partly agree: travel teaches lessons that school cannot, but it cannot replace school).
Jasna teza že v uvodu.
Argument 1: travel teaches independence and problem-solving, e.g. finding your way in a foreign city without help.
Argument + konkreten primer.
Argument 2: meeting other cultures builds tolerance and improves language skills.
Povezovalci: Moreover, In addition.
Protiargument: school gives systematic knowledge and is available to everyone, while travel is expensive.
However, … – upoštevaj drugo stran.
Sklep: the two complement each other.
Sklep odgovori na naslov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: fewer face-to-face meetings, likes instead of real support. Against: easier to stay in touch with friends abroad.
Izberi en naslov.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Travelling teaches us more than school does.

Many people believe that a month abroad can teach us more than a year in the classroom. While I agree that travelling is a valuable way of learning, I do not think it can replace school.

On the one hand, travelling teaches things that are difficult to learn from books. When we have to ask for directions in a foreign language or try unfamiliar food, we become more independent and open-minded. During a school exchange in Spain, I learned more Spanish in two weeks than in a whole year of lessons, simply because I had to use it every day.

On the other hand, school gives us knowledge that travelling cannot. Mathematics, chemistry or the history of our own country require systematic study, explanations and practice. A tourist who visits Rome may admire the Colosseum, but without some knowledge of history it is just an old building.

Moreover, not everyone can afford to travel. If travelling were the main way of learning, education would become a privilege of the rich, which would be deeply unfair. School, in contrast, is free and open to every child, regardless of their family's income.

All things considered, I believe that travelling and school complement each other. School provides the foundation, while travelling brings that knowledge to life. The best education combines both.
