deli.A: A) PISNI SESTAVEK (V ENI OD STALNIH SPOROČANJSKIH OBLIK)

naloge.besedilo:
Report

Your school took part in an international survey on how secondary school students spend their free time. You were asked to collect the answers of students in your school and present the results.

Write a report of 120–150 words for the survey organisers, in which you:

  • present the most popular free-time activities in your school,
  • explain what surprised you in the results,
  • suggest how the school could help students use their free time better.
To: Survey Organisers
From: Ana Kovač
Subject: Free-time survey
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, uvodom z namenom in virom podatkov, tremi odstavki s podnaslovi (najbolj priljubljene dejavnosti s podatki, presenetljivi rezultati, predlogi šoli) in sklepom; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (120–150 words), formal style
  2. present the most popular free-time activities in your school
  3. explain what surprised you in the results
  4. suggest how the school could help students use their free time better
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Survey Organisers / From: Ana Kovač / Subject: Free-time survey at Gimnazija …
Glava namesto nagovora. Poročilo nima »Dear …« in »Yours sincerely«.
Introduction – The aim of this report is to present the results of the free-time survey carried out among 250 students at our school.
Prva poved pove namen in vir podatkov (koliko učencev je odgovarjalo).
Most popular activities
Over 70% of students spend at least two hours a day on social media, followed by sport (45%) and meeting friends (40%).
Iztočnica 1: konkretne številke in primerjave (followed by, the majority of).
Surprising results
Surprisingly, only 8% read books for pleasure, while more than half said they would like to join a club but did not know any.
Iztočnica 2: kaj je presenetilo + utemeljitev (Surprisingly, … / It was unexpected that …).
Recommendations
I would recommend opening the school library in the afternoon and organising a club fair at the start of the year.
Iztočnica 3: predlog z I would recommend + -ing / It would be a good idea to …
Conclusion – Overall, students would welcome more organised activities.
Kratek sklep brez novih podatkov.
Točke se podelijo za vsebino (vse tri iztočnice), zgradbo in obliko, besedišče in slovnico. Preštej besede: 120–150; glava in podnaslovi štejejo.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Survey Organisers
From: Ana Kovač, 3.A
Subject: Free-time survey at our school

Introduction

The aim of this report is to present the results of the free-time survey which was completed by 250 students at our school in March.

Most popular activities

Over 70% of students spend at least two hours a day on social media. Sport is the second most popular activity (45%), followed by meeting friends (40%).

Surprising results

Surprisingly, only 8% of students read books for pleasure. It was also unexpected that more than half of them would like to join a club but do not know which clubs exist.

Recommendations

I would recommend opening the school library in the afternoons. It would also be a good idea to organise a club fair at the beginning of the school year.

Conclusion

Overall, students would welcome more organised activities after lessons.

Ana Kovač

Število besed: 146 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Homework does more harm than good.
  2. Travelling teaches you more than school.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem v uvodu, dvema ali tremi argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej, v kolikšni meri se strinjaš (I partly agree that homework …).
Teza mora biti jasna že v uvodu; naslova ne prepisuj dobesedno.
Jedro 1: prvi argument + primer (homework causes stress and leaves little time for sleep and hobbies).
Temeljna poved + razlaga + konkreten primer iz izkušenj ali podatek.
Jedro 2: drugi argument + primer (homework that is too easy or too long teaches nothing).
Povezovalci: Furthermore, In addition, What is more.
Jedro 3: protiargument (Some argue that homework teaches discipline … However, …).
Protiargument z zavrnitvijo pokaže, da razmišljaš o obeh straneh.
Sklep: povzemi stališče (In conclusion, homework should be shorter and more meaningful rather than abolished).
Sklep odgovori na »How far do you agree?« in ne prinaša novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: languages, independence, meeting other cultures, problem solving. Against: not everyone can afford to travel, school gives systematic knowledge and qualifications.
Izberi le en naslov in ga podčrtaj. Formalen slog, brez skrajšanih oblik.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Homework does more harm than good.

Almost every student complains about homework, and some teachers have started to wonder whether it is really useful. I partly agree that homework does more harm than good, but I believe the problem is the amount, not the idea itself.

Firstly, too much homework causes stress. Many of my classmates spend three or four hours a day on assignments after seven lessons at school. As a result, they go to bed late, feel tired the next morning and have no time for sport or hobbies, which are also important for their health.

Secondly, a lot of homework is not meaningful. Copying exercises from a textbook or answering questions that were already discussed in class teaches very little. Students often copy answers from each other in the morning, so the teacher does not even find out who understands the topic.

On the other hand, some homework is necessary. Languages and mathematics need regular practice, and short tasks help students to remember what they have learned and to organise their time. Without any homework, many students would never open their books at home.

In conclusion, I believe that homework should not be abolished, but it should be shorter and more creative. Teachers in different subjects should also agree on the amount, so that students have time to rest. Only then will homework do more good than harm.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Night Porter

For thirty-one years, Walter Grimes worked the night shift at the Hotel Carlton, a grand old building on the seafront that had seen better days. He started at ten in the evening and finished at six in the morning, and in all that time he had missed only four nights: three for the births of his children and one, in 1987, because of a hurricane that had blown the hotel's front doors into the sea.

The night porter's job, Walter liked to say, was to be invisible until he was needed. Guests who came back late found the door open and a light on. Those who could not sleep found a pot of tea waiting in the lounge. Couples who had quarrelled found that Walter had quietly moved one of them to a spare room without asking a single question. Nobody ever thanked him for these things, and he did not expect them to. "If people notice you," he told every new receptionist, "you have done something wrong."

Over the years he collected what he called "the secrets of the night". He knew which businessmen ordered champagne when their wives were not with them, and which famous actor cried every time he stayed in Room 12. He never repeated any of it. His colleagues sometimes tried to make him talk, especially at Christmas parties, but Walter would only smile and change the subject to the weather.

The new owners arrived in the spring. They were young and energetic, and they had plans. The hotel was to become a "boutique experience", with a self-service check-in machine, keycards that opened rooms through a phone app, and a camera system that made a night porter unnecessary. Walter was offered early retirement and a generous cheque. He accepted both politely and went home.

It took three weeks for the problems to begin. The machine could not read foreign credit cards. The app failed during a storm, leaving forty guests locked out of their rooms at two in the morning. A wedding party, unable to find anyone to complain to, wrote such furious online reviews that bookings fell by a third.

In the end it was one of the new owners who knocked on Walter's door. She stood on the doorstep with a box of chocolates, looking embarrassed, and asked whether he might consider coming back, just for a few months, to train someone.

Walter thought about it for a long time. Then he put on his old uniform, which still fitted, and caught the last bus to the seafront. He is training his replacement now – a quiet young man who, Walter says, has a real talent for not being noticed.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.When did Walter's working day begin?
    At ten in the evening.
  2. 1.How many nights did Walter miss for family reasons?
  3. 2.What happened to the hotel's front doors in 1987?
  4. 3.What did Walter do for guests who could not sleep?
  5. 4.How did Walter deal with couples who had argued?
  6. 5.According to Walter, what does it mean if guests notice a porter?
  7. 6.What did Walter do when colleagues asked about guests' secrets?
  8. 7.What made a night porter unnecessary in the new owners' plan?
  9. 8.What was the result of the angry online reviews?
  10. 9.What does Walter think his replacement is good at?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Three.
2. They were blown into the sea.
3. He left them a pot of tea (in the lounge).
4. He moved one of them to another room.
5. He has done something wrong.
6. He changed the subject (to the weather).
7. A camera system (and self-service technology).
8. Bookings fell by a third.
9. Not being noticed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Three.
Trije izostanki so bili za rojstva otrok, četrti pa zaradi orkana. Vprašanje sprašuje le po družinskih razlogih.
2. They were blown into the sea.
»a hurricane that had blown the hotel's front doors into the sea« – odgovor lahko zapišeš v trpniku.
3. He left them a pot of tea (in the lounge).
»Those who could not sleep found a pot of tea waiting in the lounge.«
4. He moved one of them to another room.
»quietly moved one of them to a spare room without asking a single question«.
5. He has done something wrong.
Walterjevo pravilo: »If people notice you, you have done something wrong.«
6. He changed the subject (to the weather).
Ni ničesar izdal, le nasmehnil se je in govoril o vremenu.
7. A camera system (and self-service technology).
Novi lastniki so uvedli samopostrežni sprejem, aplikacijo in kamere; neposredno: »a camera system that made a night porter unnecessary«.
8. Bookings fell by a third.
Posledica: »bookings fell by a third«.
9. Not being noticed.
Konec besedila se vrne k Walterjevemu pravilu: »a real talent for not being noticed«.

Read the text and match the statements with the paragraphs. More than one statement may refer to the same paragraph. There is an example at the beginning: Example 0.

Five museums you never knew you needed

Forget dinosaurs and paintings. These small museums celebrate the strange, the ordinary and the forgotten.

A The Museum of Broken Relationships, Zagreb

Started by two artists after their own break-up, this museum displays objects donated by people from all over the world, each with a short story about a relationship that ended. There is an axe that a woman used to destroy her ex-partner's furniture, a wedding dress kept in a jar, and a garden gnome thrown at a car. Visitors often arrive laughing and leave in tears. The museum has toured more than fifty cities, and every new location adds objects from local people, so the collection keeps growing.

B The Pencil Museum, Keswick

In the sixteenth century, shepherds in the English Lake District discovered a strange black substance in the hills, which turned out to be graphite. This small museum tells the story of the local pencil industry, which lasted for almost four hundred years. Its most famous object is a pencil eight metres long, once the largest in the world. Children can try drawing workshops, and there is a secret wartime pencil with a map hidden inside, made for British pilots who might be captured. Sadly, the factory itself closed in 2008.

C The Museum of Bad Art, Boston

Founded in a basement in 1994, this museum is dedicated to art that is "too bad to be ignored". Its first painting was found in a pile of rubbish. The curators receive hundreds of offers every year but accept very few, because a picture must be sincere: the artist must have tried hard and failed in an interesting way. Deliberately bad art is rejected. The museum charges no entry fee, and its guided tours are famous for the serious, academic language the guides use to describe the most terrible portraits.

D The Dog Collar Museum, Leeds Castle

Housed in the gatehouse of a medieval castle in Kent, this collection includes more than a hundred collars from the last five centuries. Some of the oldest were made of iron with sharp spikes to protect hunting dogs from wolves and bears. Later examples, made of silver and velvet, show how dogs became fashionable pets for the rich. The collection was given to the castle by a widow in memory of her husband, a historian of dogs, and entry is included in the castle ticket.

E The Museum of Lost Sounds, online

This museum has no building at all. It is a website that preserves the sounds of disappearing machines and places: a dial-up modem, a typewriter, a cassette being rewound, the ticket machines of old railway stations. Visitors can listen to more than three hundred recordings and are invited to send their own. Its founder, a sound engineer, says that people often write to tell him that a single recording brought back childhood memories they had completely forgotten. Teachers use the site to show pupils how the world sounded before smartphones.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Which museum does not have a physical location? (E)
  2. 1.Which museum mentions an object designed to help people escape?
  3. 2.Which museum is free to visit?
  4. 3.Which museum became possible thanks to a gift from one person?
  5. 4.Which museum has been shown in many different places?
  6. 5.Which museum's founder hears from visitors about personal memories?
  7. 6.Which museum describes how attitudes to animals changed over time?
  8. 7.Which museum's collection got its start from something thrown away?
  9. 8.Which museum says that visitors' feelings change during their visit?
  10. 9.Which museum connects its collection to a local industry that no longer exists?
  11. 10.Which museum has strict rules about what it accepts?
  12. 11.Which museum is used for educational purposes in schools?

1. B
2. C
3. D
4. A
5. E
6. D
7. C
8. A
9. B
10. C
11. E
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. B
Vojni svinčnik s skrito karto je bil za pilote, »who might be captured« – pomagal naj bi jim pri pobegu.
2. C
»The museum charges no entry fee« (C). Pri D je vstop vključen v vstopnico za grad, torej ni brezplačen.
3. D
Zbirko je gradu podarila vdova v spomin na moža.
4. A
»The museum has toured more than fifty cities« – razstava potuje po svetu.
5. E
»people often write to tell him that a single recording brought back childhood memories«.
6. D
Ovratnice od železnih za lov do srebrnih in žametnih kažejo, kako so psi postali modni ljubljenčki.
7. C
»Its first painting was found in a pile of rubbish.«
8. A
»Visitors often arrive laughing and leave in tears.«
9. B
Muzej pripoveduje o lokalni industriji svinčnikov; »the factory itself closed in 2008«.
10. C
Slika mora biti »sincere«, namerno slaba umetnost je zavrnjena; sprejmejo zelo malo ponudb.
11. E
»Teachers use the site to show pupils how the world sounded before smartphones.« Delavnice v B so za otroke, ne za šole.

Teenagers and sleep: why your body clock is not lazy

Every parent of a teenager knows the scene: it is eleven at night, the house is quiet, and the teenager is wide awake. Next morning, (0) the alarm rings, the same teenager can hardly open their eyes. For years this was blamed on laziness or late-night screens. Scientists now believe the real cause lies much deeper.

During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts by up to two hours. The brain starts releasing melatonin, the hormone that makes (1) feel sleepy, later in the evening (2) it does in children or adults. As a result, most teenagers find it difficult to fall asleep (3) eleven o'clock, no matter how tired they are.

At the same time, teenagers still need between eight and ten hours of sleep a night. If school starts at eight, the numbers simply do not add (4). Surveys show that the majority of secondary school students sleep less than seven hours on school nights, (5) means that many of them are permanently tired.

The consequences are serious. Lack of sleep affects memory, concentration and mood. It has also (6) linked to a higher risk of depression, weight gain and road accidents among young drivers. "Asking a teenager to learn maths at eight in the morning," says one researcher, "is a bit (7) asking an adult to do it at five."

Some schools have decided to act. In the United States, the state of California passed a law in 2019 (8) requires most secondary schools to start no earlier than half past eight. Early results are encouraging: students arrive (9) time more often, attendance has improved and some schools report better exam results.

Not everyone is convinced, (10). Parents worry about how they will get to work if they have to take their children to school later, and sports coaches complain that training will have to finish after dark. Others argue that teenagers would simply use the extra time to stay (11) even later.

Scientists reply that good habits still matter. Switching off phones an hour (12) bed, avoiding coffee in the afternoon and getting plenty of daylight in the morning can all help to reset the body clock. But they insist that the biological shift is real (13) cannot be fixed by willpower alone.

So the next time a teenager refuses to get out of bed, it might be worth remembering that they are not necessarily being difficult. Their body is (14) doing what nature designed it to do – just at a time that does not suit the school timetable (15) the rest of the family.

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. us / you / people
Predmetni zaimek za glagolom »make« (make us feel sleepy); sprejemljiv je tudi splošni samostalnik people.
2. than
Primerjava »later … than it does in children« – za primernikom stoji than.
3. before
»find it difficult to fall asleep before eleven« = pred enajsto. Until bi zahteval drugačen pomen glagola.
4. up
Frazni glagol »add up« = se ujemati, imeti smisel (številke se ne seštejejo).
5. which
Nedoločilni oziralni stavek, ki se nanaša na vso prejšnjo trditev (… seven hours, which means …); that tu ni mogoč.
6. been
Present perfect v trpniku: It has also been linked to …
7. like
Primerjava »is a bit like asking …« = je nekoliko podobno, kot če bi …
8. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za stvar (a law) v vlogi osebka.
9. on
Stalna zveza »on time« = pravočasno, točno.
10. though / however
Na koncu povedi za vejico: »Not everyone is convinced, though.« = Vendar niso vsi prepričani.
11. up
Frazni glagol »stay up« = ostati pokonci, ne iti spat.
12. before
»an hour before bed« = uro pred spanjem.
13. and
Veznik povezuje dve trditvi o istem osebku: is real and cannot be fixed.
14. simply / just / only
Prislov poudari, da telo le dela, kar mu je narava namenila.
15. or
V nikalni povedi (does not suit) se dva predmeta povežeta z or: the school timetable or the rest of the family.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The summer London could not breathe

In the summer of 1858, London (0) (EXPERIENCE) one of the strangest disasters in its history. It was not a fire or a flood, but a smell.

For centuries, the city (1) (USE) the River Thames as its main drain. By the 1850s, more than two million people (2) (LIVE) in London, and the waste of every household, factory and slaughterhouse ended up in the river. The same water (3) (PUMP) back into many homes for drinking.

That summer was unusually hot. As temperatures (4) (RISE), the river began to boil with bacteria, and a terrible smell spread across the city. Newspapers called it "the Great Stink". People who (5) (CAN) afford it left for the countryside, and those who stayed held handkerchiefs to their faces.

The smell was worst at the Houses of Parliament, which (6) (STAND) right on the riverbank. Workers (7) (SOAK) the curtains in chemicals in an attempt to protect the politicians, but it was no use. Some members of Parliament even suggested that the government (8) (MOVE) to Oxford.

For years, engineers (9) (WARN) that London needed a modern sewer system, but nobody had wanted to pay for it. Now, with the stink entering their own offices, politicians changed their minds remarkably quickly. Within eighteen days, a law (10) (PASS), and an engineer called Joseph Bazalgette was given the job.

Bazalgette's plan was enormous. Over the next sixteen years, his workers (11) (BUILD) more than 1,800 kilometres of sewers, which carried the waste far away from the centre. Being a careful man, he made the pipes much wider than necessary. "We (12) (ONLY / DO) this once," he is reported to have said, "and there is always the unforeseen."

His caution proved wise. London's population has grown to almost nine million, yet his tunnels are still in use today. Without them, historians say, the city (13) (SUFFER) many more outbreaks of cholera in the following decades.

Today, a new "super sewer" (14) (CONSTRUCT) under the Thames to deal with the needs of the twenty-first century. If Bazalgette could see it, he (15) (PROBABLY / APPROVE).

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. experienced
naloge.rezultat:
1. had used / had been using
2. lived / were living
3. was pumped
4. rose
5. could
6. stood / stands
7. soaked
8. (should) move / moved
9. had been warning / had warned
10. was passed / had been passed
11. built
12. are only going to do / will only do
13. would have suffered
14. is being constructed
15. would probably approve
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. had used / had been using
»For centuries« do točke v preteklosti (by the 1850s): past perfect ali past perfect continuous.
2. lived / were living
Stanje v preteklosti ob določenem času (By the 1850s): past simple; sprejemljiv tudi past continuous.
3. was pumped
Vode niso črpali sami od sebe: trpnik v preteklosti, ednina (The same water).
4. rose
Zaključeno dogajanje v preteklosti: nepravilni glagol rise – rose – risen.
5. could
Preteklik modalnega glagola can je could.
6. stood / stands
Stavba stoji na bregu še danes, zato je mogoč tudi present simple; v pripovedi v pretekliku je običajen stood.
7. soaked
Zaključeno dejanje v preteklosti: past simple.
8. (should) move / moved
Za »suggest that« stoji subjunktiv (move) ali should + nedoločnik; sprejemljiv je tudi preteklik moved.
9. had been warning / had warned
»For years« do trenutka v preteklosti, ko so politiki spremenili mnenje: past perfect (continuous).
10. was passed / had been passed
Zakona ni sprejel sam od sebe: trpnik (was passed).
11. built
Zaključeno obdobje v preteklosti (Over the next sixteen years): past simple.
12. are only going to do / will only do
Bazalgette govori o prihodnosti (gradili bodo samo enkrat): going to ali will.
13. would have suffered
Tretji pogojnik: hipotetična preteklost (Without them …) → would have + pretekli deležnik.
14. is being constructed
Dejanje poteka zdaj, gradijo ga drugi: present continuous v trpniku.
15. would probably approve
Drugi pogojnik (If Bazalgette could see it, …): would + nedoločnik; prislov probably stoji za would.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Hannah Price, a vet who treats injured wild animals. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Hannah, most vets look after cats and dogs. Why did you choose wild animals?

Hannah: I grew up on a farm in Wales, so I was surrounded by animals from the start. But the moment I remember best is finding a barn owl with a broken wing when I was nine. The local vet said there was nothing he could do, and I spent the whole summer feeding it with my father. It never flew again, but I decided then that somebody should know how to help animals like that.

Interviewer: How did you train?

Hannah: The normal way – five years at veterinary school in Bristol. Wildlife medicine was only a tiny part of the course, so I spent every holiday volunteering at rescue centres. After I qualified, I worked in a small-animal practice for four years, mostly to pay back my student loan.

Interviewer: And now you run your own hospital.

Hannah: Yes, a small one, on the edge of a nature reserve. We treat around three thousand animals a year: hedgehogs, foxes, swans, bats, even the odd seal. Hedgehogs are the most common patients. Many of them are hurt by garden machines, especially by the robot lawnmowers that work at night.

Interviewer: What is the biggest difference between treating a pet and a wild animal?

Hannah: Stress. A dog knows people and trusts them. For a wild animal, a human is a predator, so simply being held can kill it. We keep the lights low, we speak very quietly, and we try to touch them as little as possible. Sometimes the best medicine is a dark box and silence.

Interviewer: Do you get attached to them?

Hannah: You have to be careful. Our aim is always to release them, so we never give them names. If an animal becomes too used to people, it won't survive outside. The volunteers find that hard – they want to cuddle the baby foxes!

Interviewer: Who pays for all this?

Hannah: Mostly the public. We receive no money from the government, so we depend on donations and on a charity shop in town. Our biggest single cost is not medicine, as people expect, but food. A recovering seal eats several kilograms of fish a day.

Interviewer: What advice would you give to young people who want to do your job?

Hannah: Get experience before you apply, because veterinary schools want to see that you understand what the work is really like. And learn to deal with loss. Not every animal can be saved, and you mustn't let the sad days stop you from coming back the next morning.

An interview with a wildlife vet

  9. 8.Apart from donations, where does the hospital's money come from?
  10. 9.What should young people get before they apply to veterinary school?

  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Marcus Bell, who directs a theatre company for young people. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Marcus, you started acting very young, didn't you?

Marcus: At seven. My grandmother took me to a pantomime in Manchester, and in the second half the actors asked for a child to come on stage. I put my hand up before she could stop me. I forgot my one line, the audience laughed, and I loved every second of it.

Interviewer: But you didn't go to drama school.

Marcus: No. My parents thought acting was not a proper job, so I studied engineering. I was quite good at it, actually. But every evening I was at a small theatre above a pub, painting scenery and selling tickets. When the director fell ill one season, they asked me to take over a play, and I never went back to engineering.

Interviewer: Did your engineering help?

Marcus: Enormously. Theatre is full of practical problems: how to change a whole set in thirty seconds, how to make a ghost appear. Engineers are trained to solve problems step by step, and that's exactly what a director does in rehearsals.

Interviewer: Tell us about your company.

Marcus: We work with teenagers who have never been to a theatre. Every year we choose about forty of them from schools in the poorest parts of the city. They write the play themselves, based on their own lives, and in July we perform it for one week. Last year's play was about a family who lose their flat, and it was so powerful that a television channel filmed it.

Interviewer: What changes do you see in the young people?

Marcus: Confidence, above all. Many of them arrive unable to look an adult in the eye. By the end, they can stand in front of five hundred people. Teachers tell us that their marks often improve too, because they've learned to concentrate and to work in a team.

Interviewer: What is the hardest part of your job?

Marcus: Saying no. We get about three hundred applications for forty places, and choosing is painful. We try to keep in touch with everyone who isn't selected and invite them to free workshops instead.

Interviewer: What's next for you?

Marcus: We're taking our next production to a festival in Edinburgh. For most of the cast, it will be the first time they've ever left Manchester, so I think the train journey will be just as exciting as the performance.

An interview with a theatre director

  5. 4.In the evenings, he painted scenery and ____ at a small theatre.
  6. 5.Engineering taught him to solve problems ____.
  7. 6.Every year, the company chooses about ____ teenagers.
  8. 7.Last year's play was about a family who ____.
  9. 8.The young people's biggest change is in their ____.
  10. 9.For most of the cast, the trip to Edinburgh will be the first time they have ____.

naloge.besedilo:
Article

The international youth magazine Generation Next is inviting secondary school students to write articles for a special issue on equality.

Write an article of about 150–180 words with ONE of the following headings:
"Equal opportunities start at school" or "Gender equality is still a dream".

In your article:

  • explain what the heading means to you,
  • give examples from your own country or experience,
  • suggest what young people can do to change the situation.
naloge.rezultat: Članek z izbranim naslovom, pritegnitvenim uvodom, tremi odstavki (pomen naslova, primeri iz Slovenije ali izkušenj, predlogi za mlade) in sklepom z nagovorom bralcev; 150–180 besed, polformalni slog.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Article (150–180 words), semi-formal style, with a title
  2. explain what the heading means to you
  3. give examples from your own country or experience
  4. suggest what young people can do to change the situation
Kako napišeš članek (article)
Članek (article): zgradba
  • Naslov: kratek in zanimiv; če navodilo ponuja naslove (headings), izberi enega in ga prepiši natančno.
  • Uvod: pritegni bralca (vprašanje, presenetljiv podatek, kratka zgodba) in v eni povedi povej, o čem bo članek.
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku; vsak odstavek začni s temeljno povedjo in jo podpri s primerom ali podatkom.
  • Sklep: povzemi svoje stališče ali nagovori bralce (So next time you …, why not …?). Nagovora »Dear …« in pozdrava ni.
Slog članka
  • Članek je namenjen širši javnosti (bralcem revije, šolskega časopisa, spletne strani), zato je slog polformalen: živahen, a ne pogovoren.
  • Uporabi retorična vprašanja (Have you ever wondered …?), neposreden nagovor bralca (you) in konkretne primere iz izkušenj.
  • Pri članku z mnenjem (opinion article) jasno povej svoje stališče in ga utemelji, upoštevaj tudi nasprotno mnenje.
  • Tudi v polformalnem slogu se izogibaj slengu (gonna, stuff, super cool) in pretiranim klicajem.
Uporabne zveze
  • Have you ever thought about …? · Imagine a school where … · According to a recent survey, …
  • On the one hand, … On the other hand, … · What is more, … · Not only … but also …
  • All in all, … · It is high time we … · The choice is yours.
Pogoste napake
  • Članek napisan kot pismo (Dear readers, … Yours sincerely).
  • Manjka naslov ali je naslov drugačen od ponujenega.
  • Iztočnice so le naštete, niso razvite s primeri in razlogi.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba članka
Naslov: prepiši izbrani naslov natančno (Equal opportunities start at school).
Članek ima naslov, nima pa nagovora »Dear …« in pozdrava.
Uvod – vprašanje ali presenetljiv podatek, ki pritegne bralca (Did you know that a child's postcode can predict their exam results?).
Uvod pove, o čem bo članek, in pritegne pozornost.
Odstavek 1: kaj naslov pomeni
Equal opportunities mean that every pupil, rich or poor, has the same chance to develop their talents.
Iztočnica 1: lastna razlaga pojma.
Odstavek 2: primeri
In Slovenia schooling is free, but private lessons, expensive equipment and school trips are not, so some pupils are left behind.
Iztočnica 2: konkretni primeri iz države ali izkušenj.
Odstavek 3: kaj lahko naredimo
Students can organise tutoring for younger pupils, share textbooks and make sure nobody is excluded because of money.
Iztočnica 3: predlogi z can / could / why not …?
Sklep – nagovor bralcev (It is up to us to make equality more than a slogan.).
Polformalni slog: živahen, a brez slenga in skrajšanih oblik v uradnem tonu.
Na višji ravni ocenjevalci pričakujejo pestro besedišče (disadvantaged, access to, bridge the gap) in zahtevnejše strukture (Not only … but also, inverzija).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Equal opportunities start at school

Did you know that a child's postcode can predict their exam results better than their intelligence? This should make us think about what equal opportunities really mean.

To me, the heading means that every pupil, whether rich or poor, should have the same chance to develop their talents. School is the first place where society can either close the gap between children or make it wider.

In Slovenia, education is free, which is a great advantage. However, private lessons, expensive calculators and school trips abroad are not. I have seen classmates stay at home while the rest of us went to London, simply because their families could not afford it.

Young people can do a lot to change this. Older students can offer free tutoring to younger ones, schools can organise second-hand book fairs, and student councils can raise money so that nobody misses a trip.

Equality will not happen by itself. It is up to us to turn it from a slogan into reality.

Število besed: 170 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the role of fear in William Golding's Lord of the Flies.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – fear is the force that destroys the boys' society; the beast they fear is not on the island but inside them.
Teza že v uvodu. Ne piši o Goldingu na splošno in ne obnavljaj zgodbe.
Jedro 1 – the littluns' fear of the 'beastie': at first the older boys laugh, but the fear spreads at assemblies and Ralph cannot control it.
Konkreten prizor: the boy with the mulberry-coloured birthmark, the assemblies with the conch.
Jedro 2 – Jack uses fear to gain power: he promises to hunt the beast, offers protection and leaves the pig's head as a gift.
Pokaži, kako strah postane orodje vodje (manipulation).
Jedro 3 – the Lord of the Flies and Simon: the beast speaks of being 'part of you'; Simon's discovery of the dead parachutist is ignored and he is killed in the frenzy.
Vrhunec teme: strah uniči tistega, ki pozna resnico.
Sklep: fear turns civilised boys into savages; the naval officer at the end cannot see that the same fear rules the adult world at war.
Sklep se vrne k tezi in jo razširi.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed. Vsako trditev podpri s prizorom ali kratkim citatom.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The role of fear in Lord of the Flies

In William Golding's Lord of the Flies, a group of schoolboys stranded on an island slowly turn from polite English children into violent savages. I believe that fear is the main force that destroys their society. The novel suggests that the beast the boys are afraid of is not hiding in the jungle but inside them.

Fear appears very early in the novel. At one of the first assemblies, a small boy with a birthmark speaks about a "beastie" that he saw in the dark. The older boys laugh, and Ralph insists that there is no beast. However, the fear does not disappear. It grows at night, spreads among the littluns and makes the meetings with the conch increasingly chaotic.

Jack is the first to understand that fear can be used. He promises to hunt and kill the beast and offers the boys protection and meat. In return, they give up the rules that Ralph and Piggy represent. When Jack leaves a pig's head on a stick as a gift for the beast, he turns fear into a kind of religion that keeps him in power.

The most important scene is Simon's conversation with the Lord of the Flies. The head tells him that the beast is "part of you". Simon is the only boy who discovers the truth, that the "beast" on the mountain is a dead parachutist. Ironically, when he runs to tell the others, they mistake him for the beast and kill him in a frenzy of fear.

In conclusion, fear destroys the boys' ability to think rationally and allows violence to take over. Even the naval officer who rescues them comes from a world at war, which shows that the same fear rules adult society as well.

Število besed: 300 (zahtevanih 250–300). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naslov: Angleščina, osnovna raven, jesenski rok 2023, izpitna pola 1: bralno razumevanje ter poznavanje in raba jezika (vadbena pola Učilnica.com)
navodilo: 60 minut (35 + 25). 2 nalogi v delu A in 2 v delu B, 50 točk, vsaka pravilna rešitev je vredna 1 točko.
vir: Vadbena pola Učilnica.com. Zgradba, vrsta nalog in točkovanje sledijo uradni poli splošne mature (jesenski rok 2023, osnovna raven, izpitna pola 1), besedila, naloge in rešitve pa so naši. Uradne pole izdaja Državni izpitni center (RIC), ki ima nanje vse avtorske pravice.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Night the Lights Went Out

It happened on the coldest night of the year, three days before Christmas. At exactly half past seven, just as my mother was taking the roast potatoes out of the oven, every light in our street went out at once. The television died in the middle of the news, the fridge stopped humming, and for a moment the whole house was completely silent.

My little brother Tom, who was six, thought it was the most exciting thing that had ever happened. He ran around the kitchen shouting that the aliens had arrived. My father, who was less excited, went to look for the torch that we kept in the drawer under the sink. Of course, its batteries were flat.

We found six candles in the end: two red Christmas candles, three birthday candles and a large white one that smelled of vanilla. My mother put them on the kitchen table, and we ate our dinner in their strange, warm light. Without the television, we actually talked to each other. My father told us about the winter of 1987, when the snow had been so deep that he had climbed out of his bedroom window to get to school.

At about nine o'clock someone knocked on the door. It was Mrs Patel from number twelve, an elderly widow whom we hardly knew. Her heating was electric, she explained, and her house was getting colder by the minute. My mother invited her in immediately and gave her the best chair, closest to the gas fire.

Soon other neighbours arrived. The Wilsons brought a guitar, the students from number nine brought a box of biscuits, and old Mr Grant came with a flask of hot chocolate and a board game that nobody had played for thirty years. By ten o'clock there were fourteen people in our kitchen, singing songs and arguing about the rules of the game.

The electricity came back just after midnight. The lights flickered, the fridge started humming again, and the television suddenly began shouting the late news into the room. Everyone groaned. For a moment nobody moved, and then, slowly, people began to collect their coats.

We still talk about that night. Mrs Patel comes for dinner every Sunday now, and the Wilsons have organised a street party every December since then. Tom, who is twelve now, says it was the best Christmas ever, even though the aliens never came.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.When did the power cut happen?
    Three days before Christmas. / On the coldest night of the year.
  2. 1.What was the narrator's mother doing when the lights went out?
  3. 2.What did Tom think had caused the power cut?
  4. 3.Why was the torch useless?
  5. 4.How many candles did the family find?
  6. 5.What changed because there was no television?
  7. 6.How did the father get to school in the winter of 1987?
  8. 7.Why did Mrs Patel come to the narrator's house?
  9. 8.Where did Mrs Patel sit?
  10. 9.What did Mr Grant bring apart from a drink?
  11. 10.How did people react when the television came back on?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Taking (the) potatoes out of the oven.
2. Aliens.
3. Its batteries were flat.
4. Six.
5. They talked to each other.
6. He climbed out of his bedroom window.
7. Her house was getting cold. / Her heating was electric.
8. In the best chair (closest to the gas fire).
9. A board game.
10. They groaned.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Taking (the) potatoes out of the oven.
»just as my mother was taking the roast potatoes out of the oven« – dejanje, ki je potekalo v trenutku izpada elektrike.
2. Aliens.
»shouting that the aliens had arrived« – otroška razlaga, ne pravi vzrok.
3. Its batteries were flat.
»Of course, its batteries were flat.« Odgovor mora navesti razlog, ne le, da ni delovala.
4. Six.
Šest sveč: dve rdeči, tri rojstnodnevne in ena bela.
5. They talked to each other.
»Without the television, we actually talked to each other.«
6. He climbed out of his bedroom window.
Sneg je bil tako visok, da je skozi okno spalnice zlezel ven.
7. Her house was getting cold. / Her heating was electric.
Brez elektrike ni imela ogrevanja: »her house was getting colder by the minute«.
8. In the best chair (closest to the gas fire).
»gave her the best chair, closest to the gas fire«.
9. A board game.
Prinesel je termovko s kakavom in družabno igro; vprašanje izključi pijačo.
10. They groaned.
»Everyone groaned.« – niso se razveselili, ker je bilo konec skupnega večera.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and match the statements with the paragraphs. More than one statement may refer to the same paragraph. There is an example at the beginning: Example 0.

My first summer job

Five young people describe the jobs that taught them the most.

A Lucy, 19: ice-cream seller

I worked on a beach in Devon, selling ice cream from a small van. It sounds like fun, and on sunny days it was, but when it rained nobody came and I sat alone for hours. My boss paid me a percentage of what I sold, so a wet week meant almost no money. I learned to talk to every customer, because people who chatted usually bought a second ice cream. I still use that skill now that I'm studying marketing.

B Jamal, 18: hotel kitchen porter

My job was washing pots in the kitchen of a big hotel. I worked from six in the evening until two in the morning, and the kitchen was so hot that I drank five litres of water a night. The chefs shouted all the time, but never at me personally – it was just the way the kitchen worked. By the end of the summer, the head chef let me prepare vegetables, and he offered me a job for next year. I said no. I want to be an architect.

C Sophie, 17: farm worker

I picked strawberries on a farm near my village, together with workers from five different countries. At first I was the slowest picker on the farm, and my back hurt so much that I nearly gave up after two days. A woman from Romania showed me how to work without bending, and we became good friends. We still write to each other. I was paid for every kilo I picked, and in the last week I earned more than in the first three put together.

D Ben, 20: museum guide

I showed tourists around a castle in Scotland. I had to learn the history by heart in two weeks, and the first time I gave a tour in front of forty people my voice was shaking. The worst part was the questions I could not answer. I started writing them down and looking for the answers in the evening, and by August I knew more about the castle than my manager. The pay was low, but visitors often gave me tips.

E Mia, 18: children's camp leader

I looked after a group of ten-year-olds at a summer camp. It was the hardest work I have ever done, because you are responsible for the children twenty-four hours a day. One boy was so homesick that he cried every night for a week, and I spent hours talking to him. On the last day he gave me a drawing of the two of us, which I keep on my wall. The job convinced me to become a primary school teacher.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Who often worked alone? (A)
  2. 1.Who earned less because of the weather?
  3. 2.Who refused an offer of future work?
  4. 3.Who made a lasting friendship at work?
  5. 4.Who did extra research in their free time?
  6. 5.Whose job influenced their choice of career?
  7. 6.Who was paid according to the amount of work done?
  8. 7.Who was nervous when speaking in public?
  9. 8.Who says that people's behaviour was not meant personally?
  10. 9.Who received a personal gift at the end of the job?
  11. 10.Who improved their results greatly by the end of the summer?
naloge.rezultat:
1. A
2. B
3. C
4. D
5. E
6. C
7. D
8. B
9. E
10. C
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A
Ob dežju ni bilo kupcev, plačilo pa je bilo odvisno od prodaje: »a wet week meant almost no money«.
2. B
Glavni kuhar mu je ponudil službo za naslednje leto: »I said no.«
3. C
Z Romunko sta postali prijateljici in si še vedno pišeta.
4. D
Vprašanja, na katera ni znal odgovoriti, je zvečer raziskal.
5. E
»The job convinced me to become a primary school teacher.« Pri A spretnost uporablja, a službe ni izbrala zaradi nje; B poklica ne spremeni.
6. C
Plačana je bila po kilogramih: »I was paid for every kilo I picked«. Pri A je šlo za odstotek prodaje, ne količino dela.
7. D
Pri prvem vodenju pred štiridesetimi ljudmi se mu je tresel glas.
8. B
Kuharji so kričali, »but never at me personally – it was just the way the kitchen worked«.
9. E
Fant ji je zadnji dan dal risbo.
10. C
V zadnjem tednu je zaslužila več kot v prvih treh skupaj, ker se je naučila delati hitreje.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The city that said goodbye to cars

Twenty years ago, the main square of Pontevedra, a small city in north-west Spain, was a car park. Today children play football there, older people sit on benches in the sun, and the only sound is the noise of conversations. The change began in 1999, (0) the new mayor decided to close the city centre to private cars.

At first, the idea was extremely unpopular. Shop owners were afraid (1) they would lose customers, and drivers complained that they would have nowhere to park. The mayor, a doctor by profession, did not give (2). He believed that a city should belong to people, not to machines.

The changes were introduced step (3) step. First, the streets in the historic centre were closed to traffic. Then pavements were widened, traffic lights were removed and speed limits (4) the rest of the city were reduced to thirty kilometres per hour. Free car parks were built on the edge of the centre, so that visitors could leave their cars there and walk the last few minutes.

The results have surprised even the supporters of the plan. The number of cars in the centre has fallen (5) more than ninety per cent, and air pollution has dropped dramatically. Since 2011, not a single pedestrian (6) been killed in a traffic accident. Shops that were expected to close are doing well, because people (7) walk spend more time in the streets and stop more often.

The city has also become more attractive (8) families. While most Spanish towns of a similar size are losing population, Pontevedra has gained about twelve thousand new residents. Children walk to school on (9) own, and the city has created special "safe routes" where volunteers keep an eye on them.

Of course, not every problem has been solved. Deliveries are only allowed early in the morning, which causes difficulties for some businesses, and people with disabilities still depend (10) special permits. Some critics say that the model would not work in a big city like Madrid.

The mayor disagrees. "Every city is made (11) small neighbourhoods," he says. "If you can do it in one neighbourhood, you can do it in a hundred." Several cities, including Paris and Barcelona, have already sent experts (12) study the Pontevedra model.

For the people of Pontevedra, there is (13) going back. "When my parents visit and see the square," says one young mother, "they can hardly believe it is (14) same place. They remember it full of smoke and noise. My children don't even know what a traffic jam is." Perhaps that is the (15) convincing argument of all.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. when
naloge.rezultat:
1. that
2. up
3. by
4. in
5. by
6. has
7. who / that
8. for
9. their
10. on
11. of / up
12. to
13. no
14. the
15. most
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. that
Za »be afraid« lahko sledi odvisnik s that.
2. up
Frazni glagol »give up« = obupati, odnehati.
3. by
Stalna zveza »step by step« = korak za korakom, postopoma.
4. in
Predlog kraja: in the rest of the city.
5. by
Pri spremembi količine z »fall / rise« uporabimo by za razliko (fallen by 90 %).
6. has
Present perfect (Since 2011 …); osebek »not a single pedestrian« je v ednini.
7. who / that
Oziralni zaimek za osebe: people who walk = ljudje, ki hodijo.
8. for
Zveza »attractive for / to families«; v vrzeli je pričakovan for.
9. their
Stalna zveza »on their own« = sami; svojilni zaimek se ujema z »children«.
10. on
Glagol »depend on« = biti odvisen od.
11. of / up
»be made up of« = biti sestavljen iz; sprejemljivo je tudi »made of«.
12. to
Namen: sent experts to study … (da bi preučili).
13. no
Stalna zveza »there is no going back« = ni poti nazaj.
14. the
Stalna zveza »the same place«; pred same vedno stoji določni člen.
15. most
Presežnik »the most convincing argument of all«.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The surprising story of the umbrella

Few objects are as ordinary as the umbrella, yet its history is anything but (0) (BORE).

The first umbrellas were not used against rain at all. In ancient Egypt, China and India they were a symbol of (1) (ROYAL) and were carried over kings and priests to protect them from the sun. Only a few (2) (CAREFUL) chosen servants were allowed to hold them.

The Chinese were probably the first to make umbrellas (3) (WATER), by covering paper with oil and wax. From there the idea spread slowly to other parts of Asia and, much later, to Europe. In the seventeenth century, umbrellas became (4) (FASHION) among wealthy French women, but men refused to carry them, because carrying one was seen as a sign of (5) (WEAK).

In Britain, the man who changed this was a merchant named Jonas Hanway. In the 1750s he began walking through London with an umbrella, ignoring the (6) (LAUGH) of people in the streets. Coach drivers, who earned money by taking people home when it rained, were especially (7) (FRIEND). They shouted at him and sometimes tried to run him over, because they saw the umbrella as a threat to their (8) (EMPLOY).

Hanway carried on for thirty years, and by the time of his death umbrellas had become a common sight. In the nineteenth century, the (9) (INVENT) of a light steel frame made them cheaper and more (10) (RELY), and soon almost every Londoner owned one.

Today, around one billion umbrellas are sold every year. (11) (FORTUNATE), most of them are cheap and break after a few storms, which creates huge amounts of waste. Some designers are now working on stronger models that can survive winds of over a hundred kilometres per hour, while others are experimenting with materials that are completely (12) (BIODEGRADE).

There have also been some (13) (USUAL) uses. In 1978, a Bulgarian writer was killed in London by a poisoned umbrella tip, one of the most famous (14) (MURDER) of the Cold War. And in 2014, umbrellas became a symbol of (15) (RESIST) during the protests in Hong Kong. It seems that this simple object still has a few surprises left.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. boring
naloge.rezultat:
1. royalty
2. carefully
3. waterproof
4. fashionable
5. weakness
6. laughter
7. unfriendly
8. employment
9. invention
10. reliable
11. Unfortunately
12. biodegradable
13. unusual
14. murders
15. resistance
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. royalty
Za predlogom »of« stoji samostalnik: royal → royalty (kraljevska oblast, kraljevski rod).
2. carefully
Pred pridevnikom (chosen) stoji prislov: carefully chosen.
3. waterproof
Sestavljenka water + proof = nepremočljiv; za glagolom make + predmet stoji pridevnik.
4. fashionable
Za »became« stoji pridevnik: fashion → fashionable.
5. weakness
Za »a sign of« stoji samostalnik: weak → weakness (znak šibkosti).
6. laughter
Za določnim členom stoji samostalnik: the laughter of people.
7. unfriendly
Kočijaži so nanj kričali: pridevnik z nikalno predpono un-.
8. employment
Za svojilnim zaimkom »their« stoji samostalnik: employ → employment.
9. invention
Za določnim členom samostalnik: invent → invention.
10. reliable
Vzporedno s »cheaper«: more + pridevnik → reliable.
11. Unfortunately
Prislov na začetku povedi, ki izraža komentar; pomen je negativen (se hitro pokvarijo), zato un-.
12. biodegradable
Pridevnik za »completely«: bio + degrade + -able = biološko razgradljiv.
13. unusual
Pomen: nenavadne rabe; usual → unusual.
14. murders
Za »one of the most famous« stoji samostalnik v množini.
15. resistance
Za predlogom »of« samostalnik: resist → resistance.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Rosa Fenton, a chef, about her childhood. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Rosa, you grew up in a fishing village in Cornwall. What was it like?

Rosa: Small and windy! There were about four hundred people, one shop and a pub. My father was a fisherman and my mother ran a café on the harbour, so I spent most of my childhood either on a boat or behind a counter.

Interviewer: Is that where you learned to cook?

Rosa: Not exactly. My mother's café served tea and sandwiches – nothing exciting. The real cook in the family was my grandmother. She lived with us, and every Sunday she made fish stew for the whole street. I was allowed to help from the age of six, but only if I cleaned the fish first. I hated that job, but it taught me that good food starts with good ingredients.

Interviewer: Were you a good pupil at school?

Rosa: Terrible! The school was in the next town, and the bus took forty minutes. I used to look out of the window and plan menus instead of doing my homework. My teachers thought I was lazy. Only my art teacher understood me. She said that cooking was a kind of art, and she let me design the posters for the school's Christmas fair.

Interviewer: When did you decide to become a chef?

Rosa: When I was fifteen, a famous chef came to the village to film a television programme. He needed somebody to carry boxes, and my mother sent me. At the end of the day he tasted my grandmother's stew – I had brought some in a flask – and said it was better than anything in his restaurant. That evening I told my parents I was leaving school.

Interviewer: How did they react?

Rosa: My father was furious. He wanted me to finish my exams first, and in the end we agreed that I would. I went to catering college in Plymouth at eighteen.

Interviewer: Do you still go back to the village?

Rosa: Every summer. The café is closed now, and most of the fishing boats have gone, which makes me sad. But I opened a cookery school there two years ago. Local children come for free on Saturdays, and the first thing they learn is how to clean a fish.

A childhood by the sea

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where did Rosa grow up?
    In a fishing village in Cornwall.
  2. 1.How many people lived in Rosa's village?
  3. 2.What did Rosa's mother do?
  4. 3.What did Rosa's grandmother cook every Sunday?
  5. 4.What did Rosa have to do before she could help her grandmother?
  6. 5.How long was the bus journey to school?
  7. 6.What did Rosa do instead of her homework?
  8. 7.What did her art teacher let her do?
  9. 8.What did the famous chef taste?
  10. 9.What has Rosa opened in the village?
naloge.rezultat:
1. About 400.
2. She ran a café (on the harbour).
3. Fish stew.
4. Clean the fish.
5. Forty minutes.
6. She planned menus.
7. Design posters (for the Christmas fair).
8. Her grandmother's (fish) stew.
9. A cookery school.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. About 400.
»There were about four hundred people«.
2. She ran a café (on the harbour).
»my mother ran a café on the harbour«.
3. Fish stew.
»every Sunday she made fish stew for the whole street«.
4. Clean the fish.
»only if I cleaned the fish first«.
5. Forty minutes.
»the bus took forty minutes«.
6. She planned menus.
»plan menus instead of doing my homework«.
7. Design posters (for the Christmas fair).
»she let me design the posters for the school's Christmas fair«.
8. Her grandmother's (fish) stew.
Rosa je enolončnico prinesla v termovki.
