naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

You have seen the following advertisement in an English magazine:

Summer English Courses in Cambridge. Two or four weeks, all levels. Host families or student residence. Excursions every weekend. Write to Mr Peter Hall for more information.

Write an e-mail of 120–150 words in which you:

  • introduce yourself and explain why you want to attend the course,
  • inquire about the details from the advertisement (length, accommodation, excursions),
  • ask about the price and possible discounts.
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poizvedovalno e-pismo z nagovorom Dear Mr Hall, uvodom z namenom, predstavitvijo in razlogom, vljudnimi posrednimi vprašanji o tečaju in ceni ter formalnim koncem; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. introduce yourself and explain why you want to attend the course
  3. inquire about the details from the advertisement (length, accommodation, excursions)
  4. ask about the price and possible discounts
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poizvedovalnega e-pisma
Dear Mr Hall,
Ime naslovnika je v oglasu, zato »Dear Mr Hall« in na koncu »Yours sincerely«.
I am writing to inquire about the summer English courses advertised in Speak Up magazine.
Uvod: namen pisma in kje si videl oglas.
Odstavek 1: predstavitev in razlog
I am a seventeen-year-old student from Slovenia and I would like to improve my speaking before the matura.
Iztočnica 1: kratko o sebi in razlog.
Odstavek 2: vprašanja o podrobnostih
Could you tell me whether students in host families have their own room and which places the excursions visit?
Iztočnica 2: posredna vprašanja (Could you tell me whether …?), ne neposredna (Do students …?).
Odstavek 3: cena
I would also be grateful if you could let me know the price of the four-week course and whether there are discounts for groups.
Iztočnica 3: vljudno vprašanje z I would be grateful if …
I look forward to hearing from you. / Yours sincerely, / Ana Kovač
Formalen konec.
Preštej besede (120–150). Brez skrajšanih oblik.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Mr Hall,

I am writing to inquire about the summer English courses in Cambridge which I saw advertised in Speak Up magazine.

I am a seventeen-year-old student from Slovenia, and I will take my matura exam next year. I would like to attend your course because I want to improve my speaking skills before the exam.

I would be grateful if you could give me some more information. Could you tell me whether students in host families have their own room? I would also like to know which places the weekend excursions visit and whether they are included in the price.

Finally, could you please let me know how much the four-week course costs? I would also like to know whether there are any discounts for students who come in a group.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Ana Kovač

Število besed: 144 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Every student should do a part-time job.
  2. Tourism does more harm than good.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče (I largely agree that a part-time job is valuable for students …).
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1: argument + primer (responsibility, managing money).
Primer iz izkušenj: delo v trgovini, varstvo otrok.
Jedro 2: argument + primer (work experience for a future career, contacts).
Povezovalci: In addition, Furthermore.
Jedro 3: protiargument (less time for studying and rest … However, a few hours a week …).
Upoštevaj nasprotno mnenje in ga omeji.
Sklep: povzemi stališče.
Odgovori na »How far do you agree?«.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: crowds, high prices of flats, pollution, damage to nature. Against: jobs, money for local businesses, cultural exchange.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Every student should do a part-time job.

Many secondary school students in Slovenia work during the holidays or at weekends, while others concentrate only on school. In my opinion, every student should try a part-time job, as long as it does not take up too much of their time.

Firstly, a part-time job teaches responsibility. When you work in a shop or a café, you have to arrive on time, follow instructions and deal with customers who are not always polite. These are skills that are difficult to learn in a classroom.

Secondly, working helps young people understand the value of money. When I worked in a bakery last summer, I realised how many hours I needed to work to buy a new phone. Since then, I have been much more careful about what I spend.

Furthermore, a job can help students decide what they want to do in the future. A friend of mine worked in a kindergarten and discovered that she wanted to become a teacher.

On the other hand, critics argue that students who work have less time for studying and rest, and their marks may suffer. This is true if they work every afternoon. However, a few hours a week or a job during the summer holidays should not cause any problems.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that a part-time job is a valuable experience. It prepares students for adult life, as long as school remains their first priority.

Število besed: 243 (zahtevanih 220–250). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Man Who Fooled the Experts

In 1945, shortly after the end of the Second World War, Dutch police arrested a painter called Han van Meegeren. He was accused of a very serious crime: selling a national treasure, a painting by the seventeenth-century master Johannes Vermeer, to the Nazi leader Hermann Göring. The punishment for collaborating with the enemy could be death.

Van Meegeren's defence was astonishing. The painting, he said, was not a Vermeer at all. He had painted it himself. Nobody believed him. The experts had examined the picture and agreed that it was genuine. To prove his innocence, van Meegeren offered to paint another "Vermeer" in front of witnesses. For six weeks, under police guard, he worked on a new picture in the style of the master. When it was finished, even the doubters had to admit that he was telling the truth.

His story had begun twenty years earlier. Van Meegeren was a talented painter, but critics dismissed his work as old-fashioned and sentimental. Bitter and angry, he decided to take revenge by proving that the same critics could not recognise a masterpiece when they saw one.

He prepared very carefully. He bought old paintings from the seventeenth century, scraped off the original paint and used the canvases for his own work. He mixed his colours from the same natural materials that Vermeer had used, including expensive blue pigment made from a precious stone. To make the paint hard and cracked, as in a three-hundred-year-old picture, he added a type of plastic and baked the canvas in an oven. Finally, he rolled the canvas over a cylinder to create fine cracks and filled them with ink so that they looked like dirt.

His most famous forgery, The Supper at Emmaus, was bought in 1937 by a leading museum in Rotterdam. A respected art historian described it as "the masterpiece of Johannes Vermeer". Van Meegeren went on to sell several more fakes and became one of the richest men in the Netherlands.

In 1947 he was found guilty of forgery and fraud, but not of collaboration. Many Dutch people saw him as a hero who had cheated Göring, and in a survey he was named the second most popular man in the country, after the prime minister. He was sentenced to one year in prison, but he died of a heart attack before he could begin his sentence.

Today, scientists can identify his forgeries easily, because the plastic he used was not invented until the twentieth century. Yet the question his story raises remains uncomfortable: if a painting can move us and convince the experts, does it matter who painted it?

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.When was van Meegeren arrested?
    In 1945.
  2. 1.What was van Meegeren accused of?
  3. 2.What did van Meegeren claim about the painting?
  4. 3.How did he prove that he was telling the truth?
  5. 4.How did critics describe his own paintings?
  6. 5.Why did he begin forging paintings?
  7. 6.Why did he buy old paintings?
  8. 7.What did he do to make the paint hard?
  9. 8.Why did he fill the cracks with ink?
  10. 9.How did many Dutch people see him after the trial?
  11. 10.Why can scientists recognise his forgeries today?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Selling a national treasure to Göring. / Collaborating with the enemy.
2. He had painted it himself.
3. He painted another 'Vermeer' in front of witnesses.
4. (As) old-fashioned and sentimental.
5. To take revenge on the critics.
6. To use their canvases.
7. He added plastic and baked the canvas (in an oven).
8. So that they looked like dirt.
9. As a hero (who had cheated Göring).
10. The plastic he used didn't exist in Vermeer's time.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Selling a national treasure to Göring. / Collaborating with the enemy.
Obtožen je bil, da je Göringu prodal nacionalni zaklad – sodelovanje s sovražnikom.
2. He had painted it himself.
»He had painted it himself.« – slika naj ne bi bila Vermeerjeva.
3. He painted another 'Vermeer' in front of witnesses.
Pod policijskim nadzorom je šest tednov slikal novo »Vermeerjevo« sliko.
4. (As) old-fashioned and sentimental.
»critics dismissed his work as old-fashioned and sentimental«.
5. To take revenge on the critics.
Hotel je dokazati, da kritiki ne prepoznajo mojstrovine – maščevanje.
6. To use their canvases.
Postrgal je barvo in uporabil stara platna.
7. He added plastic and baked the canvas (in an oven).
»he added a type of plastic and baked the canvas in an oven«.
8. So that they looked like dirt.
Namen: »so that they looked like dirt«.
9. As a hero (who had cheated Göring).
»Many Dutch people saw him as a hero who had cheated Göring«.
10. The plastic he used didn't exist in Vermeer's time.
Plastika je bila izumljena šele v 20. stoletju.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (G).

Do trees talk to each other?

Scientists are discovering that forests are far more cooperative than we once believed.

For a long time, foresters thought of trees as individuals competing for light, water and space. The strongest survived, the weakest died. [0] But over the past thirty years, research has revealed a very different picture.

Much of this change is thanks to the Canadian ecologist Suzanne Simard. As a young woman, she worked for a logging company, where she noticed that young trees planted in cleared areas often became sick. [1] Simard suspected that something important was missing from the soil.

She discovered that the roots of trees are connected by a vast underground network of fungi. [2] In return for sugar from the trees, the fungi supply them with water and nutrients from the soil.

Simard's most surprising finding was that trees use this network to share resources. Using radioactive carbon, she showed that a large, old tree can send sugar to young trees growing in its shade. [3] She called these large trees "mother trees".

The network also seems to carry warnings. When a tree is attacked by insects, it may send chemical signals through the fungi to its neighbours. [4] Some researchers have even found that trees of different species support each other: birches and firs exchange carbon depending on the season.

Not everyone accepts this interpretation. [5] Some scientists argue that the evidence comes mainly from laboratory experiments and a small number of forests, and that the role of the network has been exaggerated in popular books and films.

They also object to the language used to describe the research. [6] A tree, they say, does not care for its children in the way a human mother does. It is simply responding to chemical conditions.

Simard admits that words like "talking" are metaphors. [7] In her view, if people feel connected to forests, they will be more willing to protect them.

The research has practical consequences. Modern forestry often involves cutting down all the trees in an area and planting a single species in neat rows. [8] Simard argues that keeping some old trees and planting a mixture of species would make forests healthier and more resistant to climate change.

Whatever the final answer, one thing is clear. [9] A forest is not just a collection of trees but a living community whose members depend on one another. [10]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AThese neighbours then produce substances that make their leaves less attractive to the pests.
  2. BSuch plantations may produce wood quickly, but they lack the networks that connect a natural forest.
  3. COlder trees that were left standing nearby, however, seemed to protect the young ones.
  4. DWords such as "mother" or "communication", they claim, make trees sound like people.
  5. EHowever, she believes that they help the public to understand complicated science.
  6. FThe debate about how forests work is far from over.
  7. GForestry was based on this idea of a battle for survival.
  8. HIts own seedlings, she claims, receive more than the seedlings of strangers.
  9. IThese fungi wrap themselves around the roots and grow far into the ground.
  10. JCritics agree that fungi are important but doubt how much trees actually share.
  11. KIt deserves to be studied, and protected, as a whole.
  12. LMost trees, in fact, live completely alone.
  13. MAs a result, logging companies stopped planting trees altogether.
naloge.rezultat:
1. C
2. I
3. H
4. A
5. J
6. D
7. E
8. B
9. F
10. K
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. C
Mlada drevesa na posekah so zbolevala; nasprotje (however) so drevesa ob starih drevesih. To Simard napelje k sumu, da v tleh nekaj manjka.
2. I
»a vast underground network of fungi« – vrzel glive opiše (These fungi …); naslednja poved pojasni izmenjavo sladkorja in hranil.
3. H
Nadaljuje misel o velikem drevesu, ki hrani mlada; »Its own seedlings« pojasni, zakaj jih imenuje »mother trees«.
4. A
Opozorilni signal sosedom (to its neighbours); »These neighbours then produce substances …« je posledica.
5. J
»Not everyone accepts this interpretation.« – vrzel predstavi kritike, naslednja poved navede njihove argumente.
6. D
»They also object to the language« – primer: besede »mother« in »communication«; naslednja poved nadaljuje z materjo.
7. E
Simard prizna, da so besede metafore, »However« uvede njen zagovor; naslednja poved ga razširi.
8. B
Opis monokultur v vrstah; B pove slabost: nimajo omrežij naravnega gozda. Sledi Simardin predlog.
9. F
»one thing is clear« – kljub temu da razprava še ni končana (F), je jasno, da je gozd skupnost.
10. K
Sklep: gozd si zasluži, da ga preučujemo in varujemo kot celoto.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Are you a lark or an owl?

Some people jump out of bed at six o'clock full of energy, while (0) can hardly open their eyes before ten. Scientists call the first group "larks" and the second "owls", and research suggests that the difference is not just a matter of habit (1) also of biology.

Our daily rhythm is controlled by an internal clock, a group of cells in the brain that responds (2) light and darkness. This clock tells the body when to release hormones, when to feel hungry and when to sleep. In most people, it runs on a cycle of slightly more (3) twenty-four hours, which is why we need daylight to reset it every morning.

Not everyone's clock runs at the same speed. Studies of thousands of volunteers have shown that our preference for mornings or evenings is partly inherited. Scientists have identified more than three hundred genes (4) influence it. If both your parents are owls, there is a good chance that you will be one (5).

Age also plays a role. Young children tend to be larks, teenagers become strong owls, and in old age most people return to being early risers. This is (6) grandparents and grandchildren are often awake at dawn together, while teenagers sleep until noon.

Being an owl can be difficult in a world that is organised around early mornings. Schools and offices usually start at eight or nine, which forces owls (7) get up when their bodies are still in "night mode". Researchers call this "social jet lag". It is similar to the tiredness we feel after flying across time zones, (8) owls experience it every working week.

The consequences can be serious. Studies have found that owls who are forced to live like larks are more likely to suffer (9) depression, heart disease and diabetes. They also tend to get lower marks at school, not because they are less intelligent, but (10) they are tested at the wrong time of day.

Some employers have started to take this into account. A number of companies now offer flexible working hours, allowing staff to start whenever suits them best. Several schools have experimented with later start times, with encouraging results.

So, can an owl turn (11) a lark? Up to a point. Getting plenty of sunlight in the morning, avoiding screens late in the evening and going to bed at the same time every day can shift the internal clock by about an hour. However, experts warn that it is very difficult to change it completely. "Your chronotype is a bit (12) your height," says one researcher. "You can stand up straight, but you can't make (13) much taller."

Perhaps the answer is not to change people but to accept that we are all different. After all, a society needs both: larks to bake the morning bread, and owls to keep the world running (14) the rest of us are asleep. The important thing is to know (15) type you are.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. others
naloge.rezultat:
1. but
2. to
3. than
4. that / which
5. too
6. why
7. to
8. but / except
9. from
10. because
11. into
12. like
13. yourself
14. while / when
15. which / what
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. but
Zveza »not just … but also« = ne le …, ampak tudi.
2. to
»respond to« = odzivati se na.
3. than
»slightly more than twenty-four hours« – primerjava.
4. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za stvari (genes) v vlogi osebka.
5. too
Na koncu povedi »too« = tudi (you will be one too).
6. why
»This is why …« = zato.
7. to
»force someone to do something« = prisiliti.
8. but / except
Nasprotje: podobno kot pri letenju, a sove ga doživljajo vsak teden.
9. from
»suffer from« = trpeti zaradi, bolehati za.
10. because
»not because …, but because …« – vzporedna zgradba vzroka.
11. into
»turn into« = spremeniti se v.
12. like
Primerjava: is a bit like your height = je nekoliko podoben tvoji višini.
13. yourself
Povratni zaimek: you can't make yourself taller.
14. while / when
Časovni veznik: medtem ko mi spimo.
15. which / what
Vprašalni zaimek v odvisnem vprašanju: know which type you are.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Walking around the world

In 1970, a young American reporter called Tom Reed (0) (READ) a book about a man who had walked across America. Twelve years later, he set off from his home in Ohio to walk around the world.

Reed's plan was simple: he (1) (WALK) through as many countries as possible and write about the people he met. Before he left, he (2) (SPEND) two years preparing. He studied maps, saved money from his job as a reporter and trained by walking forty kilometres a day with a heavy backpack.

For the next four years, he (3) (CROSS) twenty countries on five continents. He walked through the deserts of Algeria, the mountains of Turkey and the bush of Australia. Wherever he went, he (4) (INVITE) into people's homes. "I (5) (NEVER / FORGET) how kind strangers were," he wrote later. "The poorest families always shared the most."

His journey was not without danger. In one country, he was arrested by soldiers who thought he (6) (BE) a spy. In Thailand, he caught a serious fever after he (7) (BITE) by mosquitoes, and in Australia he nearly died of thirst when his water supply ran out. By the time he reached the Indian Ocean, he (8) (WEAR) out eighteen pairs of boots.

While he (9) (WALK) through Europe, he regularly sent articles to newspapers in the United States. Readers followed his progress every week, and many schools used his letters in geography lessons. Children (10) (SEND) him thousands of letters, which were waiting for him at post offices along his route.

Four years after he had set off, Reed finally walked back into his home town, where thousands of people (11) (WAIT) for him in the main street. He had covered more than 22,000 kilometres. He was one of very few people who (12) (WALK) around the world alone.

Today, Reed gives talks in schools and encourages young people to travel. "If I (13) (STAY) at home, I would never have learned that the world is a friendly place," he says. "People often ask me whether I (14) (DO) it again. My answer is always yes – but this time, I (15) (TAKE) more socks."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com; zgodba je izmišljena.)

Example: 0. read
naloge.rezultat:
1. would walk / was going to walk
2. spent / had spent
3. crossed
4. was invited
5. will never forget
6. was
7. had been bitten / was bitten
8. had worn
9. was walking
10. sent
11. were waiting
12. had walked
13. had stayed
14. would do
15. will take / would take / am going to take
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. would walk / was going to walk
Prihodnost v preteklosti (načrt): would ali was going to.
2. spent / had spent
Pred odhodom (before he left): past simple ali past perfect.
3. crossed
Zaključeno obdobje v preteklosti (For the next four years): past simple.
4. was invited
Povabili so ga drugi: trpnik v pretekliku.
5. will never forget
Prihodnost; govori ob pisanju po potovanju: will never forget.
6. was
Poročani govor v preteklosti: they thought he was a spy.
7. had been bitten / was bitten
Dejanje pred drugim preteklim dejanjem in v trpniku: had been bitten.
8. had worn
»By the time he reached …« zahteva past perfect.
9. was walking
»While« + dejanje v teku: past continuous.
10. sent
Zaključeno dejanje v preteklosti: past simple.
11. were waiting
Dejanje v teku ob prihodu: past continuous.
12. had walked
Dosežek pred drugim preteklim trenutkom (vrnitev domov): past perfect.
13. had stayed
Tretji pogojnik: If I had stayed …, I would never have learned.
14. would do
Poročano vprašanje o hipotetični prihodnosti: whether I would do it again.
15. will take / would take / am going to take
Hipotetični odgovor ali načrt: would take; sprejemljivo tudi will take.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Megan Lloyd, a volunteer with a lifeboat crew on the coast of Wales. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Megan, how long have you been a lifeboat volunteer?

Megan: Eleven years now. I joined when I was seventeen, which is the youngest age you're allowed to start. My uncle was a member of the crew, and I used to sit in the lifeboat station after school, listening to his stories.

Interviewer: What do you do when you're not on the lifeboat?

Megan: I'm a hairdresser. I have my own small salon in the town, and my customers are used to me running out in the middle of a haircut. When the pager goes off, I have about seven minutes to get to the station. Usually I leave a colleague to finish the job, but once I had to leave a woman with only half her hair cut!

Interviewer: What kind of calls do you get?

Megan: All sorts. In summer, it's mostly tourists – people on inflatable boats who get carried out to sea by the wind, or walkers who are cut off by the tide. In winter, it's more often fishing boats with engine problems. We go out about sixty times a year.

Interviewer: Is it dangerous?

Megan: It can be, but our training is very good. Every Tuesday evening we practise, whatever the weather. We learn first aid, navigation and how to work with a helicopter. The most important thing is that you trust the people next to you completely.

Interviewer: Can you remember your most difficult rescue?

Megan: Yes. Three years ago, a father and his two sons were sailing when their boat turned over in a storm. The waves were five metres high, and it was dark. We found the boys holding on to the boat, but the father had drifted away. We searched for almost two hours and finally saw the light on his life jacket. He was extremely cold, but he survived.

Interviewer: Do you get paid?

Megan: No, none of the crew is paid. The charity that runs the lifeboats is funded by donations from the public. People sometimes don't realise that – they think we're part of the coastguard.

Interviewer: What would you say to someone who wants to join?

Megan: You don't need to be a sailor or super fit. You need to be reliable, calm and willing to get up at three in the morning. And you need an understanding boss!

A lifeboat volunteer

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to two speakers, a writer and a scientist, talking about Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Today we're discussing Frankenstein, which was first published more than two hundred years ago. Clare, as a writer, what do you find most surprising about the book?

Clare: That Mary Shelley was only eighteen when she started writing it. She was on holiday near Lake Geneva in 1816, a summer when it hardly stopped raining because of a volcanic eruption on the other side of the world. The guests were stuck indoors, so the poet Lord Byron suggested that everyone should write a ghost story. Most of them gave up, but Mary didn't.

Presenter: Tom, you're a biologist. Does the science in the novel make any sense?

Tom: Surprisingly, it was based on real experiments. At that time, scientists were using electricity to make the muscles of dead animals move. Some even tried it on the bodies of executed criminals, and audiences watched in horror as the faces twitched. Mary Shelley had heard about these experiments, so the idea of bringing a body back to life was not pure fantasy for her readers.

Presenter: Most people imagine the monster as a large green creature with bolts in his neck.

Clare: Yes, but that comes from the films of the 1930s, not from the book. In the novel, the creature is intelligent and sensitive. He teaches himself to read by secretly listening to a family through a hole in a wall, and he reads poetry and history. He only becomes violent after everyone rejects him because of his appearance.

Tom: And people often forget that the creature has no name. Frankenstein is the scientist, not the monster.

Presenter: Why is the book still relevant today?

Tom: Because it asks a question that we face all the time in science: just because we can do something, should we? Victor Frankenstein creates life, but he refuses to take responsibility for what he has made. When I teach students about genetic engineering or artificial intelligence, I often start with this book.

Clare: For me, it's a book about loneliness. The creature says that he is wicked because he is miserable. I think every teenager who has felt like an outsider can understand that.

Presenter: If you could ask Mary Shelley one question, what would it be?

Clare: I'd ask her whether she felt sorry for the creature or for Victor. I've read it five times, and I still can't decide.

Talking about Frankenstein

    two hundred
  2. 1.Mary Shelley was on holiday near ____ in 1816.
  3. 2.It rained a lot that summer because of a ____.
  4. 3.Scientists used electricity to make the ____ of dead animals move.
  5. 4.Some experiments were carried out on the bodies of ____.
  6. 5.The popular image of the monster comes from ____.
  7. 6.The creature listens to a family through ____.
  8. 7.The creature becomes violent after people reject him because of ____.
  9. 8.Victor refuses to take ____ for his creation.
  10. 9.Clare has read the novel ____.

naloge.besedilo:
Article

The international journal European Identity is publishing a special issue on how young people feel about Europe. It has asked students from different countries to contribute.

Write an article of 150–180 words about this issue for the journal, in which you:

  • explain whether young people in your country feel European,
  • describe what the European Union means in their everyday lives,
  • suggest how young Europeans could be brought closer together.
naloge.rezultat: Članek z naslovom, živim uvodom, odstavki o občutku evropske pripadnosti, vlogi EU v vsakdanu in predlogu za povezovanje mladih ter sklepom; 150–180 besed, polformalni slog.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Article (150–180 words), semi-formal style, with a title
  2. explain whether young people in your country feel European
  3. describe what the European Union means in their everyday lives
  4. suggest how young Europeans could be brought closer together
Kako napišeš članek (article)
Članek (article): zgradba
  • Naslov: kratek in zanimiv; če navodilo ponuja naslove (headings), izberi enega in ga prepiši natančno.
  • Uvod: pritegni bralca (vprašanje, presenetljiv podatek, kratka zgodba) in v eni povedi povej, o čem bo članek.
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku; vsak odstavek začni s temeljno povedjo in jo podpri s primerom ali podatkom.
  • Sklep: povzemi svoje stališče ali nagovori bralce (So next time you …, why not …?). Nagovora »Dear …« in pozdrava ni.
Slog članka
  • Članek je namenjen širši javnosti (bralcem revije, šolskega časopisa, spletne strani), zato je slog polformalen: živahen, a ne pogovoren.
  • Uporabi retorična vprašanja (Have you ever wondered …?), neposreden nagovor bralca (you) in konkretne primere iz izkušenj.
  • Pri članku z mnenjem (opinion article) jasno povej svoje stališče in ga utemelji, upoštevaj tudi nasprotno mnenje.
  • Tudi v polformalnem slogu se izogibaj slengu (gonna, stuff, super cool) in pretiranim klicajem.
Uporabne zveze
  • Have you ever thought about …? · Imagine a school where … · According to a recent survey, …
  • On the one hand, … On the other hand, … · What is more, … · Not only … but also …
  • All in all, … · It is high time we … · The choice is yours.
Pogoste napake
  • Članek napisan kot pismo (Dear readers, … Yours sincerely).
  • Manjka naslov ali je naslov drugačen od ponujenega.
  • Iztočnice so le naštete, niso razvite s primeri in razlogi.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba članka
Naslov: More than a passport: what Europe means to us
Naslov pritegne; nagovora in pozdrava ni.
Uvod: osebna izkušnja ali vprašanje (When I crossed the border to Italy last summer, nobody asked for my passport …).
Uvod uvede temo z živim primerom.
Odstavek 1: ali se mladi počutijo Evropejce
Most young Slovenians feel both Slovenian and European; they grew up with the euro and open borders.
Iztočnica 1: stališče z razlogi.
Odstavek 2: EU v vsakdanjem življenju
Erasmus exchanges, no roaming charges, studying abroad, EU-funded cycle paths.
Iztočnica 2: konkretni primeri.
Odstavek 3: predlog
Free Interrail passes for every eighteen-year-old and more online exchanges between schools.
Iztočnica 3: predlog z utemeljitvijo.
Sklep: Europe is not only a map but a community we build ourselves.
Polformalni slog; višja raven zahteva pestrejše besedišče.
Preštej besede (150–180). Naslov šteje.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
More than a passport: what Europe means to us

Last summer, nobody asked for my passport at the Italian border, and I paid for my ice cream in euros, just like at home. Moments like this make many young Slovenians feel European without even thinking about it.

Most people of my generation see themselves as both Slovenian and European. We have grown up with the euro, open borders and the freedom to study or work anywhere in the Union.

In our everyday lives, the European Union is surprisingly present. Students go on Erasmus exchanges, we use our phones abroad without roaming charges, and many cycle paths and school projects in my town were funded by the EU.

However, young Europeans still know too little about each other. Every eighteen-year-old could receive a free Interrail pass, and schools could organise regular online exchanges with partner classes in other countries.

After all, Europe is not only a map or an institution in Brussels. It is a community that we build ourselves, one friendship at a time.

Število besed: 174 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss the role of Tommy in Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go.

Kazuo Ishiguro: Never Let Me Go

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo o Tommyju kot liku, ki najbolj iskreno reagira na krivico, podprto s prizori (izbruhi v Hailshamu, Miss Lucy, risbe živali, obisk pri Madame in Miss Emily, krik na polju); brez obnove; 250–300 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the role of Tommy in Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – Tommy is the character who reacts most honestly to the injustice of the clones' fate; his anger and his art reveal what the others hide.
Teza v uvodu, brez obnove.
Jedro 1 – Hailsham: his tantrums, the other students' cruelty, Miss Lucy tells him that it doesn't matter if he is not creative.
Konkretni prizori iz otroštva.
Jedro 2 – the Cottages: his drawings of imaginary animals and the theory of the Gallery; his relationship with Ruth and then with Kathy.
Pokaži njegovo upanje na odlog (deferral).
Jedro 3 – the visit to Madame and Miss Emily: the truth that there are no deferrals; Tommy's scream in the dark field.
Vrhunec: Tommyjeva jeza izrazi bolečino, ki je Kathy ne pokaže.
Sklep: Tommy embodies the humanity that the system denies; through him, the reader feels the cruelty of their fate.
Sklep se vrne k tezi.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The role of Tommy in Never Let Me Go

In Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go, most of the students who grow up at Hailsham accept their fate calmly. Tommy is different. In my opinion, he is the character who reacts most honestly to the injustice of their lives, and his anger and his art reveal what the others try to hide.

As a child, Tommy is an outsider. He is not creative, so the other students laugh at him and provoke his famous tantrums. The turning point comes when Miss Lucy tells him that it does not matter if he cannot draw. Later, she tells the students the truth about their future. Tommy is the first to understand that the guardians have kept something important from them.

At the Cottages, Tommy secretly draws tiny, detailed imaginary animals. He believes in a rumour that couples who are truly in love can get a deferral, and that Madame's Gallery was created to see into their souls. His relationship with Ruth keeps him away from Kathy, but in the end he and Kathy become a couple, and his drawings become a symbol of their hope.

The most painful scene in the novel is the visit to Madame and Miss Emily. They learn that deferrals have never existed and that the Gallery was only meant to prove that clones have souls. On the way back, Tommy gets out of the car and screams in a dark field. His scream expresses the pain that Kathy, the calm narrator, never shows.

In conclusion, Tommy embodies the humanity that the system denies. Through his anger, the reader feels how cruel and unfair the fate of the clones really is.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

My Grandfather's Garden

Every Saturday morning when I was a boy, my mother dropped me off at my grandfather's house on the edge of town. It was a small brick house with a garden that seemed enormous to me, full of vegetables, fruit trees and a greenhouse that smelled of tomatoes and warm earth.

My grandfather had been a train driver for forty years, and he ran his garden like a railway: everything had a timetable. Potatoes went in on Good Friday, the beans were planted when the oak tree had leaves, and the onions were harvested on the first Sunday in August, whatever the weather. He kept a notebook with every date written in pencil, going back to the year I was born.

At first I was given only small jobs. I collected snails from the lettuces and dropped them in a bucket, which he then carried to the field across the road. "They have as much right to live as we do," he said. "Just not in my lettuces." Later, he gave me my own bed, two metres long and one metre wide, and let me decide what to grow. I chose sunflowers, because I wanted something taller than me.

My sunflowers were a disaster. I planted them too close together, forgot to water them during a hot week, and the birds ate most of the seeds before they could grow. My grandfather did not say a word. He simply wrote "sunflowers – too close" in his notebook, and the next spring he gave me a packet of seeds and a ruler.

That second year, my sunflowers grew to almost three metres. I measured them every Saturday and wrote the numbers in my own notebook, which he had bought for me. When the flowers finally opened, he took a photograph of me standing between them, looking very small and very proud. It still hangs in my kitchen.

My grandfather died when I was nineteen. The house was sold, and the new owners replaced the vegetables with a lawn and a garage. For years I could not drive past it. Then, last spring, I bought a small house of my own with a garden that is not much bigger than a car park.

In the drawer of my desk I found his old notebook, which my mother had kept for me. On the first page, in his careful handwriting, it says: "Potatoes – Good Friday." This year, for the first time, I followed his timetable. The potatoes are doing well. Next to them, at exactly the right distance from each other, there is a row of sunflowers.

How I learned a language

Five people explain how they became fluent in a foreign language.

A Leo, Italian

I fell in love with Italian through opera. My grandmother used to play recordings every Sunday, and by the age of twelve I could sing whole arias without understanding a word. When I finally started lessons at university, I was amazed at how much I already knew. My pronunciation was excellent, but my grammar was terrible, because operas use a very old-fashioned language. My Italian friends still laugh when I use words that nobody has said since the nineteenth century.

B Priya, German

I moved to Berlin for work without speaking any German, and the first months were very lonely. Everybody at the office spoke English, so I had no reason to practise. In the end, I joined a choir, because I had always loved singing. We sang in German, we chatted in German during the breaks, and after a year I could follow a conversation. My advice is simple: find a hobby you love and do it in the language you want to learn.

C Ivan, Spanish

I learned Spanish completely online. I used an app for twenty minutes every day on the bus to work, and twice a week I had video lessons with a teacher in Mexico, which were surprisingly cheap. After two years, I travelled to Mexico for the first time. I was nervous, but I could understand almost everything. The only problem was that I spoke Mexican Spanish, so when I later visited Spain, people found some of my expressions strange.

D Sarah, Japanese

Japanese was the hardest thing I have ever done. There are three writing systems, and it took me four years to read a newspaper. I studied in a traditional way, with textbooks and lists of characters on my bedroom wall. What kept me going was a pen friend in Osaka. We wrote letters to each other for ten years before we finally met, and she was the bridesmaid at my wedding.

E Mateo, English

I learned English mostly from video games and films. As a child, I played online with people from all over the world, and we had to communicate quickly. My teachers at school were surprised, because I spoke fluently but made a lot of spelling mistakes. I had heard thousands of words but had never seen them written. When I started reading English novels at sixteen, my writing finally improved.

  7. 6.Who discovered that people in another country found their language unusual?
  8. 7.Who needed several years before reading everyday texts?
  9. 8.Whose language learning led to a lifelong friendship?
  10. 9.Who learned through playing with others?
  11. 10.Who could speak well but had difficulty writing correctly?

Interviewer: Grace, your bakeries are famous for their bread, but also for the people who work there. How did it start?

Grace: With a loaf of bread, really. Twelve years ago I was working in a bank in London and volunteering in the evenings at a shelter for homeless people. One night a young man there told me that he had trained as a baker but couldn't find work, because nobody would employ someone without an address. I thought, that's ridiculous – people need bread and he can make it.

Interviewer: So you opened a bakery?

Grace: Not immediately. First I borrowed a friend's kitchen on Sunday mornings, and he and I baked bread and sold it at a local market. We sold out in two hours. Within six months we had three more bakers, and I left my job at the bank. My parents thought I had gone mad.

Interviewer: How many people do you employ today?

Grace: About ninety, in five bakeries. Around two thirds of them have been homeless, have been in prison or have spent a long time out of work. We give them a full-time contract and training, and after a year, most of them move on to jobs in other bakeries or restaurants. That's our aim – we're a starting point, not a final destination.

Interviewer: Is it difficult to run a business like that?

Grace: Sometimes. People who have had a hard life don't always arrive on time at four in the morning. But I've learned that if you treat people with respect and give them responsibility, they usually rise to the challenge – just like the dough!

Interviewer: Do your customers know about your mission?

Grace: Many don't, and I like that. They come back because the bread is good, not because they feel sorry for anyone. We won a national award for the best sourdough last year, and that made the team prouder than any newspaper article about our social work.

Interviewer: What is your next plan?

Grace: We're opening a training school next spring, where people can get an official qualification as a baker. And I'd like to see big supermarkets buy from businesses like ours. If every supermarket bought just one product from a social enterprise, thousands of people would get a second chance.

You will listen to an interview with Dr Tom Ashby, a scientist who designs sports equipment. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Tom, what does a sports engineer actually do?

Tom: We use science to make sport better, safer and fairer. That can mean designing a new tennis racket, testing football helmets or helping a cyclist find the best position on a bike. Last week, for example, I spent three days in a wind tunnel with a group of speed skaters, testing different suits.

Interviewer: How did you get into this field?

Tom: I was a keen runner at school, but I kept getting injured. My physiotherapist told me that my shoes were part of the problem. I was so annoyed that I started reading about how running shoes work, and I realised that I was more interested in the shoes than in the running. I studied mechanical engineering and then did a doctorate on the design of sports surfaces.

Interviewer: Has technology changed sport a lot?

Tom: Enormously. Think about the pole vault. A hundred years ago, the poles were made of wood, and athletes jumped about four metres. Today, with flexible fibreglass poles, the world record is over six metres. Or swimming: in 2008 and 2009, more than a hundred world records were broken by swimmers wearing new full-body suits. They were banned in 2010 because they gave an unfair advantage.

Interviewer: So where is the line between helping athletes and cheating?

Tom: That's the big question. Every sport has its own rules, and they are often decided by committees that include engineers like me. In general, we say that equipment should help athletes perform at their best, but it should not do the work for them. The skill must stay with the athlete.

Interviewer: Do you work only with top athletes?

Tom: No, and I think the most important work is for ordinary people. I'm currently working on playground surfaces that reduce injuries when children fall, and on cheaper running shoes for people in countries where most runners can't afford expensive brands.

Interviewer: What's the most unusual project you've worked on?

Tom: Probably designing a ball for blind footballers. It has small bells inside, so the players can hear where it is. The difficult part was making the bells loud enough without changing the way the ball bounces.

Interviewer: Finally, do you still run?

Tom: Every morning – in shoes I designed myself. And I haven't been injured for years.

naloge.besedilo:
Report

This year you took part in Reading Buddies, a volunteer project in which secondary school students read with children at a local primary school once a week. The project coordinator has asked volunteers to describe their experience.

Write a report of 120–150 words for the project coordinator in which you should:

  • describe what you did with the children,
  • explain what you found most rewarding,
  • suggest one improvement for next year.
To: Project Coordinator
From: Ana Kovač
Subject: Reading Buddies project
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, uvodom z namenom, odstavki s podnaslovi (dejavnosti z otroki, najbolj dragocen del, predlog za izboljšavo) in sklepom; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (120–150 words), formal style
  2. describe what you did with the children
  3. explain what you found most rewarding
  4. suggest one improvement for next year
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Project Coordinator / From: Ana Kovač / Subject: Reading Buddies project
Glava in naslov; ni nagovora »Dear …«.
Introduction – The aim of this report is to describe my experience as a volunteer in the Reading Buddies project.
Uvod z namenom.
Activities
Every Wednesday I read picture books with two eight-year-olds, played word games and helped them write short stories.
Iztočnica 1: konkretne dejavnosti.
The most rewarding part
The most rewarding moment was when a shy boy read a whole page aloud to the class.
Iztočnica 2: konkreten primer z utemeljitvijo.
Recommendation
I would recommend a larger choice of books, as the school library had few books for weaker readers.
Iztočnica 3: predlog z razlogom.
Conclusion – Overall, the project was a valuable experience for both the children and the volunteers.
Kratek sklep.
Preštej besede (120–150).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Project Coordinator
From: Ana Kovač, 3.C
Subject: Reading Buddies project

Introduction

The aim of this report is to describe my experience as a volunteer in the Reading Buddies project this school year.

Activities

Every Wednesday afternoon, I spent an hour with two eight-year-old pupils. We read picture books together, played word games and wrote short stories, which the children later illustrated.

The most rewarding part

The most rewarding moment came in May, when a very shy boy read a whole page aloud in front of his class. His teacher told me that he had never done that before.

Recommendation

I would recommend buying more books for weaker readers, as the school library had very few short and simple stories.

Conclusion

Overall, the project was a valuable experience for both the children and the volunteers, and I would be happy to take part again.

Ana Kovač

Število besed: 147 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Life was better before smartphones.
  2. Schools should teach practical skills rather than academic subjects.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče (I do not agree that life was better before smartphones, although …).
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1: argument + primer (access to information, maps, emergency calls).
Konkretni primeri.
Jedro 2: argument + primer (keeping in touch, online learning).
Povezovalci.
Jedro 3: protiargument (addiction, less face-to-face contact … However …).
Uravnoteženost.
Sklep: povzemi stališče.
Brez novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: cooking, first aid, managing money, repairing things. Against: academic subjects develop thinking and are needed for university.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Life was better before smartphones.

Many older people say that life was simpler and happier before everyone had a smartphone in their pocket. Although I understand why they feel this way, I do not agree that life was better in the past.

Firstly, smartphones give us access to information at any moment. If I do not understand something at school, I can find an explanation in seconds. Maps help us find our way in foreign cities, and in an emergency we can call for help immediately, which can save lives.

Secondly, smartphones help us stay in touch with the people we love. My brother studies in Vienna, but we talk almost every day and send each other photos. Thirty years ago, families often had to wait weeks for a letter.

On the other hand, it is true that smartphones have created new problems. Many teenagers spend hours scrolling through social media, and some people are almost addicted to their phones. Families sit at the same table without talking to each other. However, these problems are caused by the way we use our phones, not by the phones themselves.

In conclusion, I believe that life today is not worse but different. Smartphones have made our lives easier and safer, and if we learn to switch them off from time to time, we can enjoy the best of both worlds.

Read the text below and choose the correct answer (A, B, C or D). There is an example at the beginning (0).

The Cartographer's Daughter

My mother made maps for a living, which meant that our house was full of places that did not exist yet. Roads that had not been built, reservoirs that were still valleys, the outlines of new towns drawn in pale blue pencil on sheets of paper so large that they covered the dining table for weeks. As a child, I thought she could change the world simply by drawing it.

She worked for the national survey office, and in summer she travelled to remote parts of the country to check the accuracy of the old maps. When I was eleven, she took me with her for the first time. We spent a month in the north, in a region of lakes and forests where the roads were so bad that the car broke down twice in the first week. My mother did not seem to mind. "A map," she said, "is a promise that someone has been here before you. Our job is to make sure the promise is true."

Most days were boring for me. She measured angles with an instrument on three legs, wrote numbers in a notebook and compared them with the map, while I sat in the car reading or throwing stones into the lakes. Occasionally she found a mistake – a path that no longer existed, a bridge that had been washed away – and she would mark it with a small red cross, looking as pleased as if she had found treasure.

Then, in the third week, we came to a place that was not on the map at all. It was a small island in the middle of a lake, connected to the shore by a narrow strip of stones, and on the island there was a lighthouse, absurdly far from any sea. My mother checked the map three times. According to the survey of 1923, the lake was empty.

We walked across the stones together. The lighthouse door was not locked, and inside we found a spiral staircase, a dusty lamp and, on a table, a logbook. The last entry was dated 1951. The keeper had written every night for twenty years, recording the weather and the boats that passed – sometimes one, often none. On the final page, in shaky handwriting, he had written: "Nobody comes any more. I will light the lamp anyway."

My mother sat on the stairs for a long time, reading. I had never seen her so quiet. When we left, she did something she had never done before: instead of a red cross, she drew the lighthouse itself, very small and very carefully, in the middle of the lake.

Years later, when I became a cartographer myself, I looked for the lighthouse on the latest digital maps. It is there, a tiny symbol that most people would never notice. Nobody in the office could tell me who had added it. I like to think that it was her, keeping a promise to a stranger who had kept his own.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.The narrator's mother
    A was a cartographer.B was an architect.C built reservoirs.D worked as a teacher.
    Answer: A
  2. 1.As a child, the narrator believed that her mother
    A built roads and towns.B had the power to create places.C worked mainly at the dining table.D knew every place in the country.
  3. 2.What was the purpose of the mother's summer trips?
    A To draw maps of new towns.B To check that old maps were correct.C To take holidays with her daughter.D To measure the depth of lakes.
  4. 3.The mother's attitude to the problems with the car shows that she was
    A careless.B frightened.C unworried.D annoyed.
  5. 4.According to the mother, a map
    A can never be completely accurate.B should show only places people have visited.C is a guarantee that must be checked.D promises adventures to travellers.
  6. 5.How did the mother feel when she found a mistake?
    A Disappointed.B Satisfied.C Confused.D Embarrassed.
  7. 6.What was strange about the lighthouse?
    A It was not near the sea.B It was still in use.C It was locked.D It was very tall.
  8. 7.What does the keeper's last entry suggest about him?
    A He wanted to leave the island.B He was angry with the authorities.C He remained loyal to his duty.D He had stopped recording the weather.
  9. 8.Why did the mother draw the lighthouse instead of a red cross?
    A She wanted to mark a mistake in the map.B She was moved by the keeper's story.C Her daughter asked her to do it.D She needed it for her report.
  10. 9.At the end of the story, the narrator
    A knows who added the lighthouse to the map.B has removed the lighthouse from the digital map.C imagines that her mother kept a promise.D decides to visit the island again.

2. B
3. C

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take

  • Postopek: najprej preberi vprašanje brez možnosti in v besedilu poišči odgovor; šele nato preberi možnosti in izberi tisto, ki pove isto z drugimi besedami (parafraza).
