Journeys that changed history

Five travellers whose adventures changed the way we see the world.

A Ibn Battuta

In 1325, a young lawyer from Tangier set off on a pilgrimage to Mecca. He did not come home for twenty-four years. Ibn Battuta travelled about 120,000 kilometres, through North Africa, the Middle East, India and China, often working as a judge to pay for his journey. He was robbed, shipwrecked and nearly executed. When he finally returned, the sultan of Morocco ordered a writer to record his stories, and the book remains one of the most important sources on the medieval Islamic world.

B Jeanne Baret

In 1766, Jeanne Baret became the first woman known to have sailed around the world – disguised as a man. She joined a French scientific expedition as the assistant of the botanist Philibert Commerson, who was also her partner. Women were not allowed on navy ships, so she cut her hair and wore loose clothes. She collected thousands of plant specimens, including the bougainvillea, but her name did not appear in the official records. Her discovery was only recognised in 2012, when a plant was named after her.

C Matthew Henson

Matthew Henson was the son of farmers in Maryland and went to sea as a cabin boy at the age of twelve. In 1909, he was a member of the American expedition that claimed to be the first to reach the North Pole. Henson, who spoke the language of the local Inuit and was an expert at handling dog sleds, was probably the first to arrive. Because he was Black, however, he received little recognition for decades and spent most of his life working as a clerk in a customs office.

D Nellie Bly

In 1889, the American journalist Nellie Bly set out to beat the record of Phileas Fogg, the hero of Jules Verne's novel Around the World in Eighty Days. Travelling by ship and train with a single small bag, she completed the journey in seventy-two days. Her newspaper organised a competition in which readers guessed how long the trip would take, and nearly a million people took part. On the way, she visited Jules Verne himself in France, who wished her good luck.

E Tenzing Norgay

Before he became famous, Tenzing Norgay had already taken part in six attempts to climb Mount Everest. A Sherpa from Nepal who could not read or write, he had worked as a porter for foreign expeditions since he was a young man. In 1953, he and the New Zealander Edmund Hillary became the first people to stand on the summit. For years, both men refused to say who had reached the top first, insisting that they had done it as a team.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Who began their journey for religious reasons? (A)

Wolves are excellent travellers: a young wolf looking for (3) own territory can walk more than a thousand kilometres. In 2012, a wolf from Slovenia crossed the Alps and settled in northern Italy, where he found a female from the Italian population. Their pups were the first wolves (4) be born in that area in almost a century.

Today, wolves live in every country of mainland Europe, including Germany, France and even the Netherlands, one of the most densely populated countries in the world. (5) many people, their return is a sign that nature is recovering. Wolves keep the populations of deer and wild boar under control, and in doing (6), they help forests to grow.

In Slovenia and Italy, large white dogs live with the flocks day and night and chase (9) any wolf that comes too close. naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

2. when

4. to

5. For
»For many people« = za mnoge ljudi.
6. so
Stalna zveza »in doing so« = s tem.
7. up
»make up for« = nadomestiti, odtehtati.
8. under
»under my pillow« = pod blazino.
9. away / off
Frazna glagola »chase away / off« = pregnati.
10. but / although / though
Nasprotje: učinkoviti so, a dragi.
11. freely / legally / again
Prislov ob »hunted«: freely (prosto) ali legally (zakonito).
12. because / as / since
Vzrok: mladi volkovi brez staršev težje lovijo divje živali.
13. in
»fairy tales in which …« = pravljice, v katerih …
14. whenever / when / if
Kadar le lahko: whenever they can.
15. rid
Stalna zveza »get rid of« = znebiti se.

Why food tastes different on a red plate

Most of us believe that we judge food by its taste. In fact, our (0) (EXPECT) of flavour are strongly influenced by what we see. Scientists who study the (1) (CONNECT) between colour and taste have produced some surprising results.

In one famous experiment, students of wine-tasting were given a white wine that had been coloured red with a (2) (TASTE) dye. They described it using words that are normally used for red wine, such as "berries" and "chocolate". Not one of the experts noticed that the wine was actually white. Their eyes had told their brains what to expect, and their brains had obeyed (3) (COMPLETE).

The colour of the plate can also make a difference. Researchers in Spain found that a strawberry dessert tasted ten per cent sweeter and more (4) (FLAVOUR) when it was served on a white plate than on a black one. In another study, people ate (5) (CONSIDER) less snack food from red plates, perhaps because we associate red with danger and (6) (WARN).

Food companies have long been aware of this. Orange juice is often coloured to look more orange, and many sweets would look grey without artificial colours. When one drinks company launched a (7) (COLOUR) version of a popular cola in the 1990s, sales were a (8) (DISAPPOINT). Customers said the drink tasted strange, even though the recipe was (9) (CHANGE) apart from the colour.

Restaurants use the same knowledge. Chefs pay careful attention to the (10) (PRESENT) of their dishes, because diners who are served attractive food are willing to pay more and rate the meal more (11) (FAVOUR). Some top restaurants even employ designers to choose the colour of plates, lights and walls.

The effect may also have (12) (MEDICINE) uses. Patients in hospitals often lose their appetite, and some studies suggest that serving food on brightly coloured plates helps them eat more. This is particularly important for older people with dementia, whose (13) (ABLE) to see contrast is often reduced. When their mashed potatoes were served on blue plates instead of white ones, they ate about a quarter more.

So the next time you sit down to a meal, remember that your eyes are tasting it before your mouth does. It is a (14) (REMIND) that our senses do not work separately but are (15) (CONSTANT) talking to each other.

You will listen to an interview with Grace Okoye, who runs a chain of bakeries that employ people who find it hard to get a job. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Grace, your bakeries are famous for their bread, but also for the people who work there. How did it start?

Grace: With a loaf of bread, really. Twelve years ago I was working in a bank in London and volunteering in the evenings at a shelter for homeless people. One night a young man there told me that he had trained as a baker but couldn't find work, because nobody would employ someone without an address. I thought, that's ridiculous – people need bread and he can make it.

Interviewer: So you opened a bakery?

Grace: Not immediately. First I borrowed a friend's kitchen on Sunday mornings, and he and I baked bread and sold it at a local market. We sold out in two hours. Within six months we had three more bakers, and I left my job at the bank. My parents thought I had gone mad.

Interviewer: How many people do you employ today?

Grace: About ninety, in five bakeries. Around two thirds of them have been homeless, have been in prison or have spent a long time out of work. We give them a full-time contract and training, and after a year, most of them move on to jobs in other bakeries or restaurants. That's our aim – we're a starting point, not a final destination.

Interviewer: Is it difficult to run a business like that?

Grace: Sometimes. People who have had a hard life don't always arrive on time at four in the morning. But I've learned that if you treat people with respect and give them responsibility, they usually rise to the challenge – just like the dough!

Interviewer: Do your customers know about your mission?

Grace: Many don't, and I like that. They come back because the bread is good, not because they feel sorry for anyone. We won a national award for the best sourdough last year, and that made the team prouder than any newspaper article about our social work.

Interviewer: What is your next plan?

Grace: We're opening a training school next spring, where people can get an official qualification as a baker. And I'd like to see big supermarkets buy from businesses like ours. If every supermarket bought just one product from a social enterprise, thousands of people would get a second chance.

A social entrepreneur

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Dr Tom Ashby, a scientist who designs sports equipment. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Tom, what does a sports engineer actually do?

Tom: We use science to make sport better, safer and fairer. That can mean designing a new tennis racket, testing football helmets or helping a cyclist find the best position on a bike. Last week, for example, I spent three days in a wind tunnel with a group of speed skaters, testing different suits.

Interviewer: How did you get into this field?

Tom: I was a keen runner at school, but I kept getting injured. My physiotherapist told me that my shoes were part of the problem. I was so annoyed that I started reading about how running shoes work, and I realised that I was more interested in the shoes than in the running. I studied mechanical engineering and then did a doctorate on the design of sports surfaces.

Interviewer: Has technology changed sport a lot?

Tom: Enormously. Think about the pole vault. A hundred years ago, the poles were made of wood, and athletes jumped about four metres. Today, with flexible fibreglass poles, the world record is over six metres. Or swimming: in 2008 and 2009, more than a hundred world records were broken by swimmers wearing new full-body suits. They were banned in 2010 because they gave an unfair advantage.

Interviewer: So where is the line between helping athletes and cheating?

Tom: That's the big question. Every sport has its own rules, and they are often decided by committees that include engineers like me. In general, we say that equipment should help athletes perform at their best, but it should not do the work for them. The skill must stay with the athlete.

Interviewer: Do you work only with top athletes?

Tom: No, and I think the most important work is for ordinary people. I'm currently working on playground surfaces that reduce injuries when children fall, and on cheaper running shoes for people in countries where most runners can't afford expensive brands.

Interviewer: What's the most unusual project you've worked on?

Tom: Probably designing a ball for blind footballers. It has small bells inside, so the players can hear where it is. The difficult part was making the bells loud enough without changing the way the ball bounces.

Interviewer: Finally, do you still run?

Tom: Every morning – in shoes I designed myself. And I haven't been injured for years.

A sports scientist

    A sports engineer.
  2. 1.What did Tom test in the wind tunnel?

  5. 4.What were pole vault poles made of a hundred years ago?
  6. 5.How many world records were broken in the new swimsuits?
  7. 6.Who decides the rules about equipment?
  8. 7.What must stay with the athlete?
  9. 8.Who are the cheaper running shoes for?
  10. 9.What is inside the ball for blind footballers?

2. His physiotherapist.
3. The design of sports surfaces.
4. Wood.
5. More than a hundred.
6. Committees (including engineers).
7. The skill.
8. People who can't afford expensive brands.
9. (Small) bells.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take

  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

»testing different suits«.
2. His physiotherapist.
»My physiotherapist told me«.
3. The design of sports surfaces.
»a doctorate on the design of sports surfaces«.
4. Wood.
»the poles were made of wood«.
5. More than a hundred.
»more than a hundred world records were broken«.

»decided by committees that include engineers like me«.

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

Your town's youth council organises an annual award, Young Volunteer of the Year, for a young person who has helped the local community. The awards committee is asking for nominations.

Write an email of 150–180 words to the awards committee in which you:

  • recommend and present the person you are nominating,
  • describe what he or she has done for the community,
  • explain why he or she deserves the award more than others.
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-pismo s priporočilom: nagovor odbora, uvod z namenom, predstavitev kandidata, konkretni dosežki v skupnosti, utemeljitev, zakaj si nagrado zasluži bolj kot drugi, formalen konec; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (150–180 words), formal style
  2. recommend and present the person you are nominating
  3. describe what he or she has done for the community
  4. explain why he or she deserves the award more than others
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba e-pisma s priporočilom
Dear Members of the Awards Committee,
Formalni nagovor; konec »Yours faithfully« ali nevtralno »Kind regards«.
I am writing to nominate my classmate Luka Novak for the Young Volunteer of the Year award.
Uvod: namen in kandidat.
Odstavek 1: predstavitev
Luka is an eighteen-year-old student who has volunteered for three years.
Iztočnica 1: kdo je kandidat.
Odstavek 2: kaj je naredil
He set up free maths tutoring for younger pupils and organised a clean-up of the riverbank with over 100 volunteers.
Iztočnica 2: konkretni dosežki s številkami.
Odstavek 3: zakaj si zasluži nagrado
Unlike many, he does not volunteer for his CV; his projects continue without him and have inspired others.
Iztočnica 3: primerjava z drugimi in utemeljitev (What makes him exceptional is …).
I strongly believe he would be a worthy winner. / Yours faithfully, / Ana Kovač
Formalen konec.
Višja raven: 150–180 besed; ocenjevalci pričakujejo prepričljiv jezik (outstanding, tireless, a role model).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Members of the Awards Committee,

I am writing to nominate my classmate Luka Novak for this year's Young Volunteer of the Year award.

Luka is an eighteen-year-old student at Gimnazija Celje who has devoted much of his free time to our community for the past three years.

Two years ago, he set up a free maths tutoring scheme for younger pupils who could not afford private lessons. Today, twelve students take part, and more than forty children receive help every week. Last spring, he also organised a clean-up of the riverbank, which attracted over a hundred volunteers and removed two tonnes of rubbish.

What makes Luka exceptional is not only what he has achieved, but how he has achieved it. Unlike many volunteers, he does not do it to improve his CV; he always gives credit to others. Most importantly, his projects will continue after he leaves school, because he has trained younger students to run them.

I strongly believe that Luka would be a worthy winner and a role model for young people.

Yours faithfully,
Ana Kovač

Število besed: 179 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss the importance of the island setting in William Golding's Lord of the Flies.

William Golding: Lord of the Flies

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo o otoku kot preizkušnji, podprto s prizori (otok kot raj, brazgotina v džungli, ploščad in školjka nasproti Castle Rock, požara), in s sklepom, da zlo izhaja iz dečkov samih; brez obnove; 250–300 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the importance of the island setting in William Golding's Lord of the Flies.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – the island is not just a background; it is a test that removes adult rules and reveals the boys' true nature.
Teza v uvodu, brez obnove.
Jedro 1 – the island as paradise: fruit, the lagoon, Ralph's joy at the absence of grown-ups; the scar in the jungle left by the crash.
Prizori iz prvih poglavij; brazgotina napoveduje uničenje.
Jedro 2 – different places, different values: the platform and the conch (order) versus Castle Rock and the forest (savagery).
Prostor kot simbol: kraji ustrezajo skupinam.
Jedro 3 – destruction of the island: the first fire, then the final fire that burns the whole island during the hunt for Ralph.
Paradiž, ki ga uničijo sami.
Sklep: by isolating the boys, the island shows that evil comes from within, not from the outside world.
Sklep se vrne k tezi.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The island in Lord of the Flies

William Golding's Lord of the Flies is set on a deserted tropical island where a group of British schoolboys are stranded after a plane crash. The island is far more than a background to the story. In my opinion, it is a kind of test: by removing all adult rules, it reveals what the boys are really like.

At first, the island seems like a paradise. There is fruit on the trees, a warm lagoon for swimming and no adults to give orders. Ralph is delighted when he realises that there are no grown-ups, and he stands on his head for joy. Yet there is already a warning sign: the "scar" that the crashed plane has torn through the jungle. From the very beginning, the boys' arrival damages the island.

As the story develops, different parts of the island come to represent different values. The platform by the beach, where the boys meet with the conch, stands for order and discussion. The dark forest, where Jack hunts, and Castle Rock, where his tribe finally lives, stand for violence and savagery. As more boys move to Castle Rock, the platform is gradually abandoned.

The boys also destroy the island itself. Their first signal fire gets out of control and burns part of the forest, and a small boy disappears. At the end, Jack's tribe sets the whole island on fire in order to hunt Ralph. Ironically, it is this fire that attracts the ship that rescues them.

In conclusion, the island isolates the boys from civilisation and shows that evil does not come from the outside world. The paradise is destroyed not by nature but by the boys themselves.

Število besed: 285 (zahtevanih 250–300). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Bakery on Mill Street

Nobody in our town could remember a time when there was no bakery on Mill Street. Mr Kovacs had opened it in 1972, a year after he arrived from Hungary with a suitcase, a few words of English and his grandmother's recipe for poppy-seed cake. By the time I was born, the smell of his bread was as much a part of the town as the church bells.

I started working there on Saturday mornings when I was fifteen. My job was to serve customers and clean the trays, but Mr Kovacs soon decided that I should learn to bake. "Anyone can sell bread," he said. "Not everyone can make it." He made me arrive at five in the morning, when the street was still dark and the only light came from the ovens.

He was a strict teacher. He never used a recipe book; everything was in his head and in his hands. When I asked him how much flour to use, he would say, "Enough." When I asked how long to knead the dough, he would say, "Until it is ready." For weeks I got it wrong. My loaves were flat, or hard, or burnt at the bottom. He threw them into a bag for the ducks in the park without a word.

Then one morning, after almost two months, he picked up one of my loaves, knocked on the bottom with his knuckles and listened. He nodded. "Good," he said. It was the only time he ever praised me, and I walked home feeling as if I had won a prize.

When I was eighteen, I left to study engineering in the capital. I came home less and less often. On one of my visits, I noticed that the bakery was closed in the afternoons, and Mr Kovacs looked much older. He told me that his hands were not strong any more, and that nobody wanted to work the early hours.

Two years later, my mother phoned to tell me that the bakery had closed. Mr Kovacs had sold the building to a phone company. I was surprised by how upset I was. That weekend I tried to bake his bread in my student flat. It was a disaster.

I finished my degree and worked as an engineer for three years. But I could not forget the bakery. Last year, I gave up my job, borrowed money from the bank and opened a small bakery of my own, in a street not far from Mill Street. On the first morning, an old man came in, bought a loaf, knocked on the bottom with his knuckles and listened. Then he smiled. It was Mr Kovacs.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.When did Mr Kovacs open the bakery?
    In 1972.
  2. 1.What did Mr Kovacs bring with him from Hungary apart from a suitcase?
  3. 2.What was the narrator's first job at the bakery?
  4. 3.Why did Mr Kovacs want the narrator to learn to bake?
  5. 4.Where did Mr Kovacs keep his recipes?
  6. 5.What happened to the narrator's bad loaves?
  7. 6.How did Mr Kovacs test the bread?
  8. 7.What did the narrator study?
  9. 8.Why was the bakery closed in the afternoons?
  10. 9.Who bought the bakery building?
  11. 10.How did the narrator pay for the new bakery?

2. Serving customers and cleaning (the) trays.
3. Not everyone can make bread.
4. In his head (and hands).
5. They were given to the ducks.
6. He knocked on the bottom and listened.
7. Engineering.
8. His hands were weak. / Nobody wanted to work early hours.
9. A phone company.
10. With a bank loan. / He borrowed money from the bank.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A recipe (for poppy-seed cake) / a few words of English.
Prinesel je kovček, nekaj besed angleščine in babičin recept; vprašanje izključi kovček.
2. Serving customers and cleaning (the) trays.
»My job was to serve customers and clean the trays«.
3. Not everyone can make bread.
»Anyone can sell bread. Not everyone can make it.«
4. In his head (and hands).
»everything was in his head and in his hands« – recepta ni zapisal.
5. They were given to the ducks.
Vrgel jih je v vrečo za race v parku.
6. He knocked on the bottom and listened.
»knocked on the bottom with his knuckles and listened«.
7. Engineering.
»I left to study engineering in the capital«.
8. His hands were weak. / Nobody wanted to work early hours.
Navedena sta dva razloga, dovolj je eden.
9. A phone company.
»Mr Kovacs had sold the building to a phone company«.
10. With a bank loan. / He borrowed money from the bank.
»borrowed money from the bank«.

The joy of being scared

Millions of people pay to be frightened. Psychologists are trying to understand why.

Every October, cinemas fill with people who want to be terrified by ghosts, zombies and serial killers, [0]. At first sight this seems strange. Fear is an unpleasant emotion, [1].

Psychologists believe that the answer lies in the difference between real and controlled danger. When we watch a horror film, our body reacts [2]: our heart beats faster, we breathe more quickly and we produce adrenaline. But our brain knows that we are sitting safely in a cinema seat.

This combination can be very pleasant. After the danger is over, the body releases chemicals [3]. Many viewers describe the end of a scary film as a kind of relief, [4].

Scary films can also bring people together. Watching a frightening scene with friends creates a shared experience, [5]. Some researchers even believe that couples who watch horror films together feel closer afterwards.

Not everyone enjoys being frightened, however. Studies show that people [6] are more likely to choose horror films. Others find them so disturbing that they cannot sleep for days.

Interestingly, horror fans may be better prepared for real crises. During the pandemic in 2020, a study found that people who regularly watched horror films felt less anxious, [7]. The researchers suggested that the films had given them a chance to practise dealing with fear in a safe environment.

Film makers know exactly how to manipulate our emotions. They use sudden loud noises, dark colours and music [8]. The most effective moments are often those in which nothing happens at all, because our imagination fills the silence with something worse.

So the next time you hide behind a cushion [9], remember that you are not alone. You are taking part in an ancient human tradition, [10].

  2. Bin the same way as it would in a dangerous situation
  3. Csimilar to the feeling after a roller coaster ride
  4. Dwho like new and exciting experiences
  5. Ethat makes viewers feel nervous before anything happens
  6. Fand most of us do everything we can to avoid it
  7. Gand the number of horror films grows every year
  8. Hwhich gives them something to talk about afterwards
  9. Ias old as telling ghost stories around a fire
  10. Jthan those who preferred comedies
  11. Kbecause the cinema was too expensive
  12. Lalthough most of them never saw a film again
  13. Mwhen the monster finally appears

2. B
3. A
4. C
5. H
6. D
7. J
8. E
9. M
10. I
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. F
»Fear is an unpleasant emotion« + »and most of us … avoid it« – logično nadaljevanje; poved pojasni, zakaj se zdi ljubezen do grozljivk čudna.
2. B
Telo se odzove »in the same way as it would in a dangerous situation« – sledi dvopičje z naštevanjem telesnih odzivov.
3. A
»releases chemicals« + oziralni stavek »which make us feel happy and relaxed« – kemikalije (množina, make).
4. C
Olajšanje po filmu primerjamo z občutkom po vožnji z vlakcem smrti.
5. H
Skupna izkušnja »which gives them something to talk about afterwards«.
6. D
»people [6] are more likely to choose« – ljudje, ki imajo radi nove in vznemirljive izkušnje.
7. J
Primerjava: ljubitelji grozljivk so bili manj tesnobni kot tisti, ki so raje gledali komedije (less anxious than …).
8. E
Glasba, »that makes viewers feel nervous before anything happens« – napoveduje naslednjo poved o tišini.
9. M
»hide behind a cushion [9]« – časovni odvisnik pove, kdaj se skrijemo: ko se končno pokaže pošast.
10. I
»an ancient human tradition, [10]« – tradicija, stara kot pripovedovanje zgodb o duhovih ob ognju.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. than
Primerjava: fewer than half.
2. are
Trpnik v sedanjiku, množina: are turned into.
3. which
Nedoločilni oziralni stavek (za vejico) za stvari: microplastics, which …
4. what
Vprašalni zaimek: So what can be done?
5. back
»get your money back« = dobiti denar nazaj.
6. since
Present perfect + točka v času: since 2003.
7. for
Stalna zveza »for free« = brezplačno.
8. it
Zaimek nadomešča »an alternative«.
9. from / of
»made from / of seaweed« = narejen iz alg.
10. scale
Stalna zveza »on a large scale« = v velikem obsegu.
11. a
Nedoločni člen pred »person«: the simplest things a person can do.
12. at
Stalna zveza »at least« = vsaj.
13. than
Primerjava: more aware … than previous generations.
14. from
»drink water from the tap« = piti vodo iz pipe.
15. with
Pregovor: every journey begins with a single step.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

A day in the life of a bicycle courier

Jake Morris (0) (WORK) as a bicycle courier in central London for the past six years. Every morning he (1) (LEAVE) his flat at seven o'clock and cycles to the company's office near Oxford Street, where the first deliveries are already waiting.

"Most people think it's a simple job, but it's actually very demanding," he says. "On an average day I (2) (RIDE) about a hundred kilometres. Yesterday I (3) (DELIVER) forty-two packages, and I only stopped for lunch once."

Jake started the job when he (4) (STUDY) art at university. He needed extra money, and a friend (5) (SUGGEST) that he try cycling deliveries. "I thought I (6) (DO) it for a few months," he laughs. "I never imagined it would become my career."

The job has changed a lot since he started. "When I first joined, we (7) (USE) paper maps and radios. Now everything (8) (CONTROL) by an app, which tells us exactly where to go." The app also measures how fast the couriers are, and Jake admits that this can be stressful. "If you are too slow, you (9) (NOT / GET) the best jobs."

The most dangerous part of the job is the traffic. Two years ago, Jake (10) (HIT) by a taxi while he (11) (WAIT) at traffic lights. He broke his arm and could not work for three months. "Since then, I (12) (ALWAYS / WEAR) a helmet and bright clothes," he says. "Many cyclists don't, which is crazy."

Despite the risks, Jake loves his job. "I (13) (NOT / WANT) to sit in an office all day. Here I'm outside, I'm fit and I know every street in London." He also has plans for the future. Next year he (14) (OPEN) his own delivery company, using electric cargo bikes. "If cities (15) (BAN) more cars from their centres, bikes will become even more important."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. has worked / has been working

2. ride
3. delivered

5. suggested
6. would do
7. used
8. is controlled

13. don't want / wouldn't want

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. leaves
Navada v sedanjosti (Every morning): present simple, 3. oseba ednine.
2. ride
Splošna resnica o povprečnem dnevu: present simple.
3. delivered
»Yesterday« – zaključen čas v preteklosti: past simple.
4. was studying
Dejanje, ki je trajalo, ko je začel delati: past continuous.
5. suggested
Zaključeno dejanje v preteklosti: past simple.
6. would do
Prihodnost v preteklosti (I thought …): would + nedoločnik.
7. used
Preteklo stanje, ki ga ni več: past simple (ali used to use).
8. is controlled
Trpnik v sedanjiku: everything is controlled by an app.
9. don't get / won't get
Splošno pravilo (prvi pogojnik ali ničti pogojnik): don't get ali won't get.
10. was hit
Trpnik v pretekliku: zadel ga je taksi.
11. was waiting
»while« + dejanje v teku: past continuous.
12. have always worn
»Since then« – od takrat do zdaj: present perfect; prislov always stoji pred deležnikom.
13. don't want / wouldn't want
Sedanje stališče: present simple (ali hipotetično wouldn't want).
14. is going to open / will open / is opening
Načrt za prihodnost: going to ali present continuous za dogovorjene načrte.
15. ban
Prvi pogojnik: v odvisniku z if stoji present simple (If cities ban …, bikes will …).

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with a historian, Dr Ruth Ellis, about Inge Lehmann, the Danish scientist who discovered the Earth's inner core. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Ellis, most people have never heard of Inge Lehmann. Who was she?

Ruth: She was a Danish seismologist – a scientist who studies earthquakes – and in 1936 she made one of the most important discoveries about our planet: that the Earth has a solid inner core. Before her, scientists believed the centre of the Earth was completely liquid.

Interviewer: How did she become a scientist?

Ruth: She was lucky with her school. She was born in Copenhagen in 1888 and went to a school run by a remarkable woman who believed that girls and boys should be taught exactly the same subjects, including mathematics. That was very unusual at the time. Later she studied maths at university, but she didn't start working on earthquakes until she was in her late thirties.

Interviewer: How did she make her discovery?

Ruth: By looking very carefully at records of earthquakes, especially a strong one in New Zealand in 1929. When an earthquake happens, it sends waves through the Earth. Lehmann noticed that some waves appeared in places where, according to the theory, they shouldn't have been detected at all. The only explanation was that they had bounced off something solid deep inside the planet.

Interviewer: Did she have a computer to help her?

Ruth: No, nothing like that. She wrote the data on small pieces of cardboard and kept them in empty boxes of oatmeal. She would spread the cards over her kitchen table and move them around until she saw a pattern.

Interviewer: How was her discovery received?

Ruth: Surprisingly well, actually. The leading scientists of the day accepted her idea within a few years. But as a woman she found it difficult to get a senior position. She worked for many years at the Danish geodetic institute, but she was never made its director, although she had more experience than anyone else.

Interviewer: What was she like as a person?

Ruth: Very independent and quite direct. She once wrote to a colleague: "You should know how many incompetent men I had to compete with – in vain." She also loved gardening and travelling, and she continued doing research until she was nearly a hundred.

Interviewer: She lived that long?

Ruth: She died in 1993, at the age of 104. In her nineties she was still publishing papers. Today, an important prize for geophysics is named after her, which I think she would have found both amusing and well deserved.

A forgotten scientist

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.What did Inge Lehmann discover?
    The Earth's (solid) inner core.
  2. 1.What does a seismologist study?
  3. 2.What did scientists believe about the centre of the Earth before 1936?
  4. 3.What was unusual about Inge Lehmann's school?
  5. 4.Where did the earthquake that helped her discovery happen?
  6. 5.What did Lehmann write her data on?
  7. 6.Where did she keep her data cards?
  8. 7.Which position was Lehmann never given?
  9. 8.Name one of Lehmann's hobbies.
  10. 9.How old was Lehmann when she died?

1. Earthquakes.
2. That it was (completely) liquid.
3. Girls and boys were taught the same subjects.
4. In New Zealand (in 1929).
5. (Small pieces of) cardboard.
6. In (empty) oatmeal boxes.
7. Director (of the institute).
8. Gardening / travelling.
9. 104.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

»a scientist who studies earthquakes«.

»scientists believed the centre of the Earth was completely liquid«.

Ravnateljica je verjela, da se morajo dekleta in fantje učiti enake predmete.

»a strong one in New Zealand in 1929«.

»She wrote the data on small pieces of cardboard«.

»kept them in empty boxes of oatmeal«.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Professor Mark Delaney, a volcanologist, about his life and work. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Professor Delaney, how did you become interested in volcanoes?

Mark: Through a holiday disaster. When I was twelve, my family went camping in Italy, near Mount Etna. On the third night there was a small eruption. Everybody else was frightened, but I stood outside the tent in my pyjamas, watching the red glow in the sky. My parents had to drag me back inside.

Interviewer: And then you decided to study volcanoes?

Mark: Not straight away. I was actually more interested in history at school. But at university I took a geology course just because it fitted into my timetable, and on the first field trip, to the island of Santorini, I realised that I could combine both. Volcanoes have shaped human history – they have destroyed cities, changed the climate and even caused famines.

Interviewer: What does a typical working day look like?

Mark: There's no such thing! Some weeks I'm in the lab analysing rock samples. Other weeks I'm on a volcano, collecting gas with special equipment. We measure the gases that come out of the crater, because changes in their chemistry can tell us that an eruption is coming.

Interviewer: Is it dangerous?

Mark: It can be, but we take a lot of precautions. We wear gas masks and heat-resistant clothing, and we never work alone. The biggest danger is not lava, which usually moves slowly, but the clouds of hot gas and ash that can travel at hundreds of kilometres an hour.

Interviewer: Can scientists predict eruptions?

Mark: We're much better than we were thirty years ago. In 2010, for example, we knew weeks in advance that the volcano in Iceland was going to erupt. What we can't predict very well is how big an eruption will be, or how long it will last. That ash cloud closed European airspace for six days, and nobody had expected that.

Interviewer: What's the most beautiful thing you've seen?

Mark: A lava lake in Ethiopia, at night. It looks like the surface of the sun, moving and breaking apart. I sat on the edge of the crater for hours.

Interviewer: Any advice for young people?

Mark: Learn languages. Most active volcanoes are in countries where English isn't the first language, and you'll do much better work if you can talk to the people who live there.

Life on a volcano

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Mark first saw an eruption in Italy. (T)
  2. 1.Mark was frightened by the eruption he saw as a child. T / F
  3. 2.At school, Mark preferred history to science. T / F
  4. 3.Mark chose geology at university because it fitted into his timetable. T / F
  5. 4.Mark spends all his working time on volcanoes. T / F
  6. 5.Changes in volcanic gases can warn scientists of an eruption. T / F
  7. 6.According to Mark, lava is the greatest danger. T / F
  8. 7.Scientists can predict exactly how long an eruption will last. T / F
  9. 8.The ash cloud from Iceland closed European airspace for almost a week. T / F
  10. 9.Mark advises young people to learn foreign languages. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. F
2. T
3. T
4. F
5. T
6. F
7. F
8. T
9. T
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

Vsi drugi so bili prestrašeni, on pa je navdušeno gledal.
2. T
»I was actually more interested in history at school.«
3. T
»just because it fitted into my timetable«.
4. F
Nekatere tedne dela v laboratoriju.
5. T
»changes in their chemistry can tell us that an eruption is coming«.
6. F
Največja nevarnost so oblaki vročega plina in pepela.
7. F
»What we can't predict very well is how big an eruption will be, or how long it will last.«
8. T
Zračni prostor je bil zaprt šest dni.
9. T
»Learn languages.«

deli.A: A) PISNI SESTAVEK (V ENI OD STALNIH SPOROČANJSKIH OBLIK)

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

Your school is planning to shorten the lunch break from forty-five to twenty minutes so that lessons can finish earlier. Many students are unhappy about the decision.

As the student representative, write an e-mail of 120–150 words to the school's headmaster, in which you

  • explain why students are against the change,
  • describe how the lunch break is used at the moment,
  • suggest a solution that would be acceptable to both students and teachers.
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-pismo ravnatelju z nagovorom, uvodom z namenom, razlogi proti spremembi, opisom sedanje rabe odmora, kompromisnim predlogom in formalnim koncem; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. explain why students are against the change
  3. describe how the lunch break is used at the moment
  4. suggest a solution that would be acceptable to both students and teachers
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba formalnega e-pisma
Dear Mr Novak,
Ravnatelja nagovoriš s priimkom; konec Yours sincerely.
I am writing on behalf of the students to express our concern about the plan to shorten the lunch break.
Uvod: kdo piše in zakaj.
Odstavek 1: zakaj so proti
Twenty minutes is not enough to queue for lunch and eat; students would have no time to rest.
Iztočnica 1: razlogi.
Odstavek 2: kako ga uporabljamo zdaj
Students eat in the canteen, meet in clubs, visit the library or prepare for tests.
Iztočnica 2: opis s konkretnimi dejavnostmi.
Odstavek 3: predlog
A thirty-minute break and a shorter morning break would let lessons finish only ten minutes later.
Iztočnica 3: kompromis (We would like to suggest …).
I hope you will consider our suggestion. / Yours sincerely, / Ana Kovač, Student Representative
Formalen konec.
Preštej besede (120–150). Vljuden, a odločen ton.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Mr Novak,

I am writing on behalf of the students to express our concern about the plan to shorten the lunch break from forty-five to twenty minutes.

Most students are against the change because twenty minutes is simply not enough. The queue in the canteen often takes ten minutes, so there would be almost no time to eat, let alone to rest before afternoon lessons.

At the moment, the lunch break is used in many different ways. Apart from eating, students meet in clubs, borrow books from the library, ask teachers for help or prepare for tests.

We would therefore like to suggest a compromise. The lunch break could be shortened to thirty minutes, and the morning break could be reduced by five minutes. In this way, lessons would finish only ten minutes later than planned.

I hope you will consider our suggestion.

Yours sincerely,
Ana Kovač, Student Representative

Število besed: 150 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče (I largely agree that …).
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1: argument + primer (education abroad, Erasmus, the internet).
Konkretni primeri.
Jedro 2: argument + primer (travel, information, new professions).
Povezovalci.
Jedro 3: protiargument (housing is more expensive, jobs are less secure … However …).
Uravnoteženost.
Sklep: povzemi stališče.
Brez novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For closing: animals suffer in small spaces, they cannot behave naturally. Against: breeding endangered species, education, research.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Young people today have more opportunities than their parents had.

When my parents were my age, Slovenia was part of Yugoslavia, few people had a telephone at home, and travelling abroad was an adventure. Compared with them, I believe that young people today have many more opportunities, although life is not easier in every way.

Firstly, education offers far more choice. Students can spend a semester abroad through Erasmus, take online courses from the best universities in the world and learn almost anything from the internet. My mother told me that she had to wait months for a book from the library.

Secondly, the world is more open. Young people can travel, work and study in any country of the European Union, and many new professions, such as app developer or social media manager, did not exist thirty years ago.

On the other hand, some things have become more difficult. Flats are much more expensive than they used to be, and many young people have temporary jobs, so they live with their parents until their thirties. Competition for good jobs is also very strong.

In conclusion, I agree that we have more opportunities than our parents, especially in education and travel. However, having more choices does not automatically mean having an easier life, and our generation faces challenges that our parents never imagined.

Število besed: 223 (zahtevanih 220–250). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

The Woman Who Climbed in a Skirt

In the summer of 1871, a thirty-five-year-old Englishwoman called Lucy Walker became the first woman to climb the Matterhorn, one of the most dangerous mountains in the Alps. Only six years earlier, four men had died on its slopes during the first ascent. Lucy reached the summit wearing a long white dress, which she refused to take off even on the steepest rock.

Lucy had started climbing almost by accident. She suffered from rheumatism, and a doctor had advised her to go walking in the mountains for her health. Her father and brother were enthusiastic climbers, and in 1858 she joined them in Switzerland with a local guide, Melchior Anderegg. The first climb was meant to be a gentle walk, but Lucy loved it so much that she returned every summer for the next twenty years.

At the time, climbing was considered completely unsuitable for women. Ladies were expected to stay in their hotels while the men went up the mountains, and those who did climb were often criticised in the newspapers. Lucy simply ignored the comments. She never gave interviews and did not write about her achievements, which is one reason why she is not better known today.

Her diet was as unusual as her hobby. According to her companions, she lived almost entirely on sponge cake and champagne while climbing, which she believed gave her energy. Anderegg, who guided her on nearly all her climbs, said she was one of the most reliable climbers he had ever worked with. She never complained, never panicked and always knew exactly where to put her feet.

In total, Lucy completed ninety-eight climbs, including several first ascents by a woman. Her achievement on the Matterhorn caused a sensation. It was even celebrated in a poem in the satirical magazine Punch, which praised her for showing that women could do as well as men. Interestingly, she climbed the Matterhorn only a few weeks before her American rival, Meta Brevoort, who had hoped to be the first.

Later in life, Lucy became the second president of the Ladies' Alpine Club, founded in London in 1907 because the original Alpine Club did not accept women. It would be almost seventy years before women were allowed to join the men's club as full members.

Lucy Walker died in 1916. She never married, and in her later years she rarely spoke about the mountains. Today, however, she is recognised as a pioneer who opened the way for generations of female climbers.

The intelligence of the octopus

The more scientists learn about octopuses, the stranger they seem.

Octopuses have fascinated humans for thousands of years. Ancient Greek writers described them as clever and cunning. [0] Today, scientists agree that octopuses are among the most intelligent animals on Earth.

What makes this so surprising is that octopuses are very different from us. They are molluscs, closely related to snails and clams. [1] Our last common ancestor was probably a simple worm-like creature that lived about six hundred million years ago.

Their brains are also organised in an unusual way. An octopus has about five hundred million nerve cells, a similar number to a dog. [2] This means that each arm can, to some extent, taste, touch and make decisions on its own.

In laboratories, octopuses have shown remarkable abilities. They can open jars to get food, find their way through mazes and recognise individual people. [3] In one aquarium, an octopus repeatedly turned off a light that annoyed it by squirting water at it, causing the electricity to fail.

They are also masters of disguise. Using special cells in their skin, octopuses can change colour in less than a second. [4] Some species even imitate other animals, such as poisonous fish or sea snakes, to frighten away predators.

Perhaps the most mysterious thing about octopuses is how short their lives are. [5] Most species live for only one or two years, and females die soon after their eggs hatch. Scientists are still trying to understand how such a short-lived animal developed such a complex mind.

This intelligence raises difficult questions. [6] In several countries, there are plans to open the first octopus farms, which would produce thousands of tonnes of octopus meat every year. Animal welfare groups argue that it would be cruel to keep such curious animals in small, empty tanks.

In 2021, a British government report concluded that octopuses can feel pain and suffer. [7] As a result, they are now protected by animal welfare laws in the United Kingdom, just like mammals and birds.

For many people, the 2020 documentary My Octopus Teacher changed the way they see these animals. [8] It showed a man forming a close relationship with a wild octopus in a South African kelp forest over a whole year. [9]

Whatever the future of octopus farming, one thing is clear. [10]

  12. LUnfortunately, octopuses cannot learn from experience.

Po opisu filma: mnogi gledalci so rekli, da hobotnice ne bodo več jedli.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with a historian, Dr Ruth Ellis, about Inge Lehmann, the Danish scientist who discovered the Earth's inner core. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Ellis, most people have never heard of Inge Lehmann. Who was she?

Ruth: She was a Danish seismologist – a scientist who studies earthquakes – and in 1936 she made one of the most important discoveries about our planet: that the Earth has a solid inner core. Before her, scientists believed the centre of the Earth was completely liquid.

Interviewer: How did she become a scientist?

Ruth: She was lucky with her school. She was born in Copenhagen in 1888 and went to a school run by a remarkable woman who believed that girls and boys should be taught exactly the same subjects, including mathematics. That was very unusual at the time. Later she studied maths at university, but she didn't start working on earthquakes until she was in her late thirties.

Interviewer: How did she make her discovery?

Ruth: By looking very carefully at records of earthquakes, especially a strong one in New Zealand in 1929. When an earthquake happens, it sends waves through the Earth. Lehmann noticed that some waves appeared in places where, according to the theory, they shouldn't have been detected at all. The only explanation was that they had bounced off something solid deep inside the planet.

Interviewer: Did she have a computer to help her?

Ruth: No, nothing like that. She wrote the data on small pieces of cardboard and kept them in empty boxes of oatmeal. She would spread the cards over her kitchen table and move them around until she saw a pattern.

Interviewer: How was her discovery received?

Ruth: Surprisingly well, actually. The leading scientists of the day accepted her idea within a few years. But as a woman she found it difficult to get a senior position. She worked for many years at the Danish geodetic institute, but she was never made its director, although she had more experience than anyone else.

Interviewer: What was she like as a person?

Ruth: Very independent and quite direct. She once wrote to a colleague: "You should know how many incompetent men I had to compete with – in vain." She also loved gardening and travelling, and she continued doing research until she was nearly a hundred.

Interviewer: She lived that long?

Ruth: She died in 1993, at the age of 104. In her nineties she was still publishing papers. Today, an important prize for geophysics is named after her, which I think she would have found both amusing and well deserved.

A forgotten scientist

  6. 5.Some waves appeared in places where they ____.
  7. 6.The waves had bounced off something ____ inside the planet.
  8. 7.She looked for patterns by moving cards around on ____.
  9. 8.The leading scientists accepted her idea within ____.
  10. 9.Today, an important prize for ____ is named after her.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Professor Mark Delaney, a volcanologist, about his life and work. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Professor Delaney, how did you become interested in volcanoes?

Mark: Through a holiday disaster. When I was twelve, my family went camping in Italy, near Mount Etna. On the third night there was a small eruption. Everybody else was frightened, but I stood outside the tent in my pyjamas, watching the red glow in the sky. My parents had to drag me back inside.

Interviewer: And then you decided to study volcanoes?

Mark: Not straight away. I was actually more interested in history at school. But at university I took a geology course just because it fitted into my timetable, and on the first field trip, to the island of Santorini, I realised that I could combine both. Volcanoes have shaped human history – they have destroyed cities, changed the climate and even caused famines.

Interviewer: What does a typical working day look like?

Mark: There's no such thing! Some weeks I'm in the lab analysing rock samples. Other weeks I'm on a volcano, collecting gas with special equipment. We measure the gases that come out of the crater, because changes in their chemistry can tell us that an eruption is coming.

Interviewer: Is it dangerous?

Mark: It can be, but we take a lot of precautions. We wear gas masks and heat-resistant clothing, and we never work alone. The biggest danger is not lava, which usually moves slowly, but the clouds of hot gas and ash that can travel at hundreds of kilometres an hour.

Interviewer: Can scientists predict eruptions?

Mark: We're much better than we were thirty years ago. In 2010, for example, we knew weeks in advance that the volcano in Iceland was going to erupt. What we can't predict very well is how big an eruption will be, or how long it will last. That ash cloud closed European airspace for six days, and nobody had expected that.

Interviewer: What's the most beautiful thing you've seen?

Mark: A lava lake in Ethiopia, at night. It looks like the surface of the sun, moving and breaking apart. I sat on the edge of the crater for hours.

Interviewer: Any advice for young people?

Mark: Learn languages. Most active volcanoes are in countries where English isn't the first language, and you'll do much better work if you can talk to the people who live there.

Life on a volcano
