naloge.besedilo:
Report

Your school took part in a two-week exchange programme with a partner school in Ireland. As a member of the student council, you have been asked to report on the exchange to the head teacher.

Write a report of 150–180 words in which you

  • describe the activities that the visiting students took part in,
  • evaluate the success of the exchange,
  • recommend changes for the next exchange.
To: Head Teacher
From: Ana Kovač, Student Council
Subject: Exchange with our Irish partner school
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, namenom, odstavki s podnaslovi (dejavnosti, ocena uspeha, priporočila) in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (150–180 words), formal style
  2. describe the activities that the visiting students took part in
  3. evaluate the success of the exchange
  4. recommend changes for the next exchange
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Head Teacher / From: Ana Kovač, Student Council / Subject: Exchange with St Brigid's School, Galway
Glava in uvod z namenom.
Activities
The Irish students attended lessons, visited Ljubljana and Lake Bled, and took part in a cooking workshop.
Iztočnica 1: pregled dejavnosti.
Evaluation
Most participants felt the exchange improved their English and helped them make lasting friendships; however, some host families found the timetable tiring.
Iztočnica 2: uravnotežena ocena s podatki (According to a survey, 90% …).
Recommendations
I would recommend fewer long trips and more joint projects, as well as an online meeting before the visit.
Iztočnica 3: konkretna predloga z utemeljitvijo.
Conclusion: The exchange was a success and should be continued.
Formalen slog, trpnik.
Preštej besede (150–180).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Head Teacher
From: Ana Kovač, Student Council
Subject: Exchange with St Brigid's School, Galway

Introduction

The purpose of this report is to evaluate the two-week exchange with our partner school in Galway, which took place in March.

Activities

The twelve Irish students attended lessons with their hosts and gave a presentation about Irish culture. They also visited Ljubljana, Lake Bled and the Postojna Cave, and took part in a cooking workshop, where they learned to make potica.

Evaluation

According to a short survey, over ninety per cent of the participants felt that the exchange had improved their English and their confidence. Several lasting friendships were formed. However, some host families found the timetable too demanding, as there were activities almost every evening.

Recommendations

I would recommend organising fewer long excursions and more joint projects, for example a short film made by mixed teams. It would also be useful to arrange an online meeting before the visit, so that students could get to know each other.

Conclusion

Overall, the exchange was a great success and should definitely be continued.

Število besed: 179 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss how the pigs use language to control the other animals in George Orwell's Animal Farm.

George Orwell: Animal Farm

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo, da prašiči nadzorujejo živali z jezikom, podprto s primeri (Squealer in njegove razlage, spreminjanje sedmih zapovedi, gesla, prepoved Beasts of England); brez obnove; 250–300 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss how the pigs use language to control the other animals in George Orwell's Animal Farm.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – in Animal Farm, the pigs gain power not mainly by force but by controlling language: they change words, rules and memories.
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1 – Squealer: 'he could turn black into white'; statistics about food production; the explanation why the pigs need milk and apples.
Konkretni prizori.
Jedro 2 – the Seven Commandments are secretly changed ('No animal shall sleep in a bed with sheets'); the final 'All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others'.
Pokaži postopno spreminjanje pravil.
Jedro 3 – slogans and songs: 'Four legs good, two legs bad' drowns out discussion; 'Beasts of England' is banned.
Jezik onemogoči razmišljanje.
Sklep: Orwell shows that those who control language control the truth.
Sklep razširi tezo.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The power of language in Animal Farm

In George Orwell's Animal Farm, the animals drive out their cruel owner, Mr Jones, and try to build a society in which all animals are equal. Soon, however, the pigs take control. In my opinion, the pigs gain power not mainly through violence, but by controlling language. They change words, rules and even the animals' memories.

The most important tool of the pigs is Squealer, who, as the narrator says, "could turn black into white". When the other animals discover that the pigs are taking all the milk and apples, Squealer explains that pigs need them for their brains and that they are making a sacrifice for everyone. Later, he reads out long lists of figures proving that food production has increased, even though the animals are hungrier than ever.

The pigs also secretly change the Seven Commandments painted on the barn wall. When they move into the farmhouse, "No animal shall sleep in a bed" becomes "No animal shall sleep in a bed with sheets". Because the animals cannot remember the original words clearly, they believe that they were mistaken. At the end, a single commandment remains: "All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others."

Simple slogans make discussion impossible. Whenever someone tries to object at a meeting, the sheep start bleating "Four legs good, two legs bad" for several minutes. Even the song Beasts of England, which expresses the animals' dream of freedom, is finally banned and replaced by a new song written by the pig Minimus.

In conclusion, Orwell shows that those who control language also control the truth. The animals lose their freedom because they lose the words to defend it.

Read the text below and choose the correct answer (A, B, C or D). There is an example at the beginning (0).

The Stranger on the Train

I was seventeen and travelling alone for the first time, from Ljubljana to Munich, to spend the summer with my aunt. My mother had packed enough sandwiches for a week and given me a list of instructions that I promised to read and then forgot in my pocket. I had a window seat, a new book and the feeling that my real life was finally starting.

At Villach, an old woman got on and sat opposite me. She was small and very thin, with white hair tied back in a scarf, and she carried a shopping bag from which a loaf of bread was sticking out. She smiled at me, said something in German that I did not understand, and then took out a pair of knitting needles and began to work on what looked like a very long red sock.

For an hour neither of us spoke. I pretended to read, but in fact I was watching her hands, which moved so quickly that the needles seemed to fly. Every so often she held up the sock, looked at it critically and nodded to herself.

Somewhere in the Alps, the train stopped. Ten minutes passed, then twenty. An announcement was made in German, and everyone in the carriage groaned. I had no idea what was happening. The old woman looked at my worried face, put down her knitting and said, in slow, careful English, "A tree. On the line. Maybe one hour." Then she opened her shopping bag, broke the loaf in two and gave me half.

We ate the bread with my mother's sandwiches, and she told me her story in a mixture of German, English and gestures. She had been born in a village not far from where we had stopped. During the war, when she was nine, she had been sent to live with strangers in a city she did not know. She had travelled on this same line, alone, with a label tied to her coat. "I cried all the way," she said. "Then a soldier gave me an apple. I never forgot him."

When the train finally moved again, she went back to her knitting. At Salzburg she stood up, put the finished sock into my hands and said, "For your journey." Before I could answer, she was gone.

I still have the sock. It is far too long for any foot, and I have never worn it. But whenever I see someone travelling alone, looking lost, I think of her, and I try to be the person with the apple.

Five unusual festivals around Europe

Readers tell us about the strangest celebrations they have attended.

A La Tomatina, Spain

Every August, about twenty thousand people gather in the small town of Buñol to throw tomatoes at each other. The battle lasts exactly one hour and starts when a ham is pulled down from the top of a greasy pole. Afterwards, the whole town is red, and fire engines wash the streets. Tickets are now required, because the number of visitors had become dangerous. Wear old clothes and goggles – the tomato juice really hurts your eyes.

B Cheese Rolling, England

On a steep hill in Gloucestershire, competitors chase a large round cheese down a slope so steep that it is almost impossible to stay on your feet. The cheese can reach speeds of over a hundred kilometres an hour, so nobody actually catches it; the winner is the first person to cross the finish line. Injuries are common, and there are always ambulances waiting at the bottom. The tradition is at least two hundred years old, and the prize is the cheese itself.

C Kurentovanje, Slovenia

In February, the town of Ptuj is filled with kurenti, figures wearing heavy sheepskin costumes, masks with long red tongues and large cowbells around their waists. They dance through the streets to chase away winter and welcome spring. The costumes weigh up to twenty kilograms, and wearing one for a whole day is exhausting. The festival is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage, and it attracts visitors from all over Europe.

D Up Helly Aa, Scotland

On the Shetland Islands, the darkest weeks of winter end with a fire festival. Hundreds of men dressed as Vikings march through the town of Lerwick carrying burning torches and then set fire to a full-size Viking ship. Preparations take a whole year. Until recently, only men could take part in the procession, but after a long campaign, women were finally allowed to join in 2023, which divided opinion on the islands.

E Battle of the Oranges, Italy

In the town of Ivrea, teams on foot throw oranges at people riding in horse-drawn carts, who represent the soldiers of a cruel medieval ruler. The battle commemorates a revolt by the townspeople centuries ago. Spectators who do not want to be hit wear a red hat, which shows that they are not taking part. Around four hundred tonnes of oranges are used every year, most of them brought from the south of Italy.

  9. 8.At which festival is medical help always available?
  10. 9.Which festival requires long preparation?
  11. 10.Where does the writer give practical advice about clothing?
  12. 11.Which festival's costumes are physically demanding to wear?
  13. 12.Which festival uses produce transported from another region?

Why schools should teach children to fail

When we think of successful people, we usually imagine a straight road from talent to triumph. In reality, almost every success story is full (0) failures. The inventor James Dyson built 5,127 prototypes of his vacuum cleaner before he got one that worked. J. K. Rowling's first Harry Potter book was rejected by twelve publishers. Yet many young people today are so afraid (1) making mistakes that they avoid taking risks altogether.

Teachers and psychologists have noticed this trend. "Many of my students would rather not try at (2) than try and fail," says one secondary school teacher in Manchester. "They see a bad mark as proof that they are not clever, instead of as information about (3) they need to practise."

Part of the problem, experts say, is the way we praise children. When parents tell a child that he or she is "so clever", the child may begin to believe that intelligence is something you either have (4) you don't. Research by the American psychologist Carol Dweck has shown that children (5) are praised for their effort, rather than for their intelligence, are more willing to tackle difficult problems. Dweck calls this a "growth mindset": the belief that abilities can be developed through hard work.

Some schools are now trying to put this idea into practice. A girls' school in London organised a "failure week", (6) which teachers talked about their own mistakes and students were encouraged to try activities they had never done before, (7) juggling or public speaking. Other schools reward pupils not only (8) correct answers but also for interesting mistakes that help the class understand a problem.

Not everyone is convinced. Critics say that the idea of a growth mindset has become too popular too quickly, and that some studies have not been able to repeat Dweck's results. They also warn that telling children that failure is good may encourage them to take school less seriously. "Failure is only useful (9) you learn from it," says one psychologist.

Most experts agree, however, that a certain amount of failure is a normal and necessary part of learning. Children who are protected from every disappointment may find it much harder to cope (10) problems later in life. "If you never fall off your bike," says one head teacher, "you never learn to ride (11)."

Parents can help, too. Instead of solving every problem for their children, they can let them struggle a little, ask them what they could do differently and talk openly about their own mistakes. Even something (12) simple as playing board games, where children learn to lose, can make a difference.

Perhaps the most important lesson is that failure says nothing about a person's value. As the basketball player Michael Jordan once said, "I've failed over and (13) again in my life. And that is why I succeed." It is a message that many schools are now trying to pass (14) to the next generation. After all, the only people who never fail are those who never try anything new (15) all.

Sixty-nine days underground

On 5 August 2010, the San José copper mine in northern Chile (0) (COLLAPSE). Thirty-three miners were trapped seven hundred metres underground, and most people believed that none of them (1) (SURVIVE).

For seventeen days, nobody on the surface knew whether the men were alive. Rescue teams (2) (DRILL) narrow holes deep into the rock, hoping to reach the small shelter where the miners might be hiding. Meanwhile, families (3) (SET) up a camp outside the mine, which they called "Camp Hope".

Underground, the miners (4) (ORGANISE) themselves carefully. Their supervisor, Luis Urzúa, divided the tiny amount of food so that each man (5) (RECEIVE) two spoonfuls of tuna and half a glass of milk every forty-eight hours. They (6) (DRINK) water from tanks used to cool the machines.

On 22 August, a drill finally broke through into the shelter. When the rescuers pulled it back up, they (7) (FIND) a note attached to it, written in red ink: "We are fine in the shelter, the 33 of us." The whole country celebrated. Since that moment, the phrase (8) (BECOME) famous all over the world.

But the hardest part was still to come. Engineers said that it (9) (TAKE) several months to drill a hole wide enough to bring the men up. Through a small tube, the miners (10) (SEND) food, medicine, letters and even a video camera, so they could talk to their families.

While three different drilling teams (11) (WORK) day and night, NASA experts gave advice on how to keep the men healthy, both physically and mentally. A special capsule, called Phoenix, (12) (BUILD) to carry them to the surface one by one.

On 13 October, after sixty-nine days underground, the first miner (13) (LIFT) out of the mine as more than a billion people watched on television. The last man to leave was Urzúa himself. "I (14) (NEVER / WANT) to be in that situation again," he said, "but I am proud of what we did together." If the men had not stayed united, many experts believe, they (15) (NOT / SURVIVE).

You will listen to an interview with Nina Clarke, an underwater photographer. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Nina, you've spent more than twenty years photographing the oceans. How did it begin?

Nina: In a swimming pool in Birmingham, of all places! I was a very nervous swimmer as a child, and my mother signed me up for lessons to help me get over my fear. The teacher let us try a mask and snorkel at the end of each lesson, and I was amazed by how quiet and peaceful it was under the water. I've been trying to get back to that feeling ever since.

Interviewer: When did you start taking pictures?

Nina: At sixteen. I saved money from my Saturday job in a supermarket and bought a cheap waterproof camera. My first photos were terrible – mostly blue water and blurry fish – but I learned that patience matters more than equipment. You have to wait for the animals to come to you.

Interviewer: What is the most difficult thing about your job?

Nina: The light. Water absorbs colour very quickly. At only ten metres, almost all the red has disappeared, so everything looks blue or green. I use strong lights to bring the colours back. The other problem is time: on a normal dive I have about forty-five minutes before I have to go up, so I might get one good picture in a whole day.

Interviewer: Which photograph are you proudest of?

Nina: A picture of a mother humpback whale and her calf in the waters near Tonga. We spent eleven days on a boat waiting for them. On the last morning, they swam right up to me, and the calf looked straight into my camera. That picture won an international prize and was used on the cover of a book about ocean protection.

Interviewer: Have you seen the oceans change?

Nina: Dramatically. When I started diving in the Red Sea, the coral was full of life. Now, in many places, it is grey and broken. I also see plastic on almost every dive, even in places hundreds of kilometres from the nearest town. It's heartbreaking.

Interviewer: Do you think photographs can make a difference?

Nina: I hope so. Most people will never see a coral reef with their own eyes. If my pictures help them fall in love with the ocean, they might be more willing to protect it. I give talks in schools every month, and the children always ask the best questions.

Interviewer: What would you like to photograph next?

Nina: The giant squid. Very few people have ever seen one alive. It lives at depths where no diver can go, so I'm working with scientists on a special camera that can be lowered on a cable.

An underwater photographer

You will listen to two historians, Helen Shaw and Robert Price, talking about Charles Darwin's voyage on the Beagle. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Helen, Darwin was only twenty-two when he joined the Beagle. How did he get the chance?

Helen: Almost by luck. The captain, Robert FitzRoy, wanted a gentleman companion for the long voyage, someone educated to talk to at dinner, because captains were not supposed to socialise with the crew. Darwin's teacher at Cambridge recommended him. His father was against it at first – he thought it was a waste of time – and only Darwin's uncle persuaded him to change his mind.

Presenter: Robert, what did Darwin actually do on board?

Robert: He collected everything: rocks, insects, plants, birds, fossils. The voyage was supposed to last two years but in the end it took almost five, and he spent most of that time on land, while the ship was mapping the coast of South America. He was terribly seasick, by the way. He suffered on almost every day at sea, which is one reason why he preferred to be on shore.

Presenter: The Galápagos Islands are the most famous part of the voyage.

Helen: Yes, although Darwin spent only five weeks there. Interestingly, he didn't realise the importance of the finches at the time. He didn't even label which island each bird came from! It was only after he returned to England that an expert told him that the birds were different species, and he began to think about why.

Robert: The tortoises are another good example. The local governor told Darwin he could tell which island a tortoise came from by the shape of its shell. Darwin didn't take much notice then – he was more interested in eating them, to be honest.

Presenter: So the theory of evolution didn't come to him on the voyage?

Robert: Not at all. He worked on it for more than twenty years after he came home. He was afraid of how people would react, because his ideas contradicted the religious beliefs of the time. He only published On the Origin of Species in 1859, when another scientist, Alfred Russel Wallace, sent him a paper with very similar ideas.

Presenter: What can we learn from Darwin today?

Helen: Patience, and the value of careful observation. He spent eight years studying barnacles – tiny sea creatures – before he felt ready to write about evolution.

Robert: And that it's never too late to change your mind. He started the voyage believing every species had been created separately, and he ended up changing the way we understand life.

Darwin's voyage

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Darwin was twenty-two when he joined the Beagle. (T)
  2. 1.FitzRoy wanted someone to talk to during the voyage. T / F
  3. 2.Darwin's father supported the idea from the start. T / F
  4. 3.The voyage lasted longer than planned. T / F
  5. 4.Darwin enjoyed being at sea. T / F
  6. 5.Darwin spent several months on the Galápagos Islands. T / F
  7. 6.Darwin understood the importance of the finches immediately. T / F
  8. 7.Darwin was afraid of how people would react to his theory. T / F
  9. 8.Darwin published his theory after receiving a paper from Wallace. T / F
  10. 9.Darwin studied barnacles for eight years. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. T
2. F
3. T
4. F
5. F
6. F
7. T
8. T
9. T

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
Želel je izobraženega spremljevalca za pogovor pri večerji.
2. F
Oče je bil sprva proti; prepričal ga je stric.
3. T
Načrtovani sta bili dve leti, trajala je skoraj pet.
4. F
Trpel je za morsko boleznijo skoraj vsak dan.
5. F
Tam je bil le pet tednov.
6. F
Pomena ščinkavcev takrat ni prepoznal; ni niti označil otokov.
7. T
Bal se je odziva, ker so ideje nasprotovale verskim prepričanjem.
8. T
Knjigo je izdal 1859, ko mu je Wallace poslal članek s podobnimi idejami.
9. T
»He spent eight years studying barnacles«.

naloge.besedilo:
Article

Education Matters Magazine has invited secondary school students to write articles about school life.

Write an article of 120–150 words for Education Matters Magazine. Choose one of the two headings:
"My ideal school day" or "What I would change at my school".

In your article:

  • describe what a school day looks like for you now,
  • explain what you like and dislike about it,
  • suggest how it could be improved.
naloge.rezultat: Članek z izbranim naslovom, pritegnitvenim uvodom, odstavki o sedanjem šolskem dnevu, o tem, kaj je dobro in slabo, in s predlogi ter sklepom; 120–150 besed, polformalni slog.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Article (120–150 words), semi-formal style, with a title
  2. describe what a school day looks like for you now
  3. explain what you like and dislike about it
  4. suggest how it could be improved
Kako napišeš članek (article)
Članek (article): zgradba
  • Naslov: kratek in zanimiv; če navodilo ponuja naslove (headings), izberi enega in ga prepiši natančno.
  • Uvod: pritegni bralca (vprašanje, presenetljiv podatek, kratka zgodba) in v eni povedi povej, o čem bo članek.
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku; vsak odstavek začni s temeljno povedjo in jo podpri s primerom ali podatkom.
  • Sklep: povzemi svoje stališče ali nagovori bralce (So next time you …, why not …?). Nagovora »Dear …« in pozdrava ni.
Slog članka
  • Članek je namenjen širši javnosti (bralcem revije, šolskega časopisa, spletne strani), zato je slog polformalen: živahen, a ne pogovoren.
  • Uporabi retorična vprašanja (Have you ever wondered …?), neposreden nagovor bralca (you) in konkretne primere iz izkušenj.
  • Pri članku z mnenjem (opinion article) jasno povej svoje stališče in ga utemelji, upoštevaj tudi nasprotno mnenje.
  • Tudi v polformalnem slogu se izogibaj slengu (gonna, stuff, super cool) in pretiranim klicajem.
Uporabne zveze
  • Have you ever thought about …? · Imagine a school where … · According to a recent survey, …
  • On the one hand, … On the other hand, … · What is more, … · Not only … but also …
  • All in all, … · It is high time we … · The choice is yours.
Pogoste napake
  • Članek napisan kot pismo (Dear readers, … Yours sincerely).
  • Manjka naslov ali je naslov drugačen od ponujenega.
  • Iztočnice so le naštete, niso razvite s primeri in razlogi.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba članka
Naslov: prepiši izbrani naslov (What I would change at my school).
Naslov natančno, brez nagovora.
Uvod: pritegni bralca (Imagine a school where nobody yawns in the first lesson.).
Uvod uvede temo.
Odstavek 1: sedanji šolski dan
Lessons start at 7:30, we have seven forty-five-minute lessons and a short lunch break.
Iztočnica 1: opis s podatki.
Odstavek 2: kaj mi je všeč in kaj ne
I like the friendly teachers and the clubs; I dislike the early start and the heavy bags.
Iztočnica 2: obe plati.
Odstavek 3: predlogi
Lessons could start at 8:30, and textbooks could be digital.
Iztočnica 3: predlogi s could / should.
Sklep: nagovor bralcev (Small changes could make a big difference.).
Polformalni slog.
Preštej besede (120–150).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
What I would change at my school

Imagine a school where nobody yawns in the first lesson. Sadly, mine is not that school – yet.

At the moment, my school day starts at 7:30. We usually have seven lessons, each forty-five minutes long, with only one short break for lunch. After school, I often stay for drama club or volleyball.

There are many things I like. Most teachers are friendly and helpful, and the clubs are great fun. However, I dislike getting up so early, and my bag full of heavy textbooks gives me a backache.

So what would I change? Firstly, lessons could start at 8:30, because tired students do not learn much. Secondly, our textbooks could be digital, so we would only need a tablet. Finally, a longer lunch break would give us time to relax.

Small changes could make a big difference. Don't you agree?

Število besed: 149 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Celebrities have too much influence on young people.
  2. Shopping online is better than shopping in shops.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče.
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1: argument + primer (fashion and diets copied from Instagram).
Konkretni primeri.
Jedro 2: argument + primer (unrealistic lifestyles, pressure).
Povezovalci.
Jedro 3: protiargument (some celebrities raise awareness of important issues … However …).
Uravnoteženost.
Sklep: povzemi stališče.
Brez novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: convenience, prices, choice. Against: local shops close, returns, packaging waste, no advice from staff.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Celebrities have too much influence on young people.

Every day, millions of teenagers scroll through photos of famous singers, footballers and influencers. In my opinion, these celebrities have far too much influence on young people, although not all of it is negative.

Firstly, many young people copy everything their idols do. If a famous influencer wears a certain brand of trainers, thousands of teenagers want the same pair, even if they cannot afford them. Some even follow dangerous diets because a celebrity has promoted them on Instagram.

Secondly, celebrities often show an unrealistic lifestyle. Their photos are edited, their homes are enormous and they seem to be on holiday all the time. As a result, ordinary teenagers may feel that their own lives are boring and that they are not attractive enough. This pressure can lead to low self-esteem and even depression.

On the other hand, some celebrities use their fame in a positive way. Greta Thunberg has made millions of young people think about climate change, and several footballers have raised money for children in need. Such people can be excellent role models.

In conclusion, I believe that celebrities influence young people too strongly, mainly because teenagers often accept everything they see online without thinking. Parents and schools should therefore teach young people to think critically and to choose their role models carefully.

Število besed: 224 (zahtevanih 220–250). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

Remembering Everything

In 2006, a group of American neuroscientists published a paper about a woman they called "AJ". Unlike the rest of us, AJ could remember almost every day of her life since the age of fourteen. Give her any date, and she could tell you what day of the week it was, what she had done, what the weather had been like and what had been on the news. Her real name, it later emerged, was Jill Price, and she was the first person to be diagnosed with what scientists now call highly superior autobiographical memory, or HSAM.

At first, the researchers were sceptical. They tested her with dates from her own diaries, which she had kept for decades, and with historical events that she could not have prepared for. She was almost never wrong. Yet in other ways, her memory was quite ordinary. She had not been a particularly good student and found it difficult to memorise lists of words or facts that had no personal meaning for her.

Since then, about sixty people with HSAM have been identified around the world. Brain scans show that some areas linked to memory are larger than average, but scientists are still not sure whether this is a cause or a result of the condition. Many people with HSAM share certain habits: they tend to collect things, keep detailed records and organise their possessions very carefully.

It might sound like a wonderful gift, but many people with HSAM describe it as a burden. Jill Price has said that her memories run constantly, "like a split screen", and that she cannot switch them off. Painful moments come back as vividly as if they had happened yesterday, together with all the feelings she had at the time. Most of us are protected by forgetting: over the years, bad memories fade and lose their power. People with HSAM do not have this protection.

Researchers believe that studying HSAM could help people at the other end of the scale. Understanding why some people remember so much may help scientists find ways to slow down memory loss in diseases such as Alzheimer's. It may also teach us something about the function of forgetting. According to one theory, the brain forgets deliberately, to make room for new information and to help us concentrate on what is important.

For Jill Price, the question is more personal. "People ask me if I would like to get rid of it," she once said. "I tell them no. My memories are who I am. But some days I would give anything to forget one single afternoon."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.What does HSAM stand for?
    Highly superior autobiographical memory.
  2. 1.From what age could AJ remember almost every day?
  3. 2.What did the researchers use to check AJ's memories of her own life?
  4. 3.What kind of information did AJ find hard to memorise?
  5. 4.Approximately how many people with HSAM are known today?
  6. 5.What are scientists unsure about regarding the brain scans?
  7. 6.Name one habit that many people with HSAM share.
  8. 7.How does Jill Price describe her memories?
  9. 8.What protects most people from painful memories?
  10. 9.Which disease could research on HSAM help with?
naloge.rezultat:
1. (From) fourteen.
2. Her diaries.
3. Facts / lists with no personal meaning.
4. About sixty.
5. Whether the larger areas are a cause or a result.
6. Collecting things / keeping records / organising possessions.
7. Like a split screen. / They run constantly.
8. Forgetting.
9. Alzheimer's.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. (From) fourteen.
»since the age of fourteen«.
2. Her diaries.
»They tested her with dates from her own diaries«.
3. Facts / lists with no personal meaning.
»lists of words or facts that had no personal meaning for her«.
4. About sixty.
»about sixty people with HSAM have been identified«.
5. Whether the larger areas are a cause or a result.
»not sure whether this is a cause or a result of the condition«.
6. Collecting things / keeping records / organising possessions.
Dovolj je eden od treh navedenih.
7. Like a split screen. / They run constantly.
»like a split screen« – ne more jih izklopiti.
8. Forgetting.
»Most of us are protected by forgetting«.
9. Alzheimer's.
»memory loss in diseases such as Alzheimer's«.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (G).

Why are records spinning again?

Thirty years after the CD was supposed to kill it, vinyl is enjoying a remarkable comeback.

In the early 1990s, record shops around the world were closing. CDs were cheaper to produce, easier to carry and did not scratch. [0] By 2006, vinyl records made up less than one per cent of music sales in Britain.

Today, the situation looks very different. [1] In 2020, for the first time since the 1980s, more money was spent on vinyl records in the United States than on CDs.

What is surprising is who is buying them. [2] Surveys show that many buyers are under thirty, and some of them do not even own a record player. They buy records as objects to display, or as a way of supporting their favourite artists.

For many fans, the appeal is partly physical. [3] Large cover art, printed lyrics and coloured vinyl make a record feel like a work of art rather than a file on a phone.

Others say that vinyl simply sounds better. [4] Sound engineers point out that much of what people hear as "warmth" is actually a slight distortion, but listeners say that they enjoy it anyway.

There is also something ritual about playing a record. [5] You choose the album, take it carefully out of its sleeve, place the needle on the edge and sit down to listen to a whole side. In a world of endless playlists, this forces people to slow down and concentrate.

The revival has brought problems, however. [6] There are only a few dozen factories in the world that can press records, and many of them use machines that are more than forty years old. Delays of six months or more are now common.

Environmentalists are also concerned. [7] Records are made from PVC, a type of plastic that is difficult to recycle and produces toxic chemicals when it is made.

The revival has also been good news for record shops. [8] In Britain alone, the number of independent record shops has risen sharply over the last ten years. Many of them have become meeting places rather than just places to buy things. [9] For their customers, buying music has become a social event once again.

Nobody expects vinyl to replace streaming, which still accounts for the vast majority of music listening. [10] As one shop owner in Manchester puts it: "People don't come here because they need music. They come because they want to own it." [11] Perhaps that is something no algorithm can provide.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AIt is not only older people who remember the music of their youth.
  2. BHolding a record in your hands is very different from pressing a button.
  3. CSome music lovers claim that analogue recordings have a warmer, richer quality.
  4. DUnlike streaming, it requires a series of deliberate actions.
  5. EFactories cannot keep up with demand.
  6. FRecord sales have risen every year for more than a decade.
  7. GMost music fans happily replaced their old collections.
  8. HProducing vinyl has a much larger environmental impact than streaming.
  9. IBut for a growing number of people, it offers something that streaming cannot.

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take

  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

5. D
»something ritual« – D: zahteva vrsto namernih dejanj; sledi opis teh dejanj.
6. E
»problems« – E: tovarne ne zmorejo povpraševanja; sledi podatek o maloštevilnih tovarnah in zamudah.
7. H

8. K

9. N
»meeting places« – N našteje, kaj trgovine ponujajo (koncerti, kava, večeri poslušanja); sledi »a social event«.
10. I
»Nobody expects vinyl to replace streaming« – nasprotje (But …): ponuja nekaj, česar pretakanje ne more.
11. J
Po citatu: glasba ni več le nekaj, kar slišimo – nekaj, kar posedujemo.

What can we learn from the world's oldest people?

In a few places around the world, people live much longer than average. On the Japanese island of Okinawa, in the mountains of Sardinia and on the Nicoya Peninsula in Costa Rica, an unusually high number of people reach the age of a hundred. Researchers have called these areas "Blue Zones", and they have spent years trying to discover (0) makes them special.

The first thing they noticed was that none of these people followed a special diet (1) went to a gym. Instead, they moved naturally throughout the day: they walked, worked in their gardens and climbed hills to visit friends. Many of them continued working well (2) their eighties. "Nobody in Sardinia goes jogging," says one researcher. "But a ninety-year-old shepherd might walk ten kilometres a day."

Their diets were also similar in some ways. Most of their food came from plants, especially beans, vegetables and whole grains. Meat was eaten only a few times a month, and (3) in small amounts. In Okinawa, older people follow a traditional rule called "hara hachi bu", which means eating (4) they are eighty per cent full.

But the most important factors may not be physical (5) all. People in Blue Zones tend to have strong family ties and close friendships that last (6) life. In Okinawa, many people belong to a "moai", a small group of friends who support each other from childhood (7) old age. Studies have shown that loneliness can be (8) harmful to health as smoking fifteen cigarettes a day.

A sense of purpose also seems to matter. The people of Nicoya call it "plan de vida", the reason (9) which you get up in the morning. For some it is their family, for others their work, their garden or their faith. Researchers have found that people who have a clear purpose in life live up (10) seven years longer than those who do not.

Critics point out that not all the claims about Blue Zones are reliable. In some regions, birth records from a hundred years ago are incomplete, and a few "centenarians" turned out to be younger than they claimed. (11), most scientists agree that the basic lessons are sound.

The good news is that we do not have to move to a Mediterranean island to benefit (12) them. Walking more, eating more vegetables, spending time with friends and finding something we care about are all changes (13) anyone can make. As one Sardinian grandmother put it when she was asked about the secret of her long life: "Work hard, eat simply and never stay angry (14) more than a day." By then the Second World War (9) (START), and the need for a drug that could treat infected wounds was urgent. You will listen to an interview with Nina Clarke, an underwater photographer. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Nina, you've spent more than twenty years photographing the oceans. How did it begin?

Nina: In a swimming pool in Birmingham, of all places! I was a very nervous swimmer as a child, and my mother signed me up for lessons to help me get over my fear. The teacher let us try a mask and snorkel at the end of each lesson, and I was amazed by how quiet and peaceful it was under the water. I've been trying to get back to that feeling ever since.

Interviewer: When did you start taking pictures?

Nina: At sixteen. I saved money from my Saturday job in a supermarket and bought a cheap waterproof camera. My first photos were terrible – mostly blue water and blurry fish – but I learned that patience matters more than equipment. You have to wait for the animals to come to you.

Interviewer: What is the most difficult thing about your job?

Nina: The light. Water absorbs colour very quickly. At only ten metres, almost all the red has disappeared, so everything looks blue or green. I use strong lights to bring the colours back. The other problem is time: on a normal dive I have about forty-five minutes before I have to go up, so I might get one good picture in a whole day.

Interviewer: Which photograph are you proudest of?

Nina: A picture of a mother humpback whale and her calf in the waters near Tonga. We spent eleven days on a boat waiting for them. On the last morning, they swam right up to me, and the calf looked straight into my camera. That picture won an international prize and was used on the cover of a book about ocean protection.

Interviewer: Have you seen the oceans change?

Nina: Dramatically. When I started diving in the Red Sea, the coral was full of life. Now, in many places, it is grey and broken. I also see plastic on almost every dive, even in places hundreds of kilometres from the nearest town. It's heartbreaking.

Interviewer: Do you think photographs can make a difference?

Nina: I hope so. Most people will never see a coral reef with their own eyes. If my pictures help them fall in love with the ocean, they might be more willing to protect it. I give talks in schools every month, and the children always ask the best questions.

Interviewer: What would you like to photograph next?

Nina: The giant squid. Very few people have ever seen one alive. It lives at depths where no diver can go, so I'm working with scientists on a special camera that can be lowered on a cable.

An underwater photographer

  8. 7.The whale photograph was used on the cover of a book about ____.
  9. 8.When Nina started diving in the Red Sea, the coral was ____.
  10. 9.Nina gives talks in schools ____.

2. sixteen

4. bring the colours back
5. one good picture
6. Tonga
7. ocean protection

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to two historians, Helen Shaw and Robert Price, talking about Charles Darwin's voyage on the Beagle. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Helen, Darwin was only twenty-two when he joined the Beagle. How did he get the chance?

Helen: Almost by luck. The captain, Robert FitzRoy, wanted a gentleman companion for the long voyage, someone educated to talk to at dinner, because captains were not supposed to socialise with the crew. Darwin's teacher at Cambridge recommended him. His father was against it at first – he thought it was a waste of time – and only Darwin's uncle persuaded him to change his mind.

Presenter: Robert, what did Darwin actually do on board?

Robert: He collected everything: rocks, insects, plants, birds, fossils. The voyage was supposed to last two years but in the end it took almost five, and he spent most of that time on land, while the ship was mapping the coast of South America. He was terribly seasick, by the way. He suffered on almost every day at sea, which is one reason why he preferred to be on shore.

Presenter: The Galápagos Islands are the most famous part of the voyage.

Helen: Yes, although Darwin spent only five weeks there. Interestingly, he didn't realise the importance of the finches at the time. He didn't even label which island each bird came from! It was only after he returned to England that an expert told him that the birds were different species, and he began to think about why.

Robert: The tortoises are another good example. The local governor told Darwin he could tell which island a tortoise came from by the shape of its shell. Darwin didn't take much notice then – he was more interested in eating them, to be honest.

Presenter: So the theory of evolution didn't come to him on the voyage?

Robert: Not at all. He worked on it for more than twenty years after he came home. He was afraid of how people would react, because his ideas contradicted the religious beliefs of the time. He only published On the Origin of Species in 1859, when another scientist, Alfred Russel Wallace, sent him a paper with very similar ideas.

Presenter: What can we learn from Darwin today?

Helen: Patience, and the value of careful observation. He spent eight years studying barnacles – tiny sea creatures – before he felt ready to write about evolution.

Robert: And that it's never too late to change your mind. He started the voyage believing every species had been created separately, and he ended up changing the way we understand life.

Darwin's voyage

  7. 6.What did Darwin forget to record about the finches?
  8. 7.According to the governor, how could you tell where a tortoise came from?
  9. 8.In which year was On the Origin of Species published?
  10. 9.What did Darwin believe at the start of the voyage?

naloge.besedilo:
Article

The journal Modern Society is publishing a series of articles by young people on the future of work.

Write an article of 150–180 words for the journal Modern Society by choosing one of the two headings:
"Robots will take our jobs" or "Working from home is the future".

In your article:

  • explain how the topic affects young people,
  • discuss the advantages and disadvantages,
  • say how young people should prepare for the future.
naloge.rezultat: Članek z izbranim naslovom, pritegnitvenim uvodom, odstavki o tem, kako tema zadeva mlade, o prednostih in slabostih ter o pripravi na prihodnost, in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Article (150–180 words), semi-formal style, with a title
  2. explain how the topic affects young people
  3. discuss the advantages and disadvantages
  4. say how young people should prepare for the future
Kako napišeš članek (article)
Članek (article): zgradba
  • Naslov: kratek in zanimiv; če navodilo ponuja naslove (headings), izberi enega in ga prepiši natančno.
  • Uvod: pritegni bralca (vprašanje, presenetljiv podatek, kratka zgodba) in v eni povedi povej, o čem bo članek.
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku; vsak odstavek začni s temeljno povedjo in jo podpri s primerom ali podatkom.
  • Sklep: povzemi svoje stališče ali nagovori bralce (So next time you …, why not …?). Nagovora »Dear …« in pozdrava ni.
Slog članka
  • Članek je namenjen širši javnosti (bralcem revije, šolskega časopisa, spletne strani), zato je slog polformalen: živahen, a ne pogovoren.
  • Uporabi retorična vprašanja (Have you ever wondered …?), neposreden nagovor bralca (you) in konkretne primere iz izkušenj.
  • Pri članku z mnenjem (opinion article) jasno povej svoje stališče in ga utemelji, upoštevaj tudi nasprotno mnenje.
  • Tudi v polformalnem slogu se izogibaj slengu (gonna, stuff, super cool) in pretiranim klicajem.
Uporabne zveze
  • Have you ever thought about …? · Imagine a school where … · According to a recent survey, …
  • On the one hand, … On the other hand, … · What is more, … · Not only … but also …
  • All in all, … · It is high time we … · The choice is yours.
Pogoste napake
  • Članek napisan kot pismo (Dear readers, … Yours sincerely).
  • Manjka naslov ali je naslov drugačen od ponujenega.
  • Iztočnice so le naštete, niso razvite s primeri in razlogi.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba članka
Naslov: Working from home is the future
Prepiši izbrani naslov natančno.
Uvod: osebna izkušnja ali vprašanje (During the pandemic, my parents turned the kitchen into an office …).
Pritegni bralca.
Odstavek 1: kako tema zadeva mlade
Young people will enter a job market where many employers expect flexible, online work.
Iztočnica 1.
Odstavek 2: prednosti in slabosti
No commuting, more free time, cheaper housing outside cities versus loneliness, blurred boundaries between work and private life.
Iztočnica 2: uravnoteženo (On the one hand … On the other hand …).
Odstavek 3: kako se pripraviti
Develop self-discipline, digital skills and the ability to communicate online.
Iztočnica 3: predlogi.
Sklep: The office may not disappear, but it will never be the same again.
Polformalni slog, višja raven: pestro besedišče.
Preštej besede (150–180).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Working from home is the future

During the pandemic, my parents turned our kitchen table into an office. More than a year later, they still work there three days a week, and they have no intention of going back full time. Are they a sign of things to come?

For young people, the question is crucial. We will enter a job market in which many employers already expect flexible, online work, and a laptop may become more important than a desk in a city centre.

The advantages are obvious. Without commuting, employees save time and money, and they can live in cheaper areas outside big cities. On the other hand, working from home can be lonely, and the boundary between work and private life easily disappears when your office is also your living room.

So how should we prepare? Above all, we need self-discipline, strong digital skills and the ability to communicate clearly online. It also helps to build a network of real-life contacts.

The office may not disappear, but it will never be the same again.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss the character of Jack and his rise to power in William Golding's Lord of the Flies.

William Golding: Lord of the Flies

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo o Jacku kot predstavniku želje po oblasti, podprto s prizori (vodja zbora, prvi prašič, poslikan obraz, ugasnjen ogenj, lastno pleme na Castle Rock, vladanje s strahom); brez obnove; 250–300 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the character of Jack and his rise to power in William Golding's Lord of the Flies.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – Jack represents the desire for power and the attraction of violence; he wins because he offers the boys what they want rather than what they need.
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1 – Jack at the beginning: leader of the choir, disappointed when Ralph is elected; he cannot kill the first pig.
Prizori iz začetka.
Jedro 2 – the hunter: painted face as a mask ('liberated from shame'); the signal fire goes out while he hunts and a ship passes.
Pokaži spremembo.
Jedro 3 – the chief: he forms his own tribe at Castle Rock, offers meat and protection from the beast, rules through fear; Roger's violence is allowed.
Vrhunec moči.
Sklep: Jack shows how easily people follow a leader who gives them excitement and an enemy.
Sklep razširi tezo.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Jack and his rise to power in Lord of the Flies

In William Golding's Lord of the Flies, Jack Merridew represents the desire for power and the attraction of violence. He becomes the most powerful boy on the island not because he is wiser than Ralph, but because he offers the boys what they want rather than what they need.

At the beginning, Jack is already a leader: he arrives marching at the head of his choir and clearly expects to be chief. When the boys vote for Ralph instead, he is humiliated, and Ralph tries to keep him happy by making the choir his hunters. Yet when Jack finds a piglet caught in the creepers, he cannot bring himself to kill it. The rules of civilisation are still stronger than his instincts.

Gradually, hunting becomes an obsession. Jack paints his face with clay and, hidden behind this mask, feels "liberated from shame and self-consciousness". The most important moment comes when he takes the boys who should be watching the signal fire hunting. The fire goes out just as a ship passes, and the chance of rescue is lost. For Jack, meat matters more than escape.

Finally, Jack forms his own tribe at Castle Rock. He attracts the boys with feasts and promises to protect them from the beast, but he rules through fear. Boys are beaten for no reason, and Roger's cruelty is not only allowed but encouraged, which leads to Piggy's death and the hunt for Ralph.

In conclusion, Jack's rise to power shows how easily people follow a leader who gives them excitement, food and an enemy to fear. Golding suggests that such leaders are dangerous precisely because they appeal to the savage side in all of us.

Slow Days on Inchmore

The ferry to Inchmore leaves the mainland twice a day in summer and once a day in winter, if the weather allows. On the morning I travelled, there were only six passengers: a farmer with two sheepdogs, a retired couple from Glasgow, a postman and me. The crossing took fifty minutes, and for most of it we could see nothing but grey sea and gulls.

Inchmore is a small island off the west coast of Scotland, about eight kilometres long and three kilometres wide. Around a hundred and twenty people live there all year round, most of them in the village of Port Ailean, which has one shop, one pub, a primary school with nine pupils and a church that is used as a cinema on Friday nights.

There are no traffic lights on the island and only one road, which is so narrow that drivers have to stop in special passing places to let other cars by. Everybody waves at everybody. On my first day, I was surprised when a stranger in a tractor waved at me; by the third day, I was waving first.

Mobile phone signal on Inchmore is weak, and in some parts of the island it does not exist at all. At first this made me nervous. I kept checking my phone and walking up hills to find one bar of signal. But after a couple of days I stopped worrying and began to notice other things instead: the seals lying on the rocks near the harbour, the smell of peat smoke from the chimneys, the way the light changed every few minutes.

I stayed in a guesthouse run by Morag, a former nurse who moved to the island from Edinburgh twenty years ago. "People come here for a weekend and stay for a month," she told me over breakfast. "The island does that to you." Every morning she cooked eggs from her own hens, and every evening she asked me what I had seen that day, as if it really mattered.

Life on the island is not always easy, though. In winter, storms can cut Inchmore off from the mainland for days. Fresh fruit and vegetables arrive only twice a week, and the nearest hospital is a helicopter ride away. Young people usually leave at sixteen to go to secondary school on the mainland, and many of them never come back. The islanders worry about the future of their school, which might close if the number of pupils falls any further.

Recently, however, things have started to change. Thanks to a new internet cable laid across the sea bed, a few young families have moved to Inchmore and work from home. A web designer from London now runs her business from a converted barn, and a young couple have opened a café that sells cakes made with island honey.

On my last morning, I sat on the harbour wall waiting for the ferry. The farmer with the sheepdogs was there again, and he nodded at me. "You'll be back," he said. He was right.

  9. 8.What was Morag's job before she moved to the island?
  10. 9.At what age do young people usually leave the island?

5. when / if / once
Časovni ali pogojni veznik: tasted better when sugar was added.
6. from
»keep something a secret from someone« = skrivati pred kom.
7. where
Oziralni prislov za kraj (Francija, Italija, Anglija).
8. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za stvar (a luxury) v vlogi predmeta.
9. from
»separate A from B« = ločiti od.
10. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za stvari (the companies) v vlogi osebka.
11. in
Predlog za regijo: in West Africa.
12. for
»criticise someone for doing something« = kritizirati zaradi.
13. if / as
Pogoj ali vzrok: if temperatures continue to rise.
14. on
»work on something« = delati na čem, razvijati.

Oziralni zaimek za osebe v vlogi predmeta: farmers whom you will never meet.
16. by
Stalna zveza »piece by piece« = košček za koščkom.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The science of a good night's sleep

We spend about a third of our lives asleep, yet for a long time scientists knew surprisingly little about why sleep is so (0) (IMPORTANCE). Today, research shows that a good night's sleep is just as (1) (ESSENCE) for our health as a balanced diet and regular exercise.

While we sleep, the brain is far from (2) (ACT). It sorts the information we have collected during the day, stores important memories and removes waste products that build up in the brain cells. Students who sleep well before an exam usually remember more than those who stay up all night studying, because their brains have had time to process what they have learned. A lack of sleep, on the other hand, makes it more (3) (DIFFICULTY) to concentrate and to make (4) (DECIDE).

Sleep is also vital for the body. During deep sleep, the body repairs muscles and produces hormones that help us grow. People who regularly sleep less than six hours a night have a higher risk of (5) (ILL) such as heart disease and diabetes, and they are more likely to catch colds because their immune system becomes (6) (WEAK).

Teenagers have a particular problem. During adolescence, the body clock shifts, so that teenagers naturally feel sleepy later in the evening and find it hard to wake up early. This is not (7) (LAZY), scientists say, but biology. Many experts believe that schools should start later, and some schools that have done so have reported better results and fewer (8) (ABSENT).

Modern technology does not help. The blue light from phones and tablets tricks the brain into thinking it is still day, and endless messages and videos keep us awake. In one survey, more than half of (9) (TEENAGE) admitted that they used their phones in bed after midnight.

So what can we do? Experts recommend going to bed and getting up at the same time every day, even at weekends. The bedroom should be dark, quiet and cool, and phones should be switched off at least an hour before bed. Caffeine should be avoided in the afternoon, as its effects can last for several hours. A short walk or a little (10) (RELAX) reading can also help.

Above all, we need to stop seeing sleep as a waste of time. In a culture that admires people who work late and get up early, sleeping eight hours can seem almost (11) (RESPONSIBLE). But the evidence is clear: people who sleep well are healthier, happier and more (12) (PRODUCE). Perhaps the most (13) (EFFECT) thing we can do for our health is simply to go to bed. It is a (14) (SOLVE) that is free, simple and available to everyone.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. important
naloge.rezultat:
1. essential
2. inactive
3. difficult
4. decisions
5. illnesses
6. weaker
7. laziness
8. absences
9. teenagers
10. relaxing
11. irresponsible
12. productive
13. effective
14. solution
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. essential
Za »as … as« pridevnik: essence → essential.
2. inactive
Za »far from« pridevnik z nikalno predpono: act → inactive (možgani niso nedejavni).
3. difficult
»make it more difficult to« – pridevnik: difficulty → difficult.
4. decisions
»make decisions« – samostalnik v množini: decide → decision(s).
5. illnesses
Za »risk of« samostalnik; »such as« našteva več bolezni, zato množina: illnesses.
6. weaker
»becomes« + pridevnik v primerniku (sistem postane šibkejši): weak → weaker.
7. laziness
»This is not …, but biology« – samostalnik: lazy → laziness.
8. absences
Za »fewer« števni samostalnik v množini: absent → absences.
9. teenagers
»more than half of« + množina: teenage → teenagers.
10. relaxing
Pred samostalnikom »reading« pridevnik: relax → relaxing.
11. irresponsible
Nasprotje: spanje se zdi skoraj neodgovorno – predpona ir-.
12. productive
»more« + pridevnik: produce → productive.
13. effective
»the most« + pridevnik: effect → effective.
14. solution
»a« + samostalnik: solve → solution.
