naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (G).

Working less, achieving more?

A growing number of companies are trying a four-day working week. Is it the future of work?

For most of the last century, the five-day working week has been taken for granted. Monday to Friday, nine to five: it is the rhythm around which we organise our lives. [0] Yet it was not always like this, and some people believe it may soon change again.

The weekend as we know it is a relatively recent invention. [1] It was only in the early twentieth century that factory owners, partly under pressure from trade unions, began to give their workers Saturday afternoons and then whole Saturdays off.

Today, a new idea is spreading: the four-day week. [2] Crucially, workers are paid the same as before, so the change is not simply a way of saving money.

The results of the first trials have surprised many people. [3] In one well-known experiment at a New Zealand company, staff said they felt less stressed and more committed to their work, and managers found that productivity had stayed the same or even improved.

How is this possible? [4] Meetings become shorter, fewer emails are sent, and workers waste less time on social media because they know they have less time to finish their tasks.

There are also wider benefits. [5] Parents can spend more time with their children, people have more time for hobbies, exercise and volunteering, and commuting one day less a week reduces traffic and pollution.

Not everyone is convinced, however. [6] A hospital, a restaurant or a shop cannot simply close for an extra day, and finding enough staff to cover the gaps can be expensive.

Others worry about the pressure. [7] Some employees in trial companies said that the fifth day off was wonderful, but that the other four had become more intense and tiring than before.

Supporters respond that the four-day week does not have to look the same everywhere. [8] Some companies give everyone Fridays off, while others let staff choose their own free day so that the business stays open all week.

It is too early to say whether the four-day week will become the new normal. [9] What seems clear is that the pandemic has made many people question old habits and ask what work is really for. As one researcher put it: "We should measure work by what people achieve, not by how many hours they sit at a desk." [10]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AIn the nineteenth century, many factory workers worked six days a week, often for twelve hours a day.
  2. BEmployees work around thirty-two hours instead of forty, usually from Monday to Thursday.
  3. CEmployees reported better health, a better work-life balance and greater job satisfaction.
  4. DAccording to researchers, people simply learn to use their time more efficiently.
  5. EA shorter week could also help society as a whole.
  6. FCritics point out that the model does not suit every type of job.
  7. GIt shapes everything from school timetables to television programmes.
  8. HDoing five days' work in four, they say, can lead to burnout.
  9. IThe model can be adapted to the needs of different organisations.
  10. JSeveral countries are now running large trials, and the results will be studied closely.
  11. KIf that is true, the five-day week may one day seem as old-fashioned as the twelve-hour day.
  12. LAs a result, most companies have decided to return to a six-day week.
  13. MSalaries are usually reduced by twenty per cent to cover the costs.

2. B
3. C
4. D
5. E
6. F
7. H
8. I
9. J
10. K
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A
»The weekend … is a relatively recent invention« – A opiše razmere v 19. stoletju; sledi »It was only in the early twentieth century …«.
2. B
»the four-day week« – B ga opiše (32 ur, pon.–čet.); »Crucially, workers are paid the same« nadaljuje opis. M je napačen, ker plača ostane enaka.
3. C
»The results … have surprised many« – C navede rezultate; sledi primer iz Nove Zelandije.
4. D
»How is this possible?« – D odgovori (bolj učinkovita raba časa); sledijo primeri (krajši sestanki …).
5. E
»wider benefits« – E: koristi za vso družbo; sledi naštevanje (starši, hobiji, promet).
6. F
»Not everyone is convinced« – F: model ne ustreza vsem poklicem; sledi primer bolnišnice in trgovine.
7. H
»Others worry about the pressure« – H: izgorelost; sledi izkušnja zaposlenih (bolj intenzivni štirje dnevi).
8. I
»does not have to look the same everywhere« – I: model se lahko prilagodi; sledita dva primera.
9. J
»too early to say« – J: več držav izvaja poskuse, rezultate bodo pozorno preučili.
10. K
Po citatu o merjenju dela po dosežkih: »If that is true« – sklep, ki se vrne k 12-urnemu delavniku iz uvoda.

At high altitude, where it is extremely cold, nothing decomposes, so the rubbish simply stays (2) it was dropped. Everest has been called "the world's highest rubbish dump".

To deal with the problem, the Nepalese government introduced a rule in 2014: every climber must bring (5) at least eight kilograms of rubbish, or lose a deposit of four thousand dollars. The rule has had some success, (6) critics say it is not always properly enforced.

Every year, teams of Sherpas and volunteers also go up the mountain to collect waste. It is dangerous work. Carrying heavy bags of rubbish at altitudes (7) there is only a third of the oxygen found at sea level is exhausting, and the cleaners face the same risks as climbers: avalanches, storms and falls. In 2019, one clean-up campaign collected more (8) ten tonnes of waste in just six weeks.

Some people believe the only real solution is to reduce the number of climbers. They argue that permits should be more expensive or limited in number, and that only experienced mountaineers should be allowed (9) attempt the climb. naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Hannah Brooks, a volunteer with a mountain rescue team in the Lake District. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Hannah, you've been a mountain rescue volunteer for eleven years. What does the job involve?

Hannah: Well, first of all, it isn't a job – nobody in our team is paid. We're all volunteers with ordinary jobs. I'm a primary school teacher. But when the phone goes, day or night, we drop everything and go up the mountain to find people who are lost or injured.

Interviewer: How often does the phone go?

Hannah: Our team gets about a hundred and twenty call-outs a year. In summer it can be three or four in a single weekend. Most of them are walkers who have slipped and hurt an ankle, but we also look for people who are lost in fog, and sometimes climbers who have fallen.

Interviewer: How did you get involved?

Hannah: It was because of my dad. When I was fourteen, he broke his leg on a walk in the mountains, and a rescue team carried him down in the dark through the rain. It took them five hours. I remember sitting in the car park watching their lights coming down the hill, and I thought, I want to do that one day.

Interviewer: Was it difficult to join?

Hannah: Quite difficult, yes. You need to be very fit, of course, and you need a lot of experience in the mountains. Then there's a probation period of about a year, when you train with the team every Wednesday evening and one weekend a month. You learn first aid, navigation, how to use ropes, how to carry a stretcher across rocks. Only after that do you become a full member.

Interviewer: What's the hardest part?

Hannah: Physically, carrying a stretcher. A person on a stretcher, with all the equipment, can weigh well over a hundred kilos, and we sometimes carry them for hours. But emotionally, the hardest moments are when we arrive too late. Those days stay with you. We talk about them as a team afterwards, which really helps.

Interviewer: Has the job changed during your time with the team?

Hannah: Enormously. When I started, we used paper maps and radios. Now we use drones with thermal cameras, which can find a person in the dark by their body heat. And most people carry a mobile phone, so we can often find their location very quickly. Strangely, though, phones have also brought more call-outs.

Interviewer: Why is that?

Hannah: Because people rely on them too much. They follow a route on an app, the battery dies, and they have no map, no torch and no idea where they are. Or they go up in trainers and a T-shirt because the weather was nice in the valley. The weather in the mountains can change in minutes.

Interviewer: So what's your advice to walkers?

Hannah: Check the forecast, tell someone where you're going, and always carry a paper map, a torch, warm clothes and some food – even on a short walk. And don't be embarrassed to turn back. The mountain will still be there next week.

Interviewer: Do you ever think about giving up?

Hannah: Sometimes, at three in the morning, when it's raining sideways. But then you find someone who has been lying on a cold hillside for hours, and you see their face when they realise they're going to be all right. There's no feeling like it.

Interviewer: Hannah, thank you very much.

A mountain rescue volunteer

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Erik Sundqvist, who helps to build an ice hotel in northern Sweden every winter. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Erik, you build a hotel every year – and every spring it melts. Why?

Erik: That's exactly the beauty of it. Nothing lasts for ever, and this hotel reminds you of that. It's built in November, it opens in December, and by the end of April it has turned back into water and flowed into the river. Then the next year we start again, with a completely new design.

Interviewer: Where does the ice come from?

Erik: From the river right next to the hotel. In March, when the ice is at its thickest, we cut huge blocks out of the river – each one weighs about two tonnes – and keep them in a cold storage hall through the summer. River ice is perfect because it moves slowly while it freezes, so it's very clear, almost like glass.

Interviewer: How long does it take to build the hotel?

Erik: About six weeks. We start with a steel frame, spray it with a mixture of snow and ice that we call "snice", and when it has frozen hard, we take the frame away. Then the artists arrive.

Interviewer: Artists?

Erik: Yes, every year we invite artists from all over the world to design the special suites. Each room is a different work of art. Last year, one room looked like the inside of a whale, and another was full of ice flowers. The artists don't need to have worked with ice before – some of them are painters or architects who have never touched a chainsaw.

Interviewer: What is it like to sleep in an ice room?

Erik: People are always worried about the cold, but the temperature inside stays between minus five and minus eight degrees, whatever the weather outside. You sleep in a thermal sleeping bag on reindeer skins, and most guests are surprised how warm they are. The hardest part is getting out of the sleeping bag in the morning!

Interviewer: Do most guests stay more than one night?

Erik: No, usually just one. Most people spend one night in the ice and the rest of their stay in warm rooms nearby. One night is an adventure; three would be a challenge.

Interviewer: What about the environment? Isn't it a strange idea, building with ice when the climate is getting warmer?

Erik: It's a fair question. We see the changes ourselves – the river freezes later than it used to. But in recent years we have also built a part of the hotel that stays open all year. It's kept cold with energy from solar panels, so in summer the sun actually keeps the ice frozen.

Interviewer: What do you enjoy most about your work?

Erik: The silence. When you're working inside the hotel early in the morning, before the guests wake up, you can hear the ice moving, a kind of soft cracking. It feels as if the building is alive.

Building with ice

E-mail

The Young Leaders Foundation offers full scholarships for a six-week summer academy in Boston, USA, for students aged 16–25 who want to develop their leadership skills. Applicants can choose one of three programmes: Environmental Leadership, Social Entrepreneurship or Media and Democracy.

Write an e-mail of application of 150–180 words to the scholarship committee in which you:

  • explain which programme you have chosen and why,
  • describe your relevant experience and skills,
  • explain why you are a suitable candidate for the scholarship.
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-pismo – prošnja za štipendijo: formalni nagovor, uvod z namenom, izbrani program z razlogi, konkretne izkušnje in spretnosti, utemeljitev, zakaj si primeren kandidat, formalen konec; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (150–180 words), formal style
  2. explain which programme you have chosen and why
  3. describe your relevant experience and skills
  4. explain why you are a suitable candidate for the scholarship
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor, ko ne poznaš imena.
I am writing to apply for a scholarship for the Environmental Leadership programme.
Uvod z namenom pisma.
I have chosen this programme because … I would like to learn how to …
Iztočnica 1: izbira in razlogi.
For two years I have led our school's Eco Club, where I organised …
Iztočnica 2: konkretne izkušnje in spretnosti.
I believe I am a suitable candidate because … On my return, I plan to …
Iztočnica 3: zakaj ravno ti; kako boš znanje uporabil.
I look forward to hearing from you. / Yours faithfully, / Ana Kovač
Formalen konec.
Višja raven: 150–180 besed; prepričljiv, formalen jezik (I am particularly interested in …, I would welcome the opportunity …).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for a scholarship for the Environmental Leadership programme at your summer academy in Boston.

I have chosen this programme because I am deeply concerned about climate change and would like to learn how to turn concern into effective action. In particular, I am interested in how young people can influence local decision-makers.

For the past two years I have led our school's Eco Club. Among other things, I organised a campaign that reduced plastic waste in our canteen by half, and I coordinated a tree-planting day with the local council. These projects have taught me how to motivate others, plan events and speak in public. My English is fluent.

I believe I am a suitable candidate because I already have practical experience and a clear plan for the future. On my return, I intend to share what I have learned by starting an environmental network for secondary schools in my region.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Ana Kovač

Število besed: 171 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo o Piggyju kot predstavniku razuma in reda, podprto s prizori (posmeh, školjka, očala in ogenj, kraja očal, Piggyjevo vprašanje na Castle Rock, smrt in uničenje školjke, Ralphove solze); brez obnove; 250–300 besed.

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the role of Piggy in William Golding's Lord of the Flies.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …

Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – Piggy represents reason, science and the adult world; his treatment shows how quickly the boys reject intelligence and order.
Teza v uvodu, brez obnove.
Jedro 1 – the outsider: his asthma, glasses and nickname; the boys laugh at him, yet he suggests using the conch to call a meeting.
Prizori iz začetka.
Jedro 2 – reason and science: his glasses light the fire; he insists on rules, shelters and the signal fire; Jack breaks one lens and later steals the glasses.
Očala kot simbol razuma.
Jedro 3 – death: at Castle Rock he holds the conch and asks 'Which is better – to have rules and agree, or to hunt and kill?'; Roger's rock kills him and destroys the conch.
Vrhunec: konec razuma in reda.
Sklep: Ralph weeps for 'the fall through the air of the true, wise friend called Piggy' – the loss of Piggy is the loss of civilisation.
Sklep se vrne k tezi.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The role of Piggy in Lord of the Flies

In William Golding's Lord of the Flies, Piggy represents reason, science and the rules of the adult world. Although he is weak and unpopular, he is the most sensible boy on the island, and the way the others treat him shows how quickly they reject intelligence and order.

From the very beginning, Piggy is an outsider. He is fat, short-sighted and suffers from asthma, and the boys laugh at him as soon as Ralph reveals his hated nickname. Yet it is Piggy who understands the value of the conch and suggests using it to call a meeting. His ideas are good, but because he is not respected, he needs Ralph to put them into practice.

Piggy's glasses are the clearest symbol of his role. They are used to light the signal fire, the boys' only hope of rescue, so reason literally gives them fire. Piggy constantly reminds the others about rules, shelters and the fire, and he behaves as a grown-up would. Significantly, Jack breaks one of the lenses in anger, and later his tribe steals the glasses, leaving Ralph's group unable to make fire.

Piggy's death marks the end of civilisation on the island. At Castle Rock, holding the conch, he asks: "Which is better – to have rules and agree, or to hunt and kill?" Roger answers by releasing a huge rock, which kills Piggy and smashes the conch at the same moment.

In conclusion, Piggy is the voice of reason that the boys refuse to hear. At the end of the novel, Ralph weeps for "the fall through the air of the true, wise friend called Piggy". Golding suggests that when a society silences its wisest members, it loses its humanity.

My Summer as a Shepherd

When my parents told me that I would spend the summer on a mountain pasture with my grandfather, I was furious. I was sixteen, all my friends were going to the seaside, and I could not imagine anything more boring than spending ten weeks with a hundred cows. I did not know then that it would be the best summer of my life.

My grandfather has spent every summer of the last fifty years in a small wooden hut at about sixteen hundred metres above sea level. There is no electricity, and water comes from a spring behind the hut. The nearest village is a two-hour walk away, and the only way to get supplies up the mountain is on the back of an old horse called Miško.

The first days were terrible. My grandfather woke me at five o'clock every morning to milk the cows, and by the evening my hands and back hurt so much that I could hardly sleep. I missed my phone, which had no signal, and I counted the days until I could go home.

Slowly, however, things began to change. My grandfather was not a man of many words, but he knew everything about the mountain. He taught me to recognise the weather from the shape of the clouds, to find wild strawberries and to tell the cows apart by the sound of their bells. He also showed me how to make cheese, which was much harder than I had expected. My first cheese was so hard that we gave it to the dog.

In the evenings, we sat outside the hut and watched the sun go down behind the peaks. Sometimes hikers stopped to buy milk or cheese, and my grandfather told them stories about the mountain: about wolves, about storms and about the year when lightning struck the hut. I had heard none of these stories before.

The most frightening moment came in August. A storm arrived in the middle of the afternoon, and two young cows ran away in panic. We searched for them in the rain for three hours. When we finally found them, standing calmly in a small valley, my grandfather laughed for the first time that summer. "Now you are a real shepherd," he said.

When my parents came to collect me at the end of the summer, they hardly recognised me. I was brown from the sun, I had lost weight and I talked about cows all the time. My friends showed me their photos from the beach, and I realised that I did not envy them at all.

Next summer, I am going back to the mountain. My grandfather says that he is getting too old for the work and that one day the hut will be mine. I think I am ready.

10. K
Sklep: psi so se tisočletja učili razumeti nas – zdaj je čas, da se mi bolj potrudimo razumeti njih.

You will listen to an interview with Leo Marsh, who keeps bees on the roofs of buildings in London. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Leo, you look after bees on top of office buildings in the middle of London. How did that happen?

Leo: Completely by chance. Ten years ago I was working as an accountant, and I was bored out of my mind. One lunchtime I went up to the roof of our office to get some fresh air, and I found a swarm of bees hanging from an air-conditioning unit. Nobody knew what to do, so I called a local beekeeper. She came, put the whole swarm into a cardboard box, and I watched her the whole time. By the end of the afternoon I had decided I wanted to learn.

Interviewer: And did you?

Leo: I did an evening course at a beekeeping association, which lasted eight weeks, and then I bought my first hive. I kept it in my parents' garden at first, because my flat didn't have a balcony. After two years, I had six hives and more honey than I could eat, and some of the companies in the area started asking whether I could put hives on their roofs.

Interviewer: Why would a company want bees on its roof?

Leo: Partly because it's good for their image – it shows they care about the environment. But many of them also want to give their staff something interesting to do. I run workshops where office workers put on a protective suit and come up to look inside the hives. Some of them are terrified at first, but by the end they don't want to leave.

Interviewer: Is London actually a good place for bees?

Leo: Surprisingly, yes. People imagine the city as concrete and traffic, but it's full of parks, gardens, trees along the streets and flowers on balconies. And because the city is warmer than the countryside, the bees can fly earlier in spring and later in autumn. Also, there are fewer pesticides than on many farms. London honey often wins prizes.

Interviewer: Does city honey taste different?

Leo: Very different – and it changes from street to street. Honey from a hive near a park full of lime trees tastes completely different from honey from a hive near railway lines, where lots of wild flowers grow. I always say that a jar of London honey is a map of the neighbourhood.

Interviewer: Are there any problems?

Leo: There's one big one: there are now too many hives in some parts of the city. Rooftop beekeeping has become so fashionable that in central London there may not be enough flowers to feed all the bees. And honeybees compete with wild bees, which are actually in much greater danger. So now I spend as much time planting flowers as I do looking after hives.

Interviewer: What would you say to someone who wants to start beekeeping?

Leo: Take a course first, and spend a season helping an experienced beekeeper before you buy anything. And if you just want to help bees, you don't need a hive at all. Plant flowers. Even a window box makes a difference.

Interviewer: Have you ever been stung?

Leo: Hundreds of times! But I think of it as part of the job. The bees are only defending their home.

A rooftop beekeeper

You will listen to a conversation with psychologist Dr Ruth Allen and primary school teacher Ben Carter about boredom. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Most of us try to avoid being bored at all costs. But my guests today believe that boredom might actually be good for us. Ruth, you've researched boredom for many years. What is it, exactly?

Ruth: Boredom is a signal. It's the brain telling us that what we're doing at the moment isn't satisfying, and that we should look for something more meaningful. In that sense, it's a bit like pain or hunger. It's unpleasant, but it pushes us to act.

Presenter: So why is it good for us?

Ruth: Because of what happens when we don't escape it immediately. In one experiment, we asked one group of people to copy numbers from a telephone directory for fifteen minutes – a very boring task. Another group started straight away with a creative task: thinking of as many uses as possible for two plastic cups. The bored group came up with far more creative ideas than the others.

Presenter: Ben, you're a teacher. Do you see this in the classroom?

Ben: Absolutely. Every Friday afternoon, I give my class of ten-year-olds what I call "empty time" – forty minutes with no screens and no instructions. At first they hated it. They kept asking, "What are we supposed to do?" But after a few weeks they started inventing games, writing stories, building things out of cardboard. One group even wrote and performed a whole play.

Presenter: Why do you think children find it so hard to be bored today?

Ben: Because they never have to be. As soon as there's a quiet moment, there's a phone or a tablet. Many children have every hour of the week organised – football, music lessons, extra maths. They've never learned to entertain themselves.

Ruth: And adults are no different. Studies show that most people check their phone the moment they have to wait for anything – a bus, a lift, a coffee. We fill every gap. The problem is that it's often in those gaps that our minds wander, and mind-wandering is when we make connections, solve problems and imagine the future.

Presenter: Is there such a thing as too much boredom, though?

Ruth: Definitely. Chronic boredom – feeling bored most of the time – is linked to depression, overeating and risky behaviour. It's very common among teenagers. But that's usually a sign that a person doesn't have enough meaningful activities in their life, not that they're occasionally bored.

Presenter: What can parents do?

Ben: Don't rush to fix it. When a child says, "I'm bored," the worst thing you can do is give them a screen. Just say, "That's fine – I'm sure you'll think of something." And leave some materials lying around: paper, pens, old boxes.

Ruth: And set an example. If children see their parents sitting in the garden doing nothing, or staring out of the train window, they learn that it's normal. I sometimes go for a walk without my phone. My family thinks I'm mad, but my best ideas come on those walks.

Presenter: Ruth, Ben, thank you.

Why boredom is good for us

Report

You are an exchange student at Seaview Language School in Brighton, UK. The school management have received several complaints about the food and service in the school canteen, so they have asked you to carry out a survey among the students and write a report that will help them decide how to improve the situation.

Write a report of 120–150 words in which you include:

  • what students like and dislike about the current menus,
  • what students think about the canteen staff and their service,
  • your recommendations for improvement.
To: School Management
From: Luka Novak
Subject: Student survey on the school canteen
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, uvodom z namenom in podatkom o anketi, odstavki s podnaslovi (jedilniki, osebje in storitve, priporočila) in sklepom; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (120–150 words), formal style
  2. what students like and dislike about the current menus
  3. what students think about the canteen staff and their service
  4. your recommendations for improvement
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: School Management / From: Luka Novak / Subject: Student survey on the school canteen
Glava in naslov; ni nagovora »Dear …«.
Introduction – The purpose of this report is to present the results of a survey of 80 students about the canteen.
Uvod z namenom in podatkom o raziskavi.
Menus
Most students like the salad bar; over half complain that hot meals are repetitive and too expensive.
Iztočnica 1: všečno in nevšečno; podatki (most, over half).
Staff and service
The staff are friendly, but queues are long and the canteen closes too early.
Iztočnica 2: mnenje o osebju in storitvah.
Recommendations
A weekly changing menu, a cheaper student meal, a second serving counter.
Iztočnica 3: predlogi (It is recommended that …).
Conclusion – These changes would improve students' satisfaction considerably.
Kratek sklep.
Preštej besede (120–150).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: School Management
From: Luka Novak
Subject: Student survey on the school canteen

Introduction

The purpose of this report is to present the results of a survey of 80 students about the school canteen.

Menus

Most students like the salad bar and the fresh fruit. However, over half complain that the hot meals are repetitive and too expensive, and vegetarians say there is little choice for them.

Staff and service

The staff are generally described as friendly and helpful. On the other hand, queues at lunchtime are very long, and many students think that the canteen closes too early.

Recommendations

It is recommended that the menu should change every week and include a cheaper student meal. A second serving counter would also shorten the queues.

Conclusion

These changes would considerably improve students' satisfaction with the canteen.

Število besed: 136 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Unhealthy food should be taxed more heavily.
  2. It is better to grow up in the countryside than in a city.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče (I believe a tax on unhealthy food would be a sensible step …).
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1: argument + primer (obesity, a sugar tax on soft drinks in some countries).
Konkretni primeri.
Jedro 2: argument + primer (money from the tax could make fruit and vegetables cheaper).
Povezovalci.
Jedro 3: protiargument (it hurts poorer families; personal freedom … However …).
Uravnoteženost.
Sklep: povzemi stališče.
Brez novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: fresh air, safety, nature, close community. Against: fewer schools and activities, long journeys, fewer opportunities for teenagers.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Unhealthy food should be taxed more heavily.

Walk into any supermarket and you will notice that a large bottle of cola often costs less than a bag of apples. No wonder obesity is a growing problem. In my opinion, taxing unhealthy food more heavily would be a sensible step, although it cannot solve the problem on its own.

Firstly, prices influence what people buy. When several countries introduced a tax on sugary drinks, many companies reduced the amount of sugar in their products, and people started buying healthier alternatives. A higher price makes customers think twice before they choose crisps or sweets.

Secondly, the money raised by such a tax could be used to make healthy food cheaper. Governments could support fruit and vegetables in school canteens or fund sports programmes for young people. In this way, the tax would not only punish bad habits but also encourage good ones.

On the other hand, critics argue that such taxes hurt poorer families most, because they spend a larger part of their income on food. Others believe that adults should be free to decide what they eat. These are fair points. However, the costs of treating diseases caused by bad diets are paid by everyone.

In conclusion, I believe that a tax on unhealthy food is justified, as long as the money is used to make healthy choices easier. Together with better education about nutrition, it could help the next generation to live longer and healthier lives.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and choose the correct answer (A, B, C or D). There is an example at the beginning (0).

The Piano Tuner

The piano had not been played for eleven years when Mr Albescu came to tune it. My grandmother had stopped playing on the day my grandfather died, and since then the piano had stood in the corner of the living room under a lace cloth, holding up photographs and a vase of dried flowers. When she announced, at the age of eighty-four, that she wanted it tuned, my mother looked at me as if this were the first sign of madness.

Mr Albescu arrived on a Tuesday afternoon carrying a small leather bag. He was a thin, elderly man with very clean hands and a coat that was too warm for the season. He took off the photographs one by one, handing them to me without looking at them, and lifted the lid as carefully as if he were opening a coffin.

For a long time he did nothing. He simply pressed one key after another and listened, his head tilted to one side. Some notes were dull, others hardly sounded at all. Once he winced, as though the piano had said something rude. "It has been lonely," he said at last, to nobody in particular.

I had expected the work to take an hour. It took the whole afternoon. My grandmother sat in her armchair by the window, pretending to read the newspaper, but I noticed that she had not turned a page. Every time Mr Albescu struck the same note again and again, adjusting it by a fraction, her hands moved slightly in her lap.

At about five o'clock, he stopped and asked her whether she would like to try it. She shook her head quickly. "I have forgotten everything," she said. Mr Albescu did not argue. He sat down himself and played a few slow chords, then a short melody that I did not recognise. My grandmother put down her newspaper.

"That was our wedding song," she said quietly. "How did you know?"

He looked embarrassed. "I did not know," he said. "It is simply what the piano wanted to play." I thought at the time that this was a strange, rather theatrical thing to say, the kind of remark that makes people tip more generously. Later I was not so sure. My mother told me that night that my grandfather had bought the piano second-hand from a music teacher in the city, a teacher whose name she could not remember. She thought it might have begun with A.

Mr Albescu refused to take any money. He packed his tools, put on his heavy coat and shook my grandmother's hand for a long moment. After he had gone, she sat down at the piano for the first time in eleven years. She played badly, with many wrong notes, and she cried a little. But she played every evening after that until she died.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.How long had the piano been silent?
    A Eleven years.B Eight years.C Eighty-four years.D One year.
    Answer: A
  2. 1.How did the narrator's mother react to the grandmother's wish?
    A She was delighted.B She thought it was a strange idea.C She offered to find a tuner.D She refused to allow it.
  3. 2.How did Mr Albescu treat the piano when he opened it?
    A Roughly and quickly.B With great care.C With obvious disgust.D Without interest.
  4. 3.What did Mr Albescu do first?
    A He started to repair the strings.B He played a melody.C He tested the sound of the keys.D He asked about the piano's history.
  5. 4.What does the narrator notice about the grandmother during the work?
    A She was reading with great interest.B She was not really reading.C She fell asleep in her chair.D She left the room several times.
  6. 5.Why did the grandmother refuse to play at first?
    A She did not like the sound.B She was angry with the tuner.C She believed she could not play any more.D She was too tired.
  7. 6.What surprised the grandmother?
    A The tuner played her wedding song.B The tuner knew her husband.C The piano sounded worse than before.D The tuner asked for a lot of money.
  8. 7.What does the narrator later begin to suspect?
    A The tuner was a dishonest man.B The tuner had a connection with the piano.C The grandmother had invited the tuner for personal reasons.D The piano had never belonged to the family.
  9. 8.What effect did the visit have on the grandmother?
    A She sold the piano.B She started playing again regularly.C She became a piano teacher.D She stopped talking about her husband.
naloge.rezultat:
1. B
2. B
3. C
4. B
5. C
6. A
7. B
8. B
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: izbrati eno od štirih možnosti (A–D).
  • Postopek: najprej preberi vprašanje brez možnosti in v besedilu poišči odgovor; šele nato preberi možnosti in izberi tisto, ki pove isto z drugimi besedami (parafraza).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilna možnost se ujema s pomenom besedila; napačne možnosti pogosto uporabijo iste besede kot besedilo, a povedo nekaj drugega, preveč posplošijo (always, never) ali so resnične, a ne odgovarjajo na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. B
Mati jo je pogledala, »as if this were the first sign of madness« – zdelo se ji je nenavadno.
2. B
Pokrov je dvignil »as carefully as if he were opening a coffin«.
3. C
»He simply pressed one key after another and listened«.
4. B
Pretvarjala se je, da bere, »she had not turned a page«; roke so se ji premikale.
5. C
»I have forgotten everything.«
6. A
»That was our wedding song … How did you know?«
7. B
Klavir je bil kupljen od učitelja glasbe, katerega ime se je morda začelo na A – mogoča povezava z g. Albescujem.
8. B
»she played every evening after that until she died«.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and match the statements with the paragraphs. More than one statement may refer to the same paragraph. There is an example at the beginning: Example 0.

Starting again

Five people describe how they changed their careers in mid-life.

A Marta, from lawyer to baker

For fifteen years I worked for a big law firm, often until midnight. I was well paid but constantly exhausted. Baking bread at the weekend was the only thing that relaxed me. When the firm was taken over and I was offered a redundancy payment, I used it to open a small bakery. I now get up at four in the morning, which my old colleagues find hilarious, but I go to bed happy. My income has halved, and I don't miss the money at all.

B Tomasz, from banker to nurse

My father was seriously ill for two years, and I spent a lot of time in hospitals. I was amazed by the nurses – their patience, their humour, their skill. At forty-two, I went back to university to train as a nurse. I was the oldest student in my year by far, and the first months of studying anatomy were a real shock to my brain. My younger classmates called me 'Grandpa', but they were always happy to borrow my notes.

C Grace, from teacher to furniture maker

I loved teaching, but after twenty years I felt I had nothing new to give. I had always enjoyed making things with my hands, so I took an evening course in woodwork. The teacher said I had a talent, and a year later I was selling tables to friends. The hardest part was the uncertainty: some months I sell nothing. I sometimes go back to school as a supply teacher when money is short, which I actually enjoy now that it is not every day.

D Raj, from engineer to wildlife guide

I designed bridges for a living and spent most of my holidays photographing animals. During a safari in Kenya, a guide told me they were looking for people with a scientific background. I laughed – and then I couldn't stop thinking about it. My family was against the idea at first; my mother still asks when I will get a 'proper job'. I now lead groups through national parks for eight months a year and spend the rest of the time writing a guidebook.

E Sophie, from accountant to actress

Everyone told me I was too old. I had acted at university but gave it up for a safe career. At thirty-eight, after a health scare, I decided that life was too short. I joined an amateur theatre group, then got a small part in a local television series. I still work two days a week as an accountant, because acting alone doesn't pay the bills. But for the first time in my life, I'm doing something I'm proud of.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Whose hobby relaxed them during a stressful career? (A)
  2. 1.Who took the decision after a personal health problem?
  3. 2.Who used money from losing a job to start a business?
  4. 3.Whose interest started during a holiday?
  5. 4.Who found studying again mentally demanding at first?
  6. 5.Who still does their old job part-time?
  7. 6.Who was inspired by the people they met during a difficult time?
  8. 7.Who finds that the irregular income is the biggest difficulty?
  9. 8.Whose relatives were not happy about the change?
  10. 9.Who now earns much less but does not mind?
  11. 10.Who now enjoys their previous job more because they do it less often?
  12. 11.Who was helpful to younger colleagues?
  13. 12.Who is working on a book?
naloge.rezultat:
1. E
2. A
3. D
4. B
5. E
6. B
7. C
8. D
9. A
10. C
11. B
12. D
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. E
»after a health scare« – zdravstvene težave so jo spodbudile.
2. A
»I was offered a redundancy payment … to open a small bakery«.
3. D
Med safarijem v Keniji mu je vodnik omenil delo.
4. B
»the first months of studying anatomy were a real shock to my brain«.
5. E
»I still work two days a week as an accountant«.
6. B
Med očetovo boleznijo ga je navdušilo osebje v bolnišnici.
7. C
»The hardest part was the uncertainty: some months I sell nothing.«
8. D
»My family was against the idea at first«.
9. A
»My income has halved, and I don't miss the money at all.«
10. C
Kot nadomestna učiteljica uživa, ker to ni vsak dan.
11. B
Mlajši sošolci so si radi izposojali njegove zapiske.
12. D
»writing a guidebook«.

Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Growing food in the middle of the city

When we think of farms, we usually imagine fields, tractors and open countryside. But in cities all over the world, a quiet revolution is taking place. On rooftops, in abandoned factories and even in old underground tunnels, people are growing fruit and vegetables just a few metres away (0) busy streets.

Urban farming is not a new idea. During the Second World War, people in Britain and the United States were encouraged to grow vegetables in their gardens and parks, (1) helped to feed the population when food was scarce. What is new is the scale and the technology (2) is being used.

Some of the most impressive projects are vertical farms. Instead of growing plants in fields, these farms grow them on shelves stacked one on top of (3), often in large warehouses. The plants are grown without soil, with their roots in water containing all the nutrients they need, and LED lights replace the sun. Because the conditions are controlled so precisely, vertical farms can produce crops all year round, regardless (4) the weather, and they use up to ninety-five per cent less water than traditional farms.

Supporters say that urban farming could help cities deal (5) several problems at once. Food grown in the city does not have to be transported (6) long distances, which reduces pollution and means that it reaches customers fresher. Green roofs also help to cool buildings in summer and absorb rainwater, (7) reduces the risk of flooding.

There are social benefits, too. Community gardens bring together neighbours who might (8) never have met, and they give children in cities the chance to see where food actually comes (9). In some poorer areas, they provide fresh vegetables to families (10) would otherwise find them too expensive.

However, urban farming also has its critics. Vertical farms use a great deal of electricity, and (11) this comes from renewable sources, their environmental benefits may be smaller than they appear. They are also expensive to build, and so far they have been most successful with salad and herbs rather than with basic foods (12) as wheat or potatoes.

Most experts agree that cities will never be able to feed (13) completely. But as the world's urban population continues to grow, every rooftop garden and vertical farm helps to make the food system a little more sustainable. And, as many urban farmers say, there is something deeply satisfying (14) eating a tomato that grew on your own roof. Perhaps, in the cities of the future, farming will no longer be something that happens far away, (15) part of everyday life – as close (16) the nearest roof.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. which
Oziralni zaimek za celoten prejšnji stavek (za vejico).
2. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za stvar (technology) v vlogi osebka.
3. another / each other
Stalna zveza »one on top of another«.
4. of
»regardless of« = ne glede na.
5. with
»deal with« = spoprijeti se s.
6. over / across
»transported over long distances« = prepeljati na dolge razdalje.
7. which
Oziralni zaimek za celoten stavek: which reduces the risk.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The appeal of the secret plot

The Moon landings were faked. A secret group controls the world's governments. Famous people who died years ago are still alive. Conspiracy theories like these have always existed, but in the age of social media they spread faster and further than ever before. Why do so many otherwise (0) (REASON) people believe them?

According to psychologists, one important factor is our need for (1) (EXPLAIN). When something frightening or confusing happens, such as a pandemic or the sudden death of a celebrity, many people find it (2) (SATISFY) to accept that it was caused by chance. A conspiracy theory offers a clear story with heroes and villains, which can feel more (3) (COMFORT) than uncertainty.

Another factor is a feeling of (4) (POWER). Research shows that people who feel that they have little control over their lives, or who distrust (5) (AUTHORITATIVE), are more likely to believe in secret plots. For them, conspiracy theories can create a sense of (6) (SUPERIOR): they believe they know the truth, while everyone else has been fooled.

Our brains also play a role. Humans are naturally good at seeing patterns, which was very useful for our ancestors, who had to recognise danger quickly. But this ability can lead us to see (7) (CONNECT) between events that are completely unrelated. Once we have accepted a theory, we tend to notice only the information that supports it and ignore any (8) (EVIDENT) against it.

Social media has made the problem much worse. Algorithms show users content that is similar to what they have already watched, so someone who clicks on one video about a conspiracy may soon find themselves surrounded by hundreds of them. Within such online communities, extreme ideas can seem completely (9) (NORMALITY).

The consequences can be serious. During health crises, conspiracy theories about vaccines can lead to (10) (DANGER) decisions, and in politics they can destroy trust in elections and institutions. In some cases, believers have even turned to (11) (VIOLENT).

So how can we fight them? Experts warn that simply laughing at believers is usually (12) (PRODUCTIVE), as it tends to make them defend their views even more strongly. A better approach is to ask questions, listen (13) (PATIENT) and help people check sources for themselves. Teaching young people to think critically about what they read online may be the most (14) (EFFECT) protection of all.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. reasonable

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Leo Marsh, who keeps bees on the roofs of buildings in London. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Leo, you look after bees on top of office buildings in the middle of London. How did that happen?

Leo: Completely by chance. Ten years ago I was working as an accountant, and I was bored out of my mind. One lunchtime I went up to the roof of our office to get some fresh air, and I found a swarm of bees hanging from an air-conditioning unit. Nobody knew what to do, so I called a local beekeeper. She came, put the whole swarm into a cardboard box, and I watched her the whole time. By the end of the afternoon I had decided I wanted to learn.

Interviewer: And did you?

Leo: I did an evening course at a beekeeping association, which lasted eight weeks, and then I bought my first hive. I kept it in my parents' garden at first, because my flat didn't have a balcony. After two years, I had six hives and more honey than I could eat, and some of the companies in the area started asking whether I could put hives on their roofs.

Interviewer: Why would a company want bees on its roof?

Leo: Partly because it's good for their image – it shows they care about the environment. But many of them also want to give their staff something interesting to do. I run workshops where office workers put on a protective suit and come up to look inside the hives. Some of them are terrified at first, but by the end they don't want to leave.

Interviewer: Is London actually a good place for bees?

Leo: Surprisingly, yes. People imagine the city as concrete and traffic, but it's full of parks, gardens, trees along the streets and flowers on balconies. And because the city is warmer than the countryside, the bees can fly earlier in spring and later in autumn. Also, there are fewer pesticides than on many farms. London honey often wins prizes.

Interviewer: Does city honey taste different?

Leo: Very different – and it changes from street to street. Honey from a hive near a park full of lime trees tastes completely different from honey from a hive near railway lines, where lots of wild flowers grow. I always say that a jar of London honey is a map of the neighbourhood.

Interviewer: Are there any problems?

Leo: There's one big one: there are now too many hives in some parts of the city. Rooftop beekeeping has become so fashionable that in central London there may not be enough flowers to feed all the bees. And honeybees compete with wild bees, which are actually in much greater danger. So now I spend as much time planting flowers as I do looking after hives.

Interviewer: What would you say to someone who wants to start beekeeping?

Leo: Take a course first, and spend a season helping an experienced beekeeper before you buy anything. And if you just want to help bees, you don't need a hive at all. Plant flowers. Even a window box makes a difference.

Interviewer: Have you ever been stung?

Leo: Hundreds of times! But I think of it as part of the job. The bees are only defending their home.

A rooftop beekeeper

  8. 7.Leo describes a jar of London honey as ____.
  9. 8.Honeybees compete with ____, which are in greater danger.
  10. 9.Leo says that even ____ makes a difference.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to a conversation with psychologist Dr Ruth Allen and primary school teacher Ben Carter about boredom. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Most of us try to avoid being bored at all costs. But my guests today believe that boredom might actually be good for us. Ruth, you've researched boredom for many years. What is it, exactly?

Ruth: Boredom is a signal. It's the brain telling us that what we're doing at the moment isn't satisfying, and that we should look for something more meaningful. In that sense, it's a bit like pain or hunger. It's unpleasant, but it pushes us to act.

Presenter: So why is it good for us?

Ruth: Because of what happens when we don't escape it immediately. In one experiment, we asked one group of people to copy numbers from a telephone directory for fifteen minutes – a very boring task. Another group started straight away with a creative task: thinking of as many uses as possible for two plastic cups. The bored group came up with far more creative ideas than the others.

Presenter: Ben, you're a teacher. Do you see this in the classroom?

Ben: Absolutely. Every Friday afternoon, I give my class of ten-year-olds what I call "empty time" – forty minutes with no screens and no instructions. At first they hated it. They kept asking, "What are we supposed to do?" But after a few weeks they started inventing games, writing stories, building things out of cardboard. One group even wrote and performed a whole play.

Presenter: Why do you think children find it so hard to be bored today?

Ben: Because they never have to be. As soon as there's a quiet moment, there's a phone or a tablet. Many children have every hour of the week organised – football, music lessons, extra maths. They've never learned to entertain themselves.

Ruth: And adults are no different. Studies show that most people check their phone the moment they have to wait for anything – a bus, a lift, a coffee. We fill every gap. The problem is that it's often in those gaps that our minds wander, and mind-wandering is when we make connections, solve problems and imagine the future.

Presenter: Is there such a thing as too much boredom, though?

Ruth: Definitely. Chronic boredom – feeling bored most of the time – is linked to depression, overeating and risky behaviour. It's very common among teenagers. But that's usually a sign that a person doesn't have enough meaningful activities in their life, not that they're occasionally bored.

Presenter: What can parents do?

Ben: Don't rush to fix it. When a child says, "I'm bored," the worst thing you can do is give them a screen. Just say, "That's fine – I'm sure you'll think of something." And leave some materials lying around: paper, pens, old boxes.

Ruth: And set an example. If children see their parents sitting in the garden doing nothing, or staring out of the train window, they learn that it's normal. I sometimes go for a walk without my phone. My family thinks I'm mad, but my best ideas come on those walks.

Presenter: Ruth, Ben, thank you.

Why boredom is good for us

naloge.besedilo:
Article

The European Reading Association, which promotes lifelong reading habits, wants to know what secondary school students in different countries think about compulsory reading lists at school. You have discussed the topic with your English class and have decided to send an article to the association's monthly magazine.

Write an article of 150–180 words with one of the following headings:
"Why compulsory reading still matters" or "Let students choose what they read".

In your article:

  • describe how reading is taught at your school,
  • present the opinions of your classmates,
  • suggest how young people could be encouraged to read more.
naloge.rezultat: Članek z izbranim naslovom, pritegnitvenim uvodom, odstavki o poučevanju branja, mnenjih sošolcev in predlogih ter z jedrnatim sklepom; 150–180 besed, polformalni slog.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Article (150–180 words), semi-formal style, with a title
  2. describe how reading is taught at your school
  3. present the opinions of your classmates
  4. suggest how young people could be encouraged to read more
Kako napišeš članek (article)
Članek (article): zgradba
  • Naslov: kratek in zanimiv; če navodilo ponuja naslove (headings), izberi enega in ga prepiši natančno.
  • Uvod: pritegni bralca (vprašanje, presenetljiv podatek, kratka zgodba) in v eni povedi povej, o čem bo članek.
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku; vsak odstavek začni s temeljno povedjo in jo podpri s primerom ali podatkom.
  • Sklep: povzemi svoje stališče ali nagovori bralce (So next time you …, why not …?). Nagovora »Dear …« in pozdrava ni.
Slog članka
  • Članek je namenjen širši javnosti (bralcem revije, šolskega časopisa, spletne strani), zato je slog polformalen: živahen, a ne pogovoren.
  • Uporabi retorična vprašanja (Have you ever wondered …?), neposreden nagovor bralca (you) in konkretne primere iz izkušenj.
  • Pri članku z mnenjem (opinion article) jasno povej svoje stališče in ga utemelji, upoštevaj tudi nasprotno mnenje.
  • Tudi v polformalnem slogu se izogibaj slengu (gonna, stuff, super cool) in pretiranim klicajem.
Uporabne zveze
  • Have you ever thought about …? · Imagine a school where … · According to a recent survey, …
  • On the one hand, … On the other hand, … · What is more, … · Not only … but also …
  • All in all, … · It is high time we … · The choice is yours.
Pogoste napake
  • Članek napisan kot pismo (Dear readers, … Yours sincerely).
  • Manjka naslov ali je naslov drugačen od ponujenega.
  • Iztočnice so le naštete, niso razvite s primeri in razlogi.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba članka
Naslov: Let students choose what they read
Prepiši izbrani naslov natančno.
Uvod: vprašanje bralcem (When did you last read a book because you wanted to, not because you had to?).
Pritegni bralca.
Odstavek 1: branje v naši šoli
Every year we read five or six set texts, mostly classics, and write tests and essays about them.
Iztočnica 1: opis.
Odstavek 2: mnenja sošolcev
Most classmates find the classics difficult and far from their lives; a few say they discovered favourite books this way.
Iztočnica 2: uravnoteženo, z deleži (most, a few).
Odstavek 3: predlogi
A mix of set and free-choice books, reading clubs, book trailers made by students.
Iztočnica 3: konkretni predlogi.
Sklep: Reading should be a pleasure, not a punishment.
Polformalni slog; višja raven: pestro besedišče.
Preštej besede (150–180).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Let students choose what they read

When did you last read a book because you wanted to, not because you had to? For many students at my school, the honest answer is: years ago.

At our school, we read five or six set texts every year, mostly classics such as Shakespeare or nineteenth-century novels. We discuss them in class and then write tests and essays about them.

When I asked my classmates for their opinion, most of them said they found the classics difficult and far removed from their own lives. Several admitted that they had only read summaries online. On the other hand, a few said that compulsory reading had introduced them to books they would never have chosen, and which they now love.

So what is the solution? I believe schools should offer a mix of set texts and free-choice books. Reading clubs, author visits and book trailers made by students could also make reading more attractive.

After all, reading should be a pleasure, not a punishment. Give students a choice, and they may surprise you.

Število besed: 178 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.
