naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Jamie Ross, who has been a street musician in Edinburgh for fifteen years. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Jamie, you've been playing on the streets of Edinburgh for fifteen years. How did it start?

Jamie: I was a student, and I needed money for my rent. I could play the guitar a bit, so one Saturday I sat down on the pavement near the castle and started singing. I was so nervous that I played with my eyes closed for the first hour. When I opened them, there was eleven pounds in my guitar case. I thought I was rich.

Interviewer: And you never stopped.

Jamie: Well, I did finish my degree – in geography, of all things. But by then I loved busking so much that I couldn't imagine working in an office. My parents weren't very happy about it. My dad still sends me job advertisements now and then.

Interviewer: What's a normal day like?

Jamie: There's no such thing as a normal day, because everything depends on the weather and the crowds. In summer, during the festival, the city is full of tourists and I can play for six or seven hours. In winter, when it's dark at four o'clock and freezing, I sometimes play for an hour and go home with almost nothing. My fingers just stop working.

Interviewer: Do you need permission to play?

Jamie: In Edinburgh you don't need a licence, but there's a code of conduct. You're supposed to move to a different spot every hour, so that the shopkeepers don't have to listen to the same songs all day. And you can't use very loud amplifiers. I think that's fair.

Interviewer: What kind of music do you play?

Jamie: Mostly my own songs, with a few famous ones mixed in. People stop for songs they know, but they buy CDs because of the songs they don't. I sell about two thousand CDs a year, which is where most of my income comes from these days, more than from the money people throw into the case.

Interviewer: Have you had any unusual experiences?

Jamie: Lots! Once, a couple asked me to play while the man proposed to his girlfriend. She said yes, and the whole street clapped. Another time, a man stopped and listened to three songs, and then he gave me his business card. He was a television producer, and one of my songs ended up in a TV series.

Interviewer: What's the hardest thing about the job?

Jamie: People sometimes treat you as if you were invisible, or as if you were begging. That hurts, because I'm working, just like they are. And there's no security – no sick pay, no holidays. If I don't play, I don't earn.

Interviewer: What advice would you give to young musicians who want to try busking?

Jamie: Practise at home first, choose a spot where people walk slowly rather than rush past, and smile. People give money to someone who looks like they're enjoying themselves. And always be polite to the shopkeepers – they're your neighbours.

A street musician

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Jamie started busking because he needed money for his rent. (T)
  2. 1.Jamie earned eleven pounds on his first day. T / F
  3. 2.Jamie studied music at university. T / F
  4. 3.Jamie's father has accepted his choice of career. T / F
  5. 4.In Edinburgh, street musicians need a licence. T / F
  6. 5.Musicians should change their location every hour. T / F
  7. 6.Most of Jamie's income now comes from selling CDs. T / F
  8. 7.One of Jamie's songs was used in a TV series. T / F
  9. 8.Jamie advises musicians to play where people walk fast. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. T
2. F
3. F
4. F
5. T
6. T
7. T
8. F
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
»there was eleven pounds in my guitar case«.
2. F
Študiral je geografijo.
3. F
»My dad still sends me job advertisements now and then.«
4. F
»In Edinburgh you don't need a licence«.
5. T
»You're supposed to move to a different spot every hour«.
6. T
»which is where most of my income comes from these days«.
7. T
»one of my songs ended up in a TV series«.
8. F
»choose a spot where people walk slowly rather than rush past«.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to a conversation with Megan Clark and Oliver Grant, two university students who spent a month on an expedition to Svalbard, in the Arctic. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Megan and Oliver, you've just come back from a month in Svalbard. What were you doing there?

Megan: We were part of a group of twelve students studying how glaciers are changing. Every day we measured the edge of a glacier and took samples of ice and water. Some glaciers in Svalbard are shrinking so fast that you can see the difference from one year to the next.

Presenter: How did you get on the expedition?

Oliver: There was a competition at our university. You had to write a research proposal and then go through a fitness test and an interview. About two hundred students applied. I still can't believe they chose me, because I'd never even been camping before.

Presenter: What was the hardest part?

Megan: For me it was the light. In summer, the sun doesn't set at all in Svalbard, so it's light twenty-four hours a day. I found it very hard to sleep. I wore a mask over my eyes, but my body just didn't believe it was night.

Oliver: For me it was the cold. Even in July, the temperature was often only a few degrees above zero, and with the wind it felt much colder. Everything took longer – writing in a notebook, using a camera, even eating – because you had to keep taking your gloves off.

Presenter: I've heard that polar bears are a real danger there.

Megan: They are. There are more polar bears than people in Svalbard. Outside the settlements, everyone has to carry a rifle or travel with someone who has one. We had two guides who were trained to use them. Fortunately, we only saw one bear, from a boat, about three hundred metres away. It was beautiful, but my heart was beating very fast.

Presenter: What did you eat?

Oliver: Mostly dried food that we mixed with hot water. It wasn't exactly delicious. Once a week a boat brought fresh supplies, and the day it arrived we all ate fruit like it was a festival. I've never been so happy to see an apple.

Presenter: Did the experience change you?

Megan: Definitely. Seeing the glaciers with my own eyes made climate change feel very real. When you read about it in the news, it's numbers. When you stand in front of a wall of ice and hear it cracking, it's different. I've decided to do a master's degree in glaciology.

Oliver: I learned that I'm tougher than I thought. And I learned to live with very little. When I came home, I looked at my wardrobe and thought, why do I need all this?

Presenter: Would you go back?

Oliver: Tomorrow. But maybe in winter next time – to see the northern lights.

A student expedition to the Arctic

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where did the expedition take place?
    In Svalbard (in the Arctic).
  2. 1.How many students were on the expedition?
  3. 2.What were the students studying?
  4. 3.What did applicants have to write?
  5. 4.What did Megan wear to help her sleep?
  6. 5.Why did everything take longer in the cold?
  7. 6.What must people carry outside the settlements?
  8. 7.How often did fresh supplies arrive?
  9. 8.What does Oliver want to see if he goes back in winter?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Twelve.
2. How glaciers are changing.
3. A research proposal.
4. A mask (over her eyes).
5. They had to keep taking their gloves off.
6. A rifle.
7. Once a week.
8. The northern lights.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Twelve.
»a group of twelve students«.
2. How glaciers are changing.
»studying how glaciers are changing«.
3. A research proposal.
»You had to write a research proposal«.
4. A mask (over her eyes).
»I wore a mask over my eyes«.
5. They had to keep taking their gloves off.
»because you had to keep taking your gloves off«.
6. A rifle.
»everyone has to carry a rifle«.
7. Once a week.
»Once a week a boat brought fresh supplies«.
8. The northern lights.

deli.A: A) PISNI SESTAVEK (V ENI OD STALNIH SPOROČANJSKIH OBLIK)

naloge.besedilo:
Report

After finishing your Matura exams, you worked for six weeks as an assistant instructor at Glenmore Outdoor Centre in Scotland, which runs adventure holidays for teenagers. At the end of the summer, the centre manager asked you to write a report of 120–150 words about your work experience.

You were in charge of:

  • climbing sessions on the indoor wall,
  • helping in the kitchen,
  • organising campfire evenings.
To: Centre Manager
From: Nika Zupan
Subject: My work experience at Glenmore Outdoor Centre
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, uvodom z namenom, odstavki s podnaslovi za vsa tri področja dela (plezanje, kuhinja, večeri ob tabornem ognju) in sklepom s priporočilom; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (120–150 words), formal style
  2. climbing sessions on the indoor wall
  3. helping in the kitchen
  4. organising campfire evenings
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Centre Manager / From: Nika Zupan / Subject: My work experience at Glenmore Outdoor Centre
Glava in naslov; ni nagovora »Dear …«.
Introduction – The aim of this report is to describe my six weeks as an assistant instructor.
Uvod z namenom.
Climbing sessions
I helped beginners with the equipment and safety rules; most of them reached the top by the end of the week.

To: Centre Manager
From: Nika Zupan
Subject: My work experience at Glenmore Outdoor Centre

Introduction

The aim of this report is to describe my six weeks as an assistant instructor at Glenmore Outdoor Centre.

Climbing sessions

I helped beginners put on their equipment and explained the safety rules. Although many teenagers were nervous at first, most of them reached the top of the wall by the end of the week.

Kitchen

I also prepared breakfasts and packed lunches. The work was enjoyable, but the kitchen was too small for so many people, which caused delays.

Campfire evenings

Campfire evenings were the most popular activity. We sang songs, told ghost stories and organised a talent show every Friday.

Conclusion

A larger kitchen would make the work more efficient. Overall, it was a valuable experience, and I would be happy to return.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Exams are not the best way to measure what students know.
  2. Tourism does more harm than good.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče (I agree that exams show only part of what students can do …).
Teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1: argument + primer (stress, a bad day, memorising instead of understanding).
Konkretni primeri.
Jedro 2: argument + primer (projects, presentations and teamwork show other skills).
Povezovalci.
Jedro 3: protiargument (exams are fair and objective, everyone has the same task … However …).
Uravnoteženost.
Sklep: povzemi stališče.
Brez novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For harm: crowds, pollution, high rents, loss of local culture. Against: jobs, money for local communities, cultural exchange.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Exams are not the best way to measure what students know.

Every June, thousands of students in Slovenia sit their Matura exams, and their future depends on a few hours. I agree that exams are not the best way to measure what students know, although they do have some advantages.

Firstly, exams show only what a student can do on one particular day. If you are ill, tired or extremely nervous, you may get a low mark even if you have studied hard. I have a friend who knows more about history than anyone in our class, yet she always panics in tests and gets poor results.

Secondly, exams often reward memorising rather than understanding. Many students learn facts by heart the night before and forget them a week later. Skills such as teamwork, creativity and presenting ideas, which are essential in real life, are rarely tested in written exams. Projects, presentations and portfolios would show these abilities much better.

On the other hand, exams have one important advantage: they are fair. Everyone answers the same questions under the same conditions, and the papers are marked anonymously. This makes it harder for teachers to favour certain students. However, fairness alone does not mean that exams measure knowledge accurately.

In conclusion, I believe that exams should not be the only way of assessing students. A combination of exams, projects and continuous assessment during the year would give a much more complete picture of what students really know and can do.

Read the text below and choose the correct answer (A, B, C or D). There is an example at the beginning (0).

The Last Letter

My grandfather was a postman for forty-one years, and in all that time, he liked to say, he lost only one letter. He told the story so often that we children could recite it with him, word for word, rolling our eyes at the familiar places. It was only after his death, when I was clearing out his house, that I discovered the story was not quite true.

The letter, according to his version, was addressed to a Miss Eleanor Vane at a farm on the edge of his round. It was the winter of 1962, the worst in living memory, and the snow lay so deep that the lane to the farm had disappeared. He tried three times to get through, he said, and three times he had to turn back. By the time the snow melted, the farm was empty. Miss Vane had moved away, nobody knew where, and the letter was sent back to the sorting office and lost.

I found the letter in a biscuit tin at the back of his wardrobe, under a pile of old payslips. The envelope was yellow and soft with age, and the stamp showed the young Queen. It was addressed, in careful blue ink, to Miss E. Vane. It had never been opened.

For a long time I simply sat on the edge of his bed with it in my lap. My first feeling was anger, I think, on behalf of a woman I had never met. He had always been so proud of his honesty. Then I began to wonder why a man who had kept so few things – no photographs of himself, no letters from my grandmother – had kept this.

I did not open it. Instead, I started to look for Eleanor Vane. It took me most of a year. The internet was less help than I had hoped; in the end it was a retired teacher in the village, who remembered everyone, who gave me the name of the town in Wales where the Vane family had gone.

Eleanor was ninety-one and living in a care home overlooking the sea. She was small and sharp-eyed and very polite, and she listened to my explanation without interrupting. When I gave her the letter, she turned it over twice and then put it down on the table beside her, unopened.

"I know who it's from," she said. "I waited for it all that winter." She looked out of the window for a while. "He told me he'd written. I thought he was lying, and I married someone else."

I asked her, carefully, whether she knew my grandfather. She smiled for the first time. "Of course I did," she said. "He brought the post. He stood at our gate every morning, talking about the weather. Every morning for a year." She paused. "He was very shy. And I am afraid I was rather beautiful."

I have thought about that afternoon many times since. I never found out who had written the letter. But I no longer believe that my grandfather lost it.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  3. 2.According to the grandfather, why could he not deliver the letter?
    A The address was wrong.B The weather made the farm unreachable.C Miss Vane refused to accept it.D He was ill that winter.
  4. 3.What did the narrator find in the biscuit tin?
    A A letter that had been opened.B A letter that had never been opened.C A photograph of Miss Vane.D Letters from the grandmother.
  5. 4.What was the narrator's first reaction?
    A Amusement.B Anger.C Fear.D Relief.
  6. 5.What made the narrator wonder about the letter?
    A It was written in blue ink.B The grandfather had kept very few personal things.C The stamp was very valuable.D It was addressed to the grandmother.
  7. 6.Who helped the narrator find Eleanor?
    A A search on the internet.B A former teacher.C A relative in Wales.D The staff of the care home.
  8. 7.Why did Eleanor marry someone else?
    A She thought the letter had never been written.B She did not love the writer.C Her family forced her.D She moved to Wales.
  9. 8.What does the narrator suggest at the end?
    A The grandfather lost the letter by accident.B The grandfather kept the letter on purpose.C Eleanor had written the letter herself.D The story was completely invented.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take

  • Postopek: najprej preberi vprašanje brez možnosti in v besedilu poišči odgovor; šele nato preberi možnosti in izberi tisto, ki pove isto z drugimi besedami (parafraza).

Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (G).

Working from paradise?

More and more people are swapping the office for a laptop and a plane ticket. But is the life of a digital nomad as perfect as it looks?

Scroll through social media and you will find thousands of photos of young people working on laptops by the pool, on the beach or in a café overlooking a jungle. They call themselves digital nomads. [0] Thanks to fast internet and online tools, they can do their jobs from almost anywhere in the world.

The idea is not entirely new. [1] What has changed is the number of people who can do it. Today, web designers, programmers, translators, writers and marketing specialists can all work for clients thousands of kilometres away.

Many nomads are attracted by the lower cost of living. [2] With the same income, they can rent a flat with a view of the sea, eat out every day and still save money.

For others, the main attraction is freedom. [3] They can decide when to work and when to explore, and they can move on whenever they feel like it.

Some cities have become particularly popular. [4] In these places, you can find co-working spaces full of foreigners, meet-ups every evening and cafés with reliable wifi and plenty of power sockets.

However, the reality is often less glamorous than the photos suggest. [5] Bright sunshine makes it almost impossible to see a laptop screen, sand gets into the keyboard, and the internet connection on a beach is usually terrible.

Loneliness is another common problem. [6] Friendships tend to be short, because everyone is always about to leave for the next destination, and many nomads say they miss having a community.

There are practical difficulties, too. [7] Visas, taxes, health insurance and bank accounts can become extremely complicated when you have no fixed address, and many nomads are technically working illegally on tourist visas.

Local people do not always welcome them either. [8] In some popular destinations, rents have risen so much that local families can no longer afford to live in the centre.

Despite these problems, the number of digital nomads keeps growing. [9] Several countries, including Estonia and Barbados, have introduced special visas that allow remote workers to stay for a year or more.

For many, the nomadic life is not a permanent choice but a phase. [10] After a few years of moving from place to place, most nomads eventually settle down – often, ironically, in a place they first visited with their laptop.

Perhaps the real lesson of the digital nomads is not that everyone should live like them, but that work no longer has to happen in a particular place. [11] That change may affect all of us, whether we ever leave home or not.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AWriters and artists have travelled while working for centuries.
  2. BIn parts of Asia or South America, a salary from Europe or the USA goes much further.
  3. CInstead of sitting in an office from nine to five, they plan their days themselves.
  4. DChiang Mai in Thailand, Lisbon and Bali are among the favourites.
  5. EWorking on a beach, for example, is far less comfortable than it looks.
  6. FIt can be hard to build lasting relationships when you change country every few months.
  7. GThese are people who use technology to work remotely while travelling.
  8. HBeing a nomad can also cause problems with official paperwork.
  9. ISome feel that nomads push up prices without contributing to the community.
  10. JGovernments have started to notice the trend, and some are even competing to attract them.
  11. KMany say they travel while they are young and then return to a more stable life.
  12. LSince the rise of remote working, more and more employers accept this idea.
  13. MMost digital nomads earn far more than people who work in offices.
  14. NAs a result, the number of digital nomads has fallen in recent years.

2. B
3. C
4. D
5. E
6. F
7. H
8. I
9. J
10. K

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

»The idea is not entirely new.« – A to podpre (pisatelji so potovali stoletja); sledi »What has changed is the number of people …«.

»lower cost of living« – B razloži (plača iz Evrope je v Aziji vredna več); »With the same income« se nanaša nanjo.
3. C
»freedom« – C: sami načrtujejo dan; sledi »They can decide when to work …«.
4. D
»Some cities have become particularly popular.« – D našteje mesta; »In these places« se nanaša nanje.
5. E
»the reality is often less glamorous« – E poda primer (plaža); sledijo podrobnosti (sonce, pesek, internet).
6. F
»Loneliness is another common problem.« – F: težko je graditi trajne odnose; sledi razlaga o kratkih prijateljstvih.
7. H
»practical difficulties« – H: uradni papirji; sledi naštevanje (vize, davki, zavarovanje).
8. I
»Local people do not always welcome them« – I: dvigajo cene; sledi primer z najemninami.
9. J
»the number … keeps growing« – J: vlade tekmujejo za nomade; sledi primer posebnih vizumov.
10. K
»not a permanent choice but a phase« – K: potujejo, dokler so mladi; sledi »After a few years … settle down«.
11. L
Po sklepni misli, da delo ni več vezano na kraj: L – vedno več delodajalcev to sprejema; »That change« se nanaša na to.

The power of believing

Imagine taking a pill that contains nothing but sugar and feeling your headache disappear. This is not magic but a well-known phenomenon called the placebo effect, and it shows just how powerful the connection between the mind and the body (0) be.

The word "placebo" comes from Latin and means "I shall please". For centuries, doctors gave patients harmless substances simply to make them feel better, often (1) telling them the truth. It was not until the twentieth century, however, that scientists began to study the effect seriously.

During the Second World War, an American doctor called Henry Beecher ran out (2) morphine while treating wounded soldiers. In desperation, a nurse injected one soldier with salt water but told him it was a strong painkiller. To Beecher's amazement, the soldier's pain was reduced, and he did not go into shock. After the war, Beecher began to investigate (3) this could happen.

Today, the placebo effect is so well documented that every new drug must be tested against it. In such tests, one group of patients receives the real drug, while (4) group receives a fake pill that looks exactly the same. Neither the patients (5) the doctors know who is getting which. Only if the real drug works significantly better than the placebo can it be approved.

The results of these studies are often surprising. Placebos seem to work best for conditions (6) as pain, nausea, depression and sleep problems, where the brain plays an important role. In some studies, as many as a third of patients taking a placebo reported a clear improvement. Brain scans have shown that placebos can trigger the release of the body's own painkillers, so the relief people feel is not imaginary (7) real.

Even the details matter. Two placebo pills tend to work better than one, injections work better than pills, and expensive placebos work better than cheap (8). The colour of a pill can also make a difference: in some studies, blue pills helped people feel calm, (9) red ones made them feel more alert.

Perhaps most surprising of all is that placebos may work even when people know they are taking one. In an experiment in the United States, patients (10) suffered from a painful bowel condition were given pills clearly labelled "placebo". Many of them still reported feeling better.

The placebo effect also has a dark side, known as the "nocebo" effect. When people expect a treatment to harm them, they may actually experience side effects, (11) the treatment itself is harmless. Patients who read a long list of possible side effects are more likely to suffer from them.

Doctors are now trying to find ethical ways of using the placebo effect. Spending more time with patients, showing understanding and explaining treatments in a positive way all seem to improve results. In the end, the placebo effect reminds us that healing is not only about chemistry. What we believe, and how we (12) treated, can make a real difference (13) how we feel. It may even be one of the most underrated medicines (14) all. And, best of all, it is completely free (15) charge.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. can

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. without
»without telling them the truth« = ne da bi jim povedali resnico.
2. of
»run out of« = zmanjkati.
3. how / why
Odvisni vprašalni stavek: how this could happen.
4. another / the other
Druga skupina: the other group / another group.
5. nor
Zveza »neither … nor« = ne … ne.
6. such
»such as« = kot na primer.
7. but
»not imaginary but real« = ne namišljeno, ampak resnično.
8. ones
Nadomestna beseda za množino (placebos).
9. while / whereas
Nasprotje: while red ones made them feel more alert.
10. who / that
Oziralni zaimek za osebe (patients).
11. even if / even though / although
Dopustni veznik: tudi če je zdravljenje neškodljivo (ena beseda: although).
12. are
Trpnik v sedanjiku: how we are treated.
13. to
»make a difference to« = vplivati na.
14. of
»of all« = od vseh.
15. of
Stalna zveza »free of charge« = brezplačno.

Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Twelve seconds that changed the world

On the morning of 17 December 1903, on a windy beach near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, a strange machine made of wood, wire and cloth (0) (RISE) into the air. It stayed up for just twelve seconds and (1) (COVER) about thirty-seven metres – less than the length of a modern passenger plane. But it was the first powered, controlled flight in history.

The two men behind it, Orville and Wilbur Wright, were not scientists or engineers. They (2) (RUN) a bicycle shop in Dayton, Ohio, and they (3) (NEVER / FINISH) high school. Since childhood, however, they (4) (FASCINATE) by flight. Their interest began when their father brought home a toy helicopter made of paper, bamboo and a rubber band.

Before the brothers started their experiments, several people (5) (TRY) to build flying machines, and some had died in the attempt. The Wrights realised that the main problem was not power but control. Watching birds, they noticed that they (6) (TWIST) the ends of their wings to turn and balance. The brothers used the same idea on their gliders, which they tested for three years on the sand dunes of Kitty Hawk.

By 1903, they were ready to add an engine. Because no company could supply one that was light enough, they (7) (BUILD) their own with the help of their mechanic. They also designed their own propellers.

On 14 December, the brothers tossed a coin to decide who (8) (FLY) first. Wilbur won, but the plane stalled and crashed after just three seconds. Three days later, it was Orville's turn. With only five witnesses watching, the machine (9) (LIFT) off the ground. The brothers made four flights that day; the longest, by Wilbur, lasted fifty-nine seconds.

Surprisingly, the world (10) (HARDLY / NOTICE). Most newspapers did not believe the story, and for several years the brothers (11) (WORK) quietly on improving their planes. It was only in 1908, when they gave public demonstrations in France and the United States, that people finally realised what they (12) (ACHIEVE).

Today, more than four billion passengers travel by plane every year. If the Wright brothers (13) (NOT / CONTINUE) after their first failures, someone else would probably have flown sooner or later. But it was two bicycle makers from Ohio who (14) (GIVE) humans their wings.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

2. ran
Nepravilni glagol run – ran – run.

»Since childhood« pred 1903: past perfect passive (be fascinated by).

»Before the brothers started« – predpreteklik.

Stalno dejstvo o pticah v poročanem govoru: twisted ali twist.
7. built
Nepravilni glagol build – built – built.
8. would fly / should fly
Prihodnost v preteklosti: who would fly first.
9. lifted
Zaključeno dejanje: past simple.
10. hardly noticed
Prislov »hardly« pred glagolom: past simple.
11. worked / were working / continued working
Daljše dogajanje v preteklosti.
12. had achieved
Dosežek pred spoznanjem: past perfect.
13. had not continued
Tretji pogojnik: If … had not continued, someone else would have flown.
14. gave
Izpostavljeni stavek v preteklosti: it was … who gave.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Jamie Ross, who has been a street musician in Edinburgh for fifteen years. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Jamie, you've been playing on the streets of Edinburgh for fifteen years. How did it start?

Jamie: I was a student, and I needed money for my rent. I could play the guitar a bit, so one Saturday I sat down on the pavement near the castle and started singing. I was so nervous that I played with my eyes closed for the first hour. When I opened them, there was eleven pounds in my guitar case. I thought I was rich.

Interviewer: And you never stopped.

Jamie: Well, I did finish my degree – in geography, of all things. But by then I loved busking so much that I couldn't imagine working in an office. My parents weren't very happy about it. My dad still sends me job advertisements now and then.

Interviewer: What's a normal day like?

Jamie: There's no such thing as a normal day, because everything depends on the weather and the crowds. In summer, during the festival, the city is full of tourists and I can play for six or seven hours. In winter, when it's dark at four o'clock and freezing, I sometimes play for an hour and go home with almost nothing. My fingers just stop working.

Interviewer: Do you need permission to play?

Jamie: In Edinburgh you don't need a licence, but there's a code of conduct. You're supposed to move to a different spot every hour, so that the shopkeepers don't have to listen to the same songs all day. And you can't use very loud amplifiers. I think that's fair.

Interviewer: What kind of music do you play?

Jamie: Mostly my own songs, with a few famous ones mixed in. People stop for songs they know, but they buy CDs because of the songs they don't. I sell about two thousand CDs a year, which is where most of my income comes from these days, more than from the money people throw into the case.

Interviewer: Have you had any unusual experiences?

Jamie: Lots! Once, a couple asked me to play while the man proposed to his girlfriend. She said yes, and the whole street clapped. Another time, a man stopped and listened to three songs, and then he gave me his business card. He was a television producer, and one of my songs ended up in a TV series.

Interviewer: What's the hardest thing about the job?

Jamie: People sometimes treat you as if you were invisible, or as if you were begging. That hurts, because I'm working, just like they are. And there's no security – no sick pay, no holidays. If I don't play, I don't earn.

Interviewer: What advice would you give to young musicians who want to try busking?

Jamie: Practise at home first, choose a spot where people walk slowly rather than rush past, and smile. People give money to someone who looks like they're enjoying themselves. And always be polite to the shopkeepers – they're your neighbours.

A street musician

    fifteen years

  3. 2.During his first hour, Jamie played with ____.
  4. 3.In summer, during the festival, Jamie can play for ____.
  5. 4.In winter, Jamie sometimes stops because ____.
  6. 5.Street musicians in Edinburgh cannot use ____.
  7. 6.Jamie sells about ____ a year.
  8. 7.Once, a man proposed to his girlfriend while ____.
  9. 8.A man who listened to three songs worked as ____.
  10. 9.Jamie says that people give money to musicians who look like ____.

2. his eyes closed
3. six or seven hours
4. his fingers stop working
5. very loud amplifiers

8. a television producer

  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami.
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem predvidi, kaj manjka (število, kraj, samostalnik). Med poslušanjem zapiši ključno besedo, pri drugem poslušanju preveri.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del posnetka. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to a conversation with Megan Clark and Oliver Grant, two university students who spent a month on an expedition to Svalbard, in the Arctic. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Megan and Oliver, you've just come back from a month in Svalbard. What were you doing there?

Megan: We were part of a group of twelve students studying how glaciers are changing. Every day we measured the edge of a glacier and took samples of ice and water. Some glaciers in Svalbard are shrinking so fast that you can see the difference from one year to the next.

Presenter: How did you get on the expedition?

Oliver: There was a competition at our university. You had to write a research proposal and then go through a fitness test and an interview. About two hundred students applied. I still can't believe they chose me, because I'd never even been camping before.

Presenter: What was the hardest part?

Megan: For me it was the light. In summer, the sun doesn't set at all in Svalbard, so it's light twenty-four hours a day. I found it very hard to sleep. I wore a mask over my eyes, but my body just didn't believe it was night.

Oliver: For me it was the cold. Even in July, the temperature was often only a few degrees above zero, and with the wind it felt much colder. Everything took longer – writing in a notebook, using a camera, even eating – because you had to keep taking your gloves off.

Presenter: I've heard that polar bears are a real danger there.

Megan: They are. There are more polar bears than people in Svalbard. Outside the settlements, everyone has to carry a rifle or travel with someone who has one. We had two guides who were trained to use them. Fortunately, we only saw one bear, from a boat, about three hundred metres away. It was beautiful, but my heart was beating very fast.

Presenter: What did you eat?

Oliver: Mostly dried food that we mixed with hot water. It wasn't exactly delicious. Once a week a boat brought fresh supplies, and the day it arrived we all ate fruit like it was a festival. I've never been so happy to see an apple.

Presenter: Did the experience change you?

Megan: Definitely. Seeing the glaciers with my own eyes made climate change feel very real. When you read about it in the news, it's numbers. When you stand in front of a wall of ice and hear it cracking, it's different. I've decided to do a master's degree in glaciology.

Oliver: I learned that I'm tougher than I thought. And I learned to live with very little. When I came home, I looked at my wardrobe and thought, why do I need all this?

Presenter: Would you go back?

Oliver: Tomorrow. But maybe in winter next time – to see the northern lights.

A student expedition to the Arctic

    A month.

  6. 5.How far away was the polar bear?
  7. 6.What did they mostly eat?
  8. 7.What has Megan decided to do?
  9. 8.What did Oliver learn about himself?

naloge.besedilo:
Report

After reading about the shortage of teachers in remote areas, you joined an international volunteering organisation, Teach Together, and spent four weeks as a teaching assistant at a primary school in a mountain village in Nepal. The organisation has asked you to submit a final report of 150–180 words in which you:

  • describe the two most serious difficulties you faced as a volunteer,
  • state which skills future volunteers will need most and why,
  • explain how the organisation could help the school most effectively.
To: Teach Together
From: Ana Kovač
Subject: Final report – volunteering in Nepal
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, uvodom z namenom, odstavki s podnaslovi (dve težavi, potrebne spretnosti z utemeljitvijo, priporočila za organizacijo) in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (150–180 words), formal style
  2. describe the two most serious difficulties you faced as a volunteer
  3. state which skills future volunteers will need most and why
  4. explain how the organisation could help the school most effectively
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Teach Together / From: Ana Kovač / Subject: Final report – volunteering in Nepal
Glava in naslov.
Introduction – The purpose of this report is to evaluate my four-week assignment.
Uvod z namenom.
Difficulties
Language barrier with younger pupils; very few books and no electricity in the afternoons.
Iztočnica 1: natanko dve težavi z razlago.
Skills needed
Flexibility, basic Nepali phrases, the ability to teach with simple materials.
Iztočnica 2: spretnosti + zakaj.
Recommendations
Solar panels, children's books in English and Nepali, longer volunteer placements.
Iztočnica 3: najučinkovitejša pomoč.
Conclusion – Despite the challenges, the assignment was extremely rewarding.
Kratek sklep.
Višja raven: formalni slog, pasivne oblike, natančno besedišče. Preštej besede (150–180).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Teach Together
From: Ana Kovač
Subject: Final report – volunteering in Nepal

Introduction

The purpose of this report is to evaluate my four-week assignment as a teaching assistant at a primary school in a mountain village in Nepal.

Difficulties

Two difficulties proved particularly serious. Firstly, the younger pupils spoke hardly any English, so communication was often only possible with gestures and pictures. Secondly, the school had very few books, and there was no electricity in the afternoons, which made lessons difficult to plan.

Skills needed

Future volunteers will above all need flexibility and creativity, as they will have to teach with very simple materials. Learning some basic Nepali phrases before arrival is also strongly recommended, since it helps to win the children's trust.

Recommendations

The organisation could help most effectively by funding solar panels for the classrooms and providing children's books in both English and Nepali. Longer placements of at least three months would also give pupils more continuity.

Conclusion

Despite the challenges, the assignment was extremely rewarding.

Število besed: 168 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.

Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The role of Lord Goring in An Ideal Husband

At first sight, Lord Goring seems the least serious character in Oscar Wilde's An Ideal Husband. He is a fashionable dandy who claims to care only about clothes, parties and witty conversation. However, he turns out to be the true moral centre of the play and the person who saves the Chilterns' marriage.

Wilde introduces Goring as an idle young man who changes his buttonhole every day and loves to talk in paradoxes. His conversations with his father, Lord Caversham, who keeps telling him to get married and do something useful, are among the funniest scenes in the play. Goring pretends to agree with nobody and to take nothing seriously.

Yet when Sir Robert Chiltern confesses that his fortune is based on a cabinet secret he sold as a young man, Goring is the friend he turns to. Goring does not condemn him. Instead, he advises Robert to fight Mrs Cheveley and to tell his wife the truth. He also tries to persuade Gertrude Chiltern that she should not demand perfection from her husband, because everyone makes mistakes.

Goring's cleverness becomes clear in the third act. He recognises the diamond brooch that Mrs Cheveley stole years ago and fastens it on her wrist as a bracelet she cannot open. Threatened with the police, she has to give up Robert's letter. Although she takes revenge by stealing Gertrude's letter to Goring, the misunderstanding is finally cleared up.

In conclusion, Lord Goring shows that wisdom and kindness can hide behind a mask of frivolity. Through him, Wilde suggests that a man who accepts human weakness is far more admirable than one who pretends to be ideal. Fittingly, the play ends with his engagement to Mabel.

Število besed: 292 (zahtevanih 250–300). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.
